title: The Aviator Collective Flight Club
name: The Aviator Collective Flight Club
description:
The Aviator Collective is a purpose-built flight club designed for pilots who value professionalism, community, and continuous growth. Located just south of Houston, we offer access to well-maintained, IFR-capable aircraft equipped with modern avionics, supported by maintenance standards that exceed FAA minimums.

Our mission is simple: to develop better, safer, more capable aviators. We are not a time-building operation—we are a true community of pilots committed to proficiency, accountability, and meaningful flying. Members are encouraged to pursue scenario-based missions, cross-country flying, and ongoing skill development, supported by a culture that prioritizes safety and discipline both in and out of the cockpit.

The Aviator Collective operates with a structured, respectful scheduling environment and limited membership, which ensures fair access while protecting aircraft availability. Our fleet philosophy is intentional, and provides for a wide range of aircraft and capabilities so members can expand their experience across different aircraft profiles.

We are building a network of aviation-minded individuals who support one another, share knowledge, and take pride in operating at a higher standard. From student pilots to experienced aviators, every member contributes to a culture rooted in professionalism, humility, and mutual respect.

If you’re looking for more than just access to an airplane, you’re looking for a place to grow as a pilot, and to be part of something meaningful—The Aviator Collective is built for you.

title: Yellow Bird Flying Club
name: Yellow Bird Flying Club
description:
If the hassle and limitations of renting aren't working, and the cost of full ownership is not practical for you, the Yellow Bird flying club may be just the ticket. Located at the well equipped, relaxed and friendly KDUH (Toledo Suburban Airport), we are about 1/4 mile North of the Ohio line in Michigan. A non-profit club, we provide both an opportunity to enjoy flying and the comradery of other pilots  Our aircraft is a very nice, low time, 1967 piper Cherokee (PA28-140 with 160 upgrade). It's quite attractive with nearly perfect paint, a refreshed interior, and a "low-mid" time engine. The aircraft is IFR capable with (NEW!!) Garmin GPS175 and Aspen E5 showing flight information in modern glass format. These are backed up by traditional boiler gage instruments with Stratus ADS-B and twin NAV/Com radios with CDI.  Thus, the format is comfortable to both new and "seasoned" pilots alike.  

Applicants must have a clean history and typically at least private pilot certification. Members all have an equal fractional ownership of the aircraft and club assets, so there is a resalable buy-in fee. The fixed operating costs are equally distributed and paid via dues (currently $90/month), and flight time is currently only $100/hr (wet!). Fees are set annually by vote as required to cover costs. The aircraft is well maintained by the onsite FBO, although light duties (cleaning, hanger upkeep, etc.) is done by members.  The aircraft has generally been flying only about 120 hours per year combined, so you can expect the airplane to usually be available to fly, even on short notice. There are no daily minimums and extended usage is typically allowed for occasional out of town trips-- so it’s almost as if it is your own airplane, but at far lower shared cost!  Membership is full at 8, but openings occur occasionally and we can put you on a short list to hold a spot at no cost. Give us a call -- we promise not to bite and airplane talk is always welcome. Phone or text is best.

name: Hill Country Flyers-Club in Formation
description:
This newly forming club (12-01-25) has a trainer, an Aero Commander 100 Darter, at its disposal. The Darter is comparable to the venerable 172 with 150hp, but it holds a little more fuel and can carry more weight. Unfortunately, it is just as slow. Though the planes type certificate does allow it to be certified IFR, it currently is not. There is 1500 hours left on the engine before TBO. A non-WAAS 430 and a glide slope is in the panel currently which is okay for IFR training.

For the hourly rate, I included a 100 hour inspection at $1,100, three oil changes at 50 hours at $150 each per year, oil consumption at $1.20 per hour, $25/hour engine overhaul reserve, $10/hour prop overhaul reserve and $10/hour general maintenance.  So total hourly rate rounds up to $57/hour. My goal is to be, including insurance, at least $50 an hour less expensive than local renting.

The goal is to have enough members to add a traveler and possibly a tailwheel plane. of TBD types. The great news is that the club already has a fantastic hangar situation. Restrooms, club house, power, gate access, the works! 

I currently anticipate forming a not-for-profit business entity. Please call David with interest and/or questions. 830-377-2752

title: 3 Rivers Taildraggers Flying Club
name: 3 Rivers Taildraggers Flying Club
description:
There’s just something about vintage, conventional geared airplanes! Maybe it’s the challenge of landing, or the nostalgia of the early decades of aviation. Certainly, some of the allure is the raw simplicity of the planes themselves. Cutting edge avionics? Not a chance. Gas-guzzling engines? Hardly. Just a stick, two pedals, and a few basic instruments. Aviation for no reason other than experiencing the pure joy of flying low and slow. Stick your elbow out the window and watch the world go by below.

Early in 2019, a group of local pilots started talking about the need for a tailwheel plane in Ft. Wayne. In a city this size, there was only one option available to rent, a late model Super Decathlon. It’s a fantastic airplane, but not very easy on the wallet. 

After extensive discussions, we formed 3 Rivers Taildraggers Flying Club. There are five charter members, and for the time being we are not accepting additional members. We want to get comfortable with our club before we consider expanding. 

In September 2019, we welcomed our first plane into the club, a 1959 Champion 7EC. Because we live near Class C airspace, we wanted a plane with full electric, including radios and transponder. N63394 has been upgraded to a Lycoming 0-235 engine, so takeoff rolls are short, and it cruises very comfortably at 90 mph while using about 5-6 gallons of gas/hour.

We currently have a Challenger 2 Experimental with a 503 Rotax. This is the only plane in our club at this time.

title: Saratoga Flyers, Inc.
name: Saratoga Flyers, Inc.
description:
Experience flying at its most affordable! 

Membership is open to certificated pilots interested in non-commercial flying for fun and sharing their flying experiences. There is no minimum flight experience required.

Saratoga Flyers, Inc. is a New York state not-for-profit corporation with a 501(c)(7) tax exempt status. The Club is managed by a five-member board with participation from all members. We meet monthly, and plan periodic breakfast meetings, an annual dinner meeting, as well as a summer group outing. 

Our website (www.SaratogaFlyers.org) has most of the basic information about membership.  Membership is open to certificated pilots (recreational or higher). The Club is limited (& fixed) to 15 members.  

The Club plane is a 1976 Cessna 172M, which is hangared at Saratoga County airport (5B2). It is equipped with a Garmin 430W GPS & Nav/Com, Garmin GTX-345 Transponder with ADS-B In + Out, 406 MHz ELT, dual VOR receivers, standby vacuum system, ILS marker beacons/glide slope, and 4 position intercom.

The engine & prop were overhauled in August 2009, and the interior was redone in November 2010.  We change the oil every 50 hrs or so and have an oil analysis done each time to keep tabs on the health of the engine.

Dues are $70/month and flight time is $45/hr plus a fuel surcharge based on the current hourly cost for fuel. (We typically experience 7+/- gph.) To encourage members to fly regularly each member is assessed one hour of (dry) flying time each month in addition to dues.  (Those hours, however, can be banked up to a total of six hours of flight time.) 
 
We use an on-line calendar to book the plane, and even with 15 members, our schedules are varied enough that there is plenty of opportunity to fly.

If you are interested in joining us, or want more information, please let us know by using the form on the “more info” page at: www.saratogaflyers.org/more-info

title: RPM Flying Club
name: RPM Flying Club
description:
The RPM Flying Club was formed in 1972 as a Not-For-Profit Corporation.  It consists of a group of student, private, commercial, and ATP  pilots who share the cost of aircraft ownership.  We currently have two aircraft. 

A 1981 Cessna 172 fully IFR equipped with the following Garmin equipment:  G-430W,  a GTX 345 transponder-ADS-B in and out transponder, G5 HSI/attitude indicator. It also has an engine monitoring system. 

A 1972 Piper Cherokee 140 with an upgraded 160 H.P. engine. It has a Garmin G5 HSI/attitude indicator and also an engine monitoring system.

Currently we charge an initial $500.00 to join and the applicant must pass a flight review with one of our Flight Instructors (CFI). The current monthly dues  are $110.00, plus $85.00 per hour for the C172 and $75.00 per hour for the PA28-140.  These rates are “DRY” Hobbs Hours without fuel. Fuel is additional and is at the expense of the pilot.  Fuel can be purchased at Lansing Airport  by either self-serve or full service from the FBO. We have a mechanic on the field who maintains our planes in good operating condition. When something needs attending to, our mechanic is very prompt at servicing our Club. 

If interested,  please contact the Club to inquire about membership.  The RPM Flying Club is dedicated to providing safe aircraft at very reasonable rates.  We are looking for pilots to share our passion for safe and fun flying.  We invite you to check us out!

For further information regarding potential membership, contact the Club President or Membership Chairman at the email addresses listed in the contacts above.

description:
ADK Flying Club, Inc. is a member-owned, non-profit flying club operating out of the Saratoga County NY Airport (5B2).
We are 50 pilot members committed to safe, affordable flying in the beautiful Capital District/Adirondack region of upstate NY.
Our current fleet consists of 5 aircraft from a  Cherokee 140, Warrior 160, Cessna 172, Cherokee 180, and a newer, all-glass  Cessna 182.
All aircraft are IFR capable and are meticulously maintained on-field by a licensed  FAA A&P mechanic.

Our members range from professional airline,  cargo, and fractional jet ATP pilots to high school students and everything in-between--all sharing a passion for flying.
Several members are also CFI's and can offer basic and advanced instruction on a private basis ( we are a Club and not a Flight School) 

Saratoga Airport is a small uncontrolled airport which offers big field amenities. In addition to the iconic town of Saratoga, the scenic beauty of the Adirondack region and lakes as well as a multitude of small paved and grass strips to explore,  our on-field amenities include Jet-A and 100LL,  a new terminal nearing completion, an active Glider Club, a fixed wing and helicopter flight schools, tail dragger and TAA endorsement training and much more!

We welcome new members. Contact us for fun and affordable flying!!

description:
The non-profit Bell Flying Club (BFC) is one of the oldest flying clubs in Central PA. It was incorporated in the early 1960's. Headquartered at the AvFlight FBO at Harrisburg International Airport (KMDT), BFC has one aircraft and 19 members.  

N80788 is a 1976 Cessna Skyhawk 172M with a 180hp engine. It is fully IFR equipped with a Garmin 430 GPS and an additional nav/comm radio, ADF, ILS glide slope, marker beacon, encoding altimeter, and 2-axis autopilot.  With full fuel (38gals), the plane has an 820lb carrying capacity. The cruise propeller allows for an average of 3 hours flying time with FAA flight reserves.  The IO 360 4-cylinder motor is replaced every 2,000 hours and the aircraft is flown year round. 

Actual use of the airplane has averaged 200 hours per year over the last few years.  As a result, we experience few scheduling conflicts. Reservations are managed through the use of ScheduleMaster, a web-based aircraft scheduling service.

Moriarty is located in the heart of the Estancia Valley, 35 miles east of Albuquerque. The club has approximately 80 active members, has two Piper Pawnee tow planes, four club gliders including a Schweizer 2-33A, a Grob 103, a Schweizer 1-26E, and a Libelle 201. Club members also own approximately 40 private ships ranging from 1-26s to a Duo-Discus.

Moriarty boasts some of the finest year round soaring conditions in the United States, including 15 knot thermals to 22,000 ft, mountain wave to 34,000 ft, and orographic lift off the Manzano, Sandia, Ortiz, and Sangre de Cristo mountain ranges. Many flights in excess of 300 miles are recorded each year.

title: Lima Whiskey Flying Club
name: Lima Whiskey Flying Club
description:
Lima Whiskey was started in the fall of 2016 by three friends who shared a common interest in flying and desired to have a fast, economical, and safe four place IFR equipped aircraft. 

After many months of searching, in January of 2017, we found N772DF a 1980 Mooney M20J with a low time engine, a Garmin 530AW GPS, and a KFC200 two axis autopilot.

Rather than forming a simple three-way partnership, instead we created the Lima Whiskey Flying Club - 501(c)(7) non profit social club - so that others might have the opportunity to join us in our love of flying.

The way that it works is simple.

The Lima Whiskey Flying Club corporation owns the aircraft and members initially purchase a share of the club which gives he/she the right to fly the Club’s aircraft. In addition to the initial share purchase, members pay monthly dues which cover hanger rental, insurance, maintenance costs, etc. And of course, members pay an hourly fee (based on the tachometer time) to fly the aircraft. The hourly rate covers fuel, oil, and funds which are set aside for annuals and ultimately future engine and propeller TBOs.

We are based in the North Hangers at Captial City Airport (KCTX) in New Cumberland, Pennsylvania, just on the other side of the Susquehanna River from Harrisburg.

We have added the following updates to the M20J.

ADSB In and Out
Garmin Flight Stream
New Audio Panel with Blue Tooth
Engine Pre-Heater
JPI Engine Monitor

title: Central Mississippi Light Flyers, Inc.
name: Central Mississippi Light Flyers, Inc.
description:
Central Mississippi Light Flyers (CMLF) is a nonprofit organization incorporated in the state of Mississippi. As a Flying Club, our mission is to facilitate and promote the sport of Flying. We provide a suitable site for flight operations in Central Mississippi and a forum for safety education, exchange of technical information, and other cooperative activities. We strive to bring the combined influence of CMLF to bear on the public policy issues affecting sport aviation in general with particular emphisis on ultralight flying and light sport aircraft (LSA). We pursue initiatives to integrate ultralight flying into the general aviation community. We support the work and objectives of the larger Ultralight and LSA movements on the national and international levels.

Our motto is "Fly For Fun", and we try to enjoy flying together to various events throughout the year. Whether it's a fly-in, a "$100 Hamburger", or a flight to a friend's strip, the fun is in doing it together safely! We enjoy sharing ideas, maintenance problems, building projects, and recent flying experiences .

title: Frontier Flyers (Club in Formation)
name: Frontier Flyers (Club in Formation)
description:
New flying club forming in Cheyenne.
Please contact Jay for more information - 307 286 1862

title: Olds Forge Flyers, Inc.
name: Olds Forge Flyers, Inc.
description:
The Olds Forge Flyers, Inc. was founded in 1945 by five workers at the Oldsmobile forge plant, and is the oldest (we think) continuously operating flying club in the US. The non-profit club's members have equity ownership of the aircraft, at present a Cessna 172P Skyhawk and a Piper Archer II, both IFR certified and equipped with dual Garmin G5s, a Garmin GTN 650Xi and an L-3 Lynx transponder.  The Archer has a Garmin GFC 500 autopilot with the Smart Glide feature..  

The aircraft are kept at AvFlight’s T-hangars at the Capital Region International Airport (KLAN).  Warm indoor pre-flighting is available inside AvFligjht’s big hangar and is an added benefit in the winter.  The line crew will even pull the plane out of the hangar with you in it!  And when you get back, the crew will put it away for you!  We have a nice computer equipped office in the AvFlight building.  

Our rates and dues structure are reviewed at least twice a year enabling us to keep up with fluctuating costs.  The current dues are $85/month.  The Skyhawk rents for $105/hour wet and the Archer for $115/hour wet.  There is an annual insurance deductible waiver fee of $100 which is assessed each May and pro-rated for new members.  This creates a fund which pays your share ($5,000) of the deductible if you have an incident.  There is an equity fee of $1500.  We have a payment plan for the fee.  We're proud of our aircraft which are meticulously maintained and we think are the best available in the Lansing area.  Our goal is to provide the safest possible flying at the lowest possible cost.  A check out in each plane with one of our instructors is required for approval to schedule the aircraft.  We have an on-line scheduling system accessible with any internet capable device.  Check out our Facebook page and "like" us. 

Please contact us for a meeting to inspect our facilities/aircraft and answer any further questions you may have.  EMail us for an application and to schedule a membership interview.

title: Silverado Soaring Club
name: Silverado Soaring Club
description:
Our Club operates with a full time glider in the California Wine Country called Crazy Creek and 2 gliders during the Summers at Truckee, CA and Winter at Minden NV.

title: Reading Aero Club

It is a great place to socialize, develop friendships, and learn more about our favorite pastime… flying!

title: Aero Club of Pennsylvania
name: Aero Club of Pennsylvania
description:
The Aero Club of PA was organized in December 1909 in Philadelphia for the purpose of “educating the public on matters of aeronautics”. 
Our goal remains intact as we:

   Offer Safety and aviation oriented presentations

title: Ace Flight Club
name: Ace Flight Club
description:
Membership Benefits:

Discounts on aircraft rentals and instruction
Four aircraft ready to fly
Overnight and weekend access to all club aircraft
Online aircraft and instructor scheduling
Monthly club meetings: food, fellowship, and fun!  
Great relationship with Ace staff and FBO community members
 
Membership Fees

Enrollment fee of $299
Monthly access fee of $30
Flight club members are required to have a credit card on file; the monthly access fee will be charged to this card the first of each month
Minimum one year (12 months) commitment for all new flight club members
Monthly access fees are guaranteed for the Club year June 1 - May 31 
Monthly access fees are pro-rated for the month of enrollment
Prices, terms, and aircraft are subject to change
 
Membership Requirements

Members must complete an application and possess at least a Student Pilot Certificate and valid FAA medical certificate.
Members must complete an applicable aircraft checkout with an Ace Aviation Instructor
Unless outlined as a specific club benefit, all standard operating procedures of Ace Aviation apply; including those outlined in the Customer & Airport User Handbook and Blanket Aircraft Rental Agreement.
 
Aircraft Scheduling

Maximum 10 reservations at once

Club Meetings

Communication

Questions may be sent to Info@AceAviation.biz

title: Back 40 Flying Club
name: Back 40 Flying Club
description: Experience the ease of flying out of Fort Wayne International Airport. Our club enjoys excellent service from the Fort Wayne Aero Center, including aircraft fueling and towing. Heated hangars, long runways and friendly air traffic control make FWA an excellent place to be. The Back 40 Flying Club has been in operation since 1952. Experience up to date, meticulously-maintained aircraft, the best service and excellent availability.

title: Wild River Flying Club
name: Wild River Flying Club
description:
Welcome to the Wild River Flying Club (WRFC)!  We are a non-profit, social flying club located at the Osceola Municipal Airport (KOEO) in Osceola, Wisconsin on the banks of the scenic St. Croix River.

WRFC was founded in 1971 by several local pilots one Saturday morning over breakfast in Dresser, WI as the "Mouseketeers" with just one airplane and a hangar.  Through the years, as they grew in size and added another airplane, they incorporated and renamed themselves the Wild River Flying Club.  

The Club has grown to what it is today - a well-respected, financially sound flying club with four diverse airplanes, two hangars, a 2,000 gallon fuel system, and only 32 members.  We challenge you to find a club with these amenities.  Browse our website and let us know how we can help you achieve your flying goals.

title: NRI Flying Club, Inc.

description: The purpose of NRI is to provide an educational, social, and economic base for pilots, with flying at the most convenient, safe, and cost-effective level possible. NRI strives to have the highest quality aircraft for its members, with maximum availability.

title: Airheads Flying Club
name: Airheads Flying Club
description:
Airheads Flying Club, based in the scenic city of Martinsburg, West Virginia, is a vibrant community of aviation enthusiasts and pilots. Founded with the vision of sharing the thrill and passion for flying, the club offers an array of services and experiences for both seasoned pilots and those new to the skies.

Airheads operates a single 1968 Cessna 172I. Its a solid and reliable plane with low hours on the engine and airframe. Airheads is actively growing its membership so that it can operate a fleet of aircraft that caters to all pilots needs. 

If you are an aircraft owner and are interested in learning more about our Leaseback Program reach out to us!

The club's location in Martinsburg, known for its picturesque landscapes and clear skies, is ideal for both training and recreational flying. With access to the Eastern Panhandle's landmarks and the beauty of the Appalachian region, flights from Martinsburg offer stunning views and diverse flying experiences.

Airheads Flying Club is also committed to education and safety. It regularly hosts safety seminars, flying events, and social gatherings, where members can learn, share experiences, and foster a culture of safe and responsible flying.

For those aspiring to become pilots, the club provides an affordable pathway. It connects members to certified flight instructors for private, instrument, commercial, and other advanced ratings

title: Spirit Flyers, Inc.
name: Spirit Flyers, Inc.
description:
Spirit Flyers is a non-profit flying club based at KSUS (Spirit of St. Louis Airport) in Chesterfield, MO. Our club owns two airplanes, a PA32-301T and a PA28-200. Both are hangered next to each other in the Spirit of St. Louis County T's. 

We have been a flying club in the St. Louis area for 25+ years and have a great group of pilots who love to share their passion for flying with each other! 

Since we are a member owned club, there are no daily minimums on trips. Our Hobbs meter, which is what we bill based on, only runs when the wheels are off the ground - so you aren't billed for runup and taxiing!

title: Northeast Florida Aero Club, Inc
name: Northeast Florida Aero Club, Inc
description:
The Northeast Florida Aero Club (NEFLAC) was formed by local pilots in December 2019. The club owns and operates 4 fully IFR certified aircraft with 3 aircraft being TAA:
1) 1967 PA-28-180 Piper Cherokee 'C', with Garmin GFC500 Autopilot, GNX375 Navigator (ADS-B Out/In), dual G5 EFI, GTR225 COM and INS 429 VOR/ILS
2) 1965 C-172F Skyhawk, Air Plains 180HP STC engine, with Garmin GFC500 Autopilot, GTN750 NAV/COM/XPDR/(ADS-B Out/In), dual G5 EFI, GNC255 NAV/COM, Apollo SL15 Audio Panel and GEM 610 engine monitor
3) 1975 C-182P Skylane with Garmin G500 Glass Panel, GTN750 and GTN650 GPS/NAV/COM, GTX345 (ADS-B Out/In) XPDR and GMA350C Audio Panel
4) 1973 C-150L with dual G5 EFI, GNX375 Navigator (ADS-B Out/In), GNC255 NAV/COM, PMA6000B Audio Panel

All aircraft are hangared at the Northeast Florida Regional Airport (KSGJ) with 3 aircraft located in the same hangar row. Hangars have a few amenities like small refrigerators, desk, chairs and cleaning and aircraft supplies.

NEFLAC membership is almost full but the club continuously accepts applications for the waiting-list in the order which they are received. Contact us at (904) 571-5068 or membership@neflac.com to learn more about NEFLAC or to schedule a visit to see our club aircraft and facilities.

The club is always open for leased-back aircraft to add to our fleet. Over the years we have operated and maintained two leased aircraft. If you are an aircraft owner interested in leasing your aircraft to the club please reach out to us for more information and details.

As part of joining NEFLAC we also ask members to join the local St Augustine Airport Pilots Association (SAAPA) (www.saapaclub.com).

For NEFLAC Bylaws and Rules of Conduct visit: www.neflac.com/membership or visit our main website at: www.neflac.com.

 Thanks for flying by.

*NOTE: Information provided subject to change without notice. Call 904-571-5068 for latest information*

title: American Flight Club
name: American Flight Club
description:
AMERICA'S ULTIMATE TIME BUILDING CLUB FOR COMMERCIAL BOUND PILOTS
We are a mission based Flight Club

Flight Club vs Flying Club
Flying is for fun. Flights have a specific mission for flying. Building time is not a mission. It is a requirement. Your real mission is to build flight experience.  We give you the aircraft and the mentoring you need to build real life decision making tools.

But we added just the right amount of fun too!
We combine a mix of fun, social events and flying to make your experiences memorial. We encourage our pilots to bring family and friends. 

Make a vacation of it! Hike, camp, fish, boat, ride a dirt bike, explore the desert in a jeep, shoot targets, ride horses, yes even gamble. 

Stay in our basecamp or rent a hotel room. Have it your way.

Get it done!
We are a club that is specifically designed to meet the needs of pilots who benefit financially from having more total time. 
• Meet FAA requirements (ATP hours, ME Ratings, IFR Ratings)
• Qualify for or Lower Insurance Costs
• Qualify to fly bigger and faster aircraft
• Meet job requirments

Our members come from all over the world to build time in our aircraft. Our rates and the quality of our aircraft cannot be matched. We are a not-for profit club designed to help new pilots get higher paying aviation jobs faster.

Memberships are for a lifetime, your hours are good for a lifetime too! You cannot have too many hours of flight experience.

title: North Coast Lite Flyers

title: Flying 20 Club, Inc.
name: Flying 20 Club, Inc.
description:
The Flying 20 Club was originally incorporated in Danbury, Connecticut on June 22, 1940, making it one of the oldest active clubs in the United States. The original twenty individuals, who each put-up $20 to buy a J-2 Cub for $400, formed the club to encourage interest in aviation, to promote safe and economical flying for its members, and to encourage and assist its members to advance in the field of aviation.

title: Club in Formation - Cessna 206
name: Club in Formation - Cessna 206
description:
I'm interested in acquiring an old Cessna 206 (P206 or older U206) to start a partnership or small club. Seems like a great balance all around. Much cheaper purchase and overhaul than newer Lycoming based models, with more useful load.

The target aircraft is (or will be) IFR equipped (to help get there/home) but also outfitted for mountain flying and grass/dirt strips for exploring the amazing PNW. 

Would like to base at KBFI, and planning on tie-down due to outrageous hangar rates.

Specs for a purchase, or future plans would  include:
- no corrosion, good condition airframe without a crazy number of hours 
- heavy nose gear
- slightly upsized tires 
- STOL cuff (Sportsman preferred)
- VG’s
- Turbo model considered
- Modern WAAS/IFR GPS
- Garmin G5’s, Aspen PFD, or G3X (ideally simple panel, consolidating with modern instrumentation)
- ADSB IN/OUT
- Engine monitor
- Autopilot (to help with workload while getting to/from the destination), modern digital autopilot strongly preferred.

Prefer partners that appreciate what new technology brings to aviation, and fit more into the “upgrade” vs “repair/replace with the same” when it comes to equipment failures and logical upgrade opportunities. 

If the stars align it would also be a nice looking aircraft that is spouse approved. But, I would rather fly a well equipped safe aircraft than an old abused one with leather and fresh paint.:)

Previous discussion with insurance providers informed me that 5 or less partners is  easy, above that and it gets expensive/complicated. Premiums tend to charge based on the lowest experience, so private pilot, ideally with instrument rating, and 50hrs high perf time is strongly preferred.

Early stages here, and in no hurry (in a good club at present), but if this describes your ideal partnership/club, please reach out.

We enjoy restoring aircraft and using the talents and abilities of the club members to serve the club as a whole. Come join us in Northern California where we enjoy beautiful flying weather at the KRDD (Redding Municipal) controlled airfield.

We 501-C-7 IRS mutual interest non-profit, non-charitable (no tax deduction for any donations) flying club. Membership is by invitation only. Any prospective member must work with us for a few times so the other members are able to discern whether or not an invitation should be extended.

The basis for the club is to minimize the dollars out of pocket while enjoying aviation. 

Every club member is required to participate in rebuilding aircraft and maintaining our aircraft. They become subject matter experts on the club aircraft because they rebuilt them.... and then the club has aircraft that are trusted and will be relatively maintenance free for years... because each aircraft is stripped down to the basics, wings off, etc, and we re-build... new wiring, new glass, overhauled of new instruments, bearings, seals, etc.
 
Our social programs: we meet every Saturday morning for breakfast and then onto the hangars for the weekly workday. Once a month, we host/present a pilot safety seminar that we call PIC Seminars (Pilot in Command).  The local EAA chapter will be allowing us to use their facility starting in March 2021. The address for the PIC seminars will be: EAA Chapter 157  -   2955 South Street  96001.
 
We have a 1963 C model,  C-150 flying, next  and 75% done is a 1952 C model Bonanza, then a 1966 H Cessna 172 and another 150 F model.

title: Cloud Niners, Inc.
name: Cloud Niners, Inc.
description:
Want to fly your own aircraft, but can’t justify the cost?  Consider a flying club.  It provides all the benefits of aircraft ownership, while sharing the financial burden.  A flying club is a "not-for-profit corporation" established for the purpose of affordable aircraft ownership. You fly the same aircraft on a regular basis, have a voice in its maintenance and improvements, but share the burden of hangar rental, insurance, and maintenance costs with the other shareholders (club members).

Cloud Niners is a flying club based at Hendricks County Airport/Gordon Graham Field (2R2). Cloud Niners has been operating since 1966 and our shareholders range from student pilots to instrument rated pilots.  Cloud Niners currently owns a 1965 Cherokee 180.  The length of ownership in the flying club varies from one year to 36 years.

The number of shareholder in Cloud Niners is capped at 15 with one aircraft.  Scheduling is done online.  There is no daily minimum number of hours if using the aircraft for an extended period of time, such as a trip.

The aircraft has a maintenance coordinator that handles all maintenance issues for the aircraft, either non-scheduled (something breaks) or regular maintenance such as oil changes and annuals. If you are interested in maintenance, there are ways for you to assist.  If it’s not your thing it is handled for you.

To join Cloud Niners you purchase a share.  The price of a share (currently $8541.00) is determined annually, by dividing the Cloud Niners total net value and dividing by 15 shareholders.   Application for a share requires unanimous approval of shareholders.  This is Cloud Niners way of ensuring quality pilots.  If you need to leave Cloud Niners in the future, you offer your share for sale.  If after 6 months, a new member has not been found to purchase your share, the club must purchase it for 80% of the share value.

name: Manhattan Flying Tigers
description:
Founded in the late-1970's the KBZN based Manhattan Flying Tigers (MFT) is one of the oldest continuously active flying clubs in the region. 

Currently, the club is the proud owner of the Cessna 172 aircraft: N80830 is a 1976 "M" Model with a mild STOL Kit and N2330E a 1978 "N" Model. Both aircraft are powered by 180 horsepower Lycoming O-320 engines. Both aircraft are wholly owned by the club and are insured. In 2022, N2330E had a digital flight display and IFR GPS installed.

MFT is active within the Montana flying community and holds monthly meetings beginning September and ending in June.  We have a July picnic at the airport shelter for general aviation flyers and do not meet at all in August.  The monthly meetings are on the first Tuesday of each month at 7:00PM in the KBZN old terminal building (across the parking lot (north) from the control tower and north of Jet Aviation).  

Maximum members allowed for the two planes are 40.  Often times our membership is at its maximum of 40.  

Come join us at one of our meetings or view our website at www.bozemanflyingclub.com for more information.

title: Troy Oakland Pilots Flying Club
name: Troy Oakland Pilots Flying Club
description:
We are located at the Oakland-Troy Airport (KVLL) which is approximately 15 miles north of Downtown Detroit.
The purpose of the TOPS Flying Club is to provide safe, reliable, and pleasurable flying and/or flight instruction for members at the most reasonable cost possible.
The club provides a friendly atmosphere for its members. There are both flying and non-flying related gatherings scheduled throughout the year (holiday parties, flying trips, barbeques, etc).

Aircraft is IFR equipped with Aspen EFD 1000 Pro, Garmin GNS 430W, GMA 340, and GTX 330 transponder, King KX-170B nav/com, encoding altimeter, ADS-B compliant, Trutrak Vizion Autopilot, & ELT. Must hold a Private pilot rating or better. Cost: $5,500 initial entry, $110/month, $20/hour dry (must pay for your fuel). Aircraft has always been hangared.

title: Clearview Flying Club
name: Clearview Flying Club
description: We are a non for profit club to make flying affordable to everyone. We are starting with a Cessna 150 and do have access to a Cessna 172 as well. We are up and running with many new members and many other ready to get signed up. We are trying to bring aviation at Clearview back to where it was 30 years ago at Clearview. If you are interested in learning how to fly or already have a licences we are the right club for you. You will have the Max Fun at the most affordable cost at 2W2. We are also signing Social membership as well to include you in the planned monthly flyouts and events at the airport. SO JOIN THE CLUB!!!

title: JB Aviation Flight Club
name: JB Aviation Flight Club
description:
No Daily Minimums:

Remember why you got your license to begin with? To FLY! Maybe you dreamed of a weekend adventure with your family, a fishing trip with your friends, or an overnight trip on a moment’s notice. We’re pilots too, and we don’t believe in daily minimums. Take the plane overnight and only pay for the time the prop is turning.

Hassle-Free:

Our aircraft are equipped with a Garmin 650, KX 155, Garmin 340 audio panel, and new interiors. They each fly and feel the same. We did this with one goal in mind: a comprehensive and hassle-free check out process. Get checked-out in all six of our planes in as little as one flight!

Online Scheduling:

Each flight club member has personal access to our easy-to-use online scheduling. Browse aircraft availability and book reservations from your home computer or even on your smart phone. Our 24-7 system allows you to book at your convenience rather than during our office hours.

Community:

Is it too much to ask to have your flight club based at an airport you love? It’s not. Whether it’s fishing down at the pond, going for a walk on one of our trails, or just enjoying some hangar grilling, there’s always something to do at Galt. With your flight club membership, you will also recieve a six-month free membership for you and your family in Galt's EAA chapter 932.

title: Ava Aviation Club
name: Ava Aviation Club
description:
Why I'm interested in starting a club:
I live in a rural community in Southwest Missouri.  I started a ground school two years ago through Ava Schools.  They have been funding the ground school part, but can not help us with a plane.  We now have students who want to go on and earn their private and commercial certificates.  Many of our students are community adults and are interested in forming a club in order to get a plane.  We feel we can make flying more affordable by having our own plane.  We are working with the airport manager and he is willing to expand the operations of the airport if we can get more activity there. Our goal is to bring more young people into general aviation and maybe even a career.  

Description of the hangar/clubhouse facilities:
We have 4 hangars, two with planes at the present time.  There are other buildings which are former hangars which could be converted back.  We have a small office, but the group would like to update it.  There is a hangar which houses the on field mechanic.

Progress made towards starting the club:
We have had a representative from Cessna come down to meet with the group to talk about different aspects and cost of operation of aircraft.  Our mechanic on the field came and talked to the group about the maintenance of aircraft.  We have talked to existing flying clubs at other airports about how they are set up.  We have also talked to AOPA and watched some of their webinars on flying clubs.  We are members of Missouri Pilots Association and are in contact with other pilots about our ambition.  Several of the ground school students who are adults of the community want to be investors.  We are looking for others to help.  Our plan is to remodel the office on site to include a classroom for training and meetings.  Our airport manager plans to add fuel at the airport with this new interest.

~ David William Davidson

title: Midway Flying Club
name: Midway Flying Club
description:
The Midway Flying club was founded as a non-profit 501(c)(7) tax-exempt organization on October 2018 by a group of pilots who felt there was a need to bring affordable and safe flying opportunities in well-maintained and capable aircraft to the pilot community of  the Mid-Way Regional airport (KJWY) located half way between Midlothian and Waxahachie in Ellis county. The objective is to build up a club with a pilot-to-aircraft ratio that we feel is a good compromise between affordability and airplane availability for the individual member. The club aircraft is a Cessna Cardinal 177. We welcome pilots who are enthusiastic about flying and about continuing to improve their flying skills and experience. We meet the third Saturday of each month at 9:00 am through online virtual meeting (Meetings will return to the Mid-Way airport FBO conference room located at 131 Airport Drive, Midlothian, TX 76065  once social distancing is no longer recommened or required). 

Guests are welcome to come to our meetings - please send us an email if you are planning to attend.

title: Naples Flying Club
name: Naples Flying Club
description: Since its beginning in 1955, Naples Flying Club, Inc. has been dedicated to making recreational flying safe, affordable, and fun in Southwest Florida.  Consequently, the Club owns two, simple, easy to fly, easy to maintain, Cessna aircraft that have a great deal of commonality.  Every member owns an undivided interest in the aircraft, and because we are a not-for-profit entity our rental rates are favorable.  Reservations are handled through an on-line scheduling service and aircraft can be kept overnight without a punitive minimum daily rate.  Spreading costs over many members has its advantages.  Our monthly dues cover all fixed costs and the hourly rental rates (tachometer time, not hobbs) cover the variable costs.  You will find our members and volunteer directors to be friendly and professional.  Come on in and see for yourself.

title: Cross Country Flying Club
name: Cross Country Flying Club
description:
Cross Country Flying Club was founded on principles we share with our membership. Our focus on flight safety combined with a club environment provides an ideal setting for pilots that enjoy everything related to flying especially Cross Country Flying. 

The Club aircraft is selected to meet the needs of the membership.  A Low-Ratio of members to aircraft will be maintained to ensure a high level of availability. Advanced training which we encourage with the club instructors can include Commercial and Instrument rating on a Complex aircraft, with Tach-Time billing saves on every flight, we have found billing base on Tach-Time rather than traditional Hobb-Time is much better for the pilot's bottom line.  As we grow our members, we will seek to purchase a Six-Seater aircraft for the club.

We have created an exclusive club for those who really mind what they fly.  For those who are tired of Renting Airplanes, Here you will find a club that is designed for Cross Country Flying and will enjoy taking the plane for days without worrying about the cost of the minimums per day.

title: The Litchfield Hills Aero Club, LLC
name: The Litchfield Hills Aero Club, LLC
description:
Getting involved in Ballooning

Many people see balloons flying and it seems like an unreachable activity. Nothing could be further from the truth. Even for a pilot it is not really any more expensive than any other hobby but you can get into ballooning at virtually no cost by crewing.

Pilots always need a team of enthusiastic crew of almost any age. Regular crew can be sure of being offered opportunities to fly in the balloon and it is a sport that can take you all over the world. Make it known at a meeting that you are interested in crewing and you will be fighting off the offers! Ballooning is an extremely sociable activity as crews typically involve three or four people and morning flights often end up in the local "greasy spoon" for breakfast.

The Litchfield Hills Aero Club welcomes anyone with an interest in ballooning to join the club. There are two levels of membership available depending on your involvement in the club. Social Membership is the basic membership for those who do not wish to use the Club balloon. Each member receives a copy of our monthly newsletter the Q-Vent full of news, stories and details of ballooning events around the country and abroad.

We also offer a Flying Membership with equity ownership in the club balloon for an additional fee which includes, 10 hours of flight instruction with one of the clubs flight instructors. The flying membership allows members to learn how to fly and earn their private pilot's license. Once you earned your pilot certificate you are able schedule time and fly the club balloon.  The cost of equity membership is $2000.00 USD which includes 10 hours of flight instruction and low monthly fixed fee of $50.00.

title: Flying Engineers, INC.

description: Flying Engineers, Inc. is a 15 member non-profit 503(c)that owns a VFR 1970 Cessna 150K Aerobat with Indianapolis Regional Airport (MQJ) as our home base. Scheduling is rarely an issue. We do accept some student pilots if they meet other criteria. Current rates are $80 monthly and $110 per hour wet, which includes building reserves for the next engine overhaul. The aircraft is well maintained, hangared, and insured by the club.There is a very reasonable buy in cost. The club maintains a current set of legal documents, an approved CFI list, a waiting list, uses AircraftClubs.com for scheduling, and uses a strong set of officers to handle day to day operations. title: Infinity Aero Club Tampa Bay, Inc
name: Infinity Aero Club Tampa Bay, Inc
description:
Infinity Aero Club is an operational non-profit flying club, Aviation STEM education center, Aero Lab, and our fundraising venue formed by Ricardo Foster a 28-year retired Navy veteran in May 2020. Proceeds provide flying opportunities to traditionally underserved youth. Our organization shares the belief that flying clubs are a great way to make aviation more accessible and affordable.
 
We're seeking new members who desire to have access to different aircrafts, shared responsibility, a sense of community, become a better pilot, and building-time, while making a difference in our young adult lives! Our flying club has recently retained two modern, roomy, fun to fly, auto-pilot with full glass-cockpit Alto aircraft for time-building while showing its lower operating costs. Additionally, we utilize a 1961 Cessna 172B aircraft, which is a recently overhauled O-300 engine along with the avionics panel with newer instruments.

We have developed a drone, flight, and maintenance Aviation STEM program for teenagers (middle, high school & college). We meet as a club weekly on Saturdays (10 am-2 pm) at our hanger-home address (4639 Birdsong Blvd) at Tampa North Aero Park for Part 107 drone, Private Pilot ground school, hands-on flight simulator and drone flight training, intro flights, maintenance training with our in-resident FAA certified IA/A&P mechanic on our Cessna 172B restoration project. 

•	To learn more visit our facebook page: www.facebook.com/infinityaeroclub/ or our website at www.infinityaeroclub.org  
•	Our impact in the community: https://issuu.com/avination/docs/avination-summer-2021/28  
•	Video showcasing our flight simulator lab: https://vimeo.com/534601625 
•	Featured on Fox News: https://www.fox13news.com/news/bay-area-stem-program-helps-disadvantaged-teens-take-dreams-to-new-heights 
 
Contact us:

Ricardo Foster, LCDR, USN (Ret.)

title: Eagle Air Flying Club, Inc.
name: Eagle Air Flying Club, Inc.
description:
Eagle Air Flying Club is a not for profit social/recreational corporation in the state of Ohio. Founded in 2003 we are a group of pilots passionate about flying and introducing others to the thrill of flight. We have two airplanes a Piper Cherokee and a Piper Arrow, both are instrument flight capable airplanes. Approximately 50% of our club members have joined the club to learn to fly and continued their membership for the fellowship and cost savings with shared ownership such as our club. Located in NW Ohio by the great lakes, we are positioned well for primary flight instruction, with lots of open airspace right in our area and a short flight to complex airspace such as Detroit, Indianapolis, Dayton or Cleveland pilots get real world experience and confidence to fly anywhere in the world.
Flying clubs are an excellent option for new pilots as well as experienced, with shared ownership there is a certain pride our members take with the airplanes. Having an active social club centered around what we love, flying, there are a lot of benefits to membership besides the cost savings. Regular monthly meetings, safety seminars, fly-ins, parties and such offer members the opportunity to hang out and immerse themselves in all things flying. Destinations such as Put in Bay, Cedar Point, Makinaw Island and Grand St Marys lake are just a short flight from our home airport Wood County Regional Airport, and offer a full day of activity for the entire family. title: 1028 Flying Club, LLC

title: The Great Plains Balloon Club
name: The Great Plains Balloon Club
description:
The Great Plains Balloon Club of Topeka, Inc. is a non-profit organization dedicated to the promotion and development of the art, science, and sport of hot air ballooning in the city of Topeka and the state of Kansas. Safety, courtesy, and fraternity are among the club's highest goals.

title: Dunedin Flying Club INC

To provide a social network where aviation enthusiasts can share ideas and experiences.

To assist our members in furthering their pilot education and skills.

title: US Flight Club
name: US Flight Club
description:
The purpose of our club is to provide safe late model aircraft at a reasonable price.  All aircraft will be air conditioned and have autopilots.  They also have dual Garmin GPS's with WAAS.

Monthly fee  = $205

title: Central Arkansas Flying Club
name: Central Arkansas Flying Club
description:
Our club is a non-profit organization which provides a social, aviation-oriented outlet for its members.  The organization caters primarily to private pilots, who are generally enthusiastic about aviation but do not have an outlet to meet and regularly interact with like-minded individuals. 

Our mission is to provide safe aviation for members by offering regularly scheduled safety classes, check rides, seminars and other safety related group activities.

Flight and Ground School instruction is offered by FAA-certified instructors allowing members to learn to fly and become pilots. 

Activities are primarily conducted at the Saline County Regional Airport and include club meetings, barbecues, and pot luck dinners.

title: Atlantic Flying Club
name: Atlantic Flying Club
description:
The Atlantic Flying Club was established at the Fernandina Beach Municipal Airport in 1970 by the late Gordan Dressler.  Gordon's plan was to form a club which would make flying affordable for all

 
The Club is a members owned and operated corporation located on lovely Amelia Island, Florida.  This means upon becoming a member, you actually become part owner.  The club's aircraft(s) is/are owned by it's members.  Not an individual.  The Club is structured in a way to allow all members who can not afford their own airplane an affordable option to fly without paying high rental fees.  The Club does this by calculating the operation costs associated with the airplane and implementing an hourly rate, without profit *(Currently $100.00).  Secondly the fixed costs, hanger fee, insurance, and so forth, are calculated and are covered by monthly dues (Currently $40.00).


We currently have a waiting list.

Airplane is a Beachcraft Sundowner.

name: Circle W Flying Club
description:
Memberships and flight training available for students as well as certificated pilots.

title: T-Craft Aero Club
name: T-Craft Aero Club
description:
We are a well established flying club, over 50 years, offering safe and well maintained aircraft at very reasonable rates in our own hanger.

The aircraft are member owned and the club is managed by a board of directors of members elected by the general membership.

description: C172N (Penn Yan 180 Hp Conversion) Flying Club located at Lancaster, PA Airport (KLNS) South T-Hangars.

title: Sky Knights Flight Club
name: Sky Knights Flight Club
description:
Sky Knights Flight Club unites a group of pilots and flight instructors with a fleet of Light Sport Aircraft for flight training and recreational flying... all in a fun, friendly environment. Come in and share our passion for aviation.

Students and licensed pilots enjoy access to our aircraft. When conditions aren't favorable for flying, students can hang out and join us 'flying the hangar'.

Sky Knights Flight Club is conveniently located at the South West corner of Camarillo Airport. We're open on weekends from around 11AM until sunset. We're eager to meet you!

title: Oklahoma Soaring Association
name: Oklahoma Soaring Association
description:
We have in our club 3 gliders:  A Grob 103; Schweizer-233 and Schwizer 1-26.

Monthly meetings are held on the third Tuesday of each month. Meetings start at 6:30 pm and are held at Ingrids Kitchen, 6501 N. May Ave. Oklahoma City, OK. 

All are welcome to participate in discussion of club activities and story telling all while enjoying some great food. 

Please contact us for membership and other information.

title: Long Island Soaring Association
name: Long Island Soaring Association
description:
The Long Island Soaring Association (LISA) is primarily a glider flying club, though we have some members who primarily fly our powered aircraft.  We have two 2-seat training gliders and two single seat gliders. We launch gliders by towing them with powered aircraft, so we also maintain a fleet of three powered aircraft, two of which are available for rental and training, including tailwheel training.  (The other power plane is our primary tow plane and is not generally flown for personal use at this time.)

We are a non-profit organization formed in 1955.  We are based at the Brookhaven Calabro Airport in Shirley, NY, which is a fairly busy general aviation airport, especially in the summer.  Many of our flights are training flights, with members pursuing pilot certificates from private to commercial and Certificated Flight Instructor in both gliders and airplanes.  We hold glider operations as often as possible Saturdays and Sundays and sometimes during the week if there is interest and a tow pilot (and if necessary, an instructor) available.  In keeping with long-standing tradition, our tow pilots, CFI-Gs (glider instructors) and officers are all unpaid volunteers, allowing us to keep flying costs low.  (Instructors in the power planes however are permitted to set their own rates for airplane flight instruction.)

Non-members are able to fly gliders with an instructor or commercial pilot onboard as Introductory Rides (primarily intended for individuals who might be interested in joining our club) or as Sightseeing / Gift Certificate flights.  Fee information is available on our website.

If you're on Long Island and want to see what it's like to soar, get in touch with us!

title: Flying Educators Flying Club
name: Flying Educators Flying Club
description:
Shares are purchased from the corporation,  not member to member. Share price is determined by the corporation to reflect aircraft value at given time.  When you leave the club you are reimbursed current set aircraft value and don’t have to worry about trying to sell your share.

Membership is limited to 12 members. Each member holds equal equity in the flying club.

Must hold Private Pilots License, Medical, FAA Flight Review. We don’t allow student pilots at this time.

We have Club Bylaws and Operational Rules. Current officers are the President, Vice President and Secretary/Treasurer.

Quarterly meetings to discuss financials, maintenance and safety topics.

Aircraft is kept inside hangar off Hotel taxiway and near runway 9 at FXE.

We are one of the oldest non profit flying clubs in south Florida. Est 1962.

No minimum hours required to fly each month. If member has not flown in three months you are required to fly with another member to regain club currency. Members must also conduct a training flight every 180 days.

24/7 access to airplane.

Flexible online scheduling. Airplane reservation for multiple nights is ok. No minimum hrs required to fly during your reservation.  Any reservation over one week requires club approval.

Flying to the Bahamas is ok.

No extra insurance is required for member. Part of your dues cover this cost.

Well maintained aircraft and proper records are kept. Members wash and clean aircraft after use. Airplane is kept in hangar. One member is an A&P and monitors club maintenance.

The club maintains cash reserves for general maintenance, annual inspection and major overhaul.

New applicants will be required to go through orientation flights and be signed off by a certified flight instructor.

Current Aircraft: 1991 Grumman Tiger AG-5B. Aspen E5, Two Axis Auto Pilot, Garmin 430. Useful load 882 lbs.

title: Titusville Flying Club

title: Arizona Cloudbusters, Inc.
name: Arizona Cloudbusters, Inc.
description:
The Arizona Cloudbusters Flying Club has been in continuous operation since 1959.  We are a club of aviation enthusiasts who have banded together to make flying nice, clean, well maintained airplanes more affordable.

We are located at Chandler Municipal Airport (KCHD) in Chandler, AZ.  This airport provides easy access in and out of the Phoenix area with no delays.

Along with currently licensed pilots, we welcome student pilots ready to take to the skies at a cost significantly less than any flight school.

In addition to affordable flying, our club also provides opportunities for pilots to socialize, fly together, participate in and learn about aircraft ownership, and train for additional licenses and ratings. 

We currently own and operate a 2001 Cessna 172SP Skyhawk, a 1998 Cessna 182S Skylane, and a 1966 Beechcraft Debonair C33.

We keep the costs of flying down with low monthly membership dues and by adjusting the hourly aircraft rates to stay in line with fuel costs.  We operate as a non-profit company so our rates are as low as possible.

Monthly membership meetings give pilot-owners time to come together to discuss our current affairs as well as help shape our clubs' future.

title: Cleveland Soaring Society, Inc.
name: Cleveland Soaring Society, Inc.
description:

CSS is a charter chapter of The Soaring Society of America, our parent organization and national advocacy group for soaring in the United States.

Cleveland Soaring Society flies every weekend, April through October - 
weather permitting.  

We also fly on weekday afternoons, when possible.

title: Eximious Flying Club
name: Eximious Flying Club
description:
Eximious Flying Club is the oldest continuously-operating Club in SE Michigan, having been founded in 1958.  The Club has a three-tier aircraft fleet:  a Flight Design CTLS primarily for lower-time and student pilots; a very well-equipped Archer II, for more advanced flying; and a Commander 114 in the complex/high-performance category.  Eximious is the only Club in the world known to have a Commander 114 and this beautiful aircraft is our flagship.  All planes have ADS-B in/out and autopilots; the CTLS has an airframe parachute installation.  The Archer and Commander are fully equipped for instrument flight, and the Archer serves as the trainer for those seeking an instrument rating.

The Club has hangars at three local airports:  Detroit City (KDET); Oakland-Troy (KVLL); and Ray Community (57D).  The Ray location was chosen in part because it is the center of EAA activity in the region and also serves a growing part of the Metro area.  Planes are shifted periodically among these locations to insure balanced Member access.  As of February 2021 the CTLS is at DET, the Archer at 57D, and the Commander is at VLL.  The Club is very self-contained, with Member CFI/CFII instructors and a Member A&P/IA.  The Club Safety officer is a 19,000 hour airline line-check Captain.

Please go to our website for lots more information and photos (eximiousflyingclub.com).

title: Comal Aero, Inc.

description:
Comal Aero Inc. is an Incorporated 501(c)(7) Not for Profit Club Based at the New Braunfels National Airport (KBAZ) Located Between San Antonio and Austin, TX. Our Bylaws Provide Ten (10) Member Shares. The Club Does Not Value Individual Member Shares. To Join Comal Aero Inc. You Must Purchase an Existing Share from a Current Member at a Mutually Agreed Upon Price With the Approval of the Majority of the Remaining Members. Shares are Available on an Irregular Basis.

Paint/Interior w/Sheepskin Covers are Average. Plane Flies Approx. 150 hours per Year. Stored at City Owned T-Hangars. Electric Tug, Battery Maintainers, Cowling/Other Plugs, XC Gear. Savvy Breakdown Program.

Avionics Include: Aspen EFD1000 Pro Max Dual EFI, Garmin GNS 430W GPS, Garmin GNC 215 Nav/Comm w/GS, Garmin GTX 327 Xponder, PS Engineering PMA 8000G Audio Panel, Garmin GDL 88 ADS-B (In/Out), Garmin Flight Stream 210 (Bluetooth), S-TEC 30 2 Axis Autopilot, JPI EDM 830 Engine Monitor, Dynon D3 Backup Attitude Indicator, USB Ports, Digital Clock and CO Monitor. Pilot Side Lower Panel Upgraded with New Switches/Breakers. Transponder/Pitot Systems Certified to IFR standards. Extra Headsets and RAM Tablet Holders.

title: NRV Flyers, Inc
name: NRV Flyers, Inc
description:
NRV Flyers owns and operates a well equipped 1974 Mooney Ranger (M20C) hangered at KPSK. Shareholders of the corporation operate N7117V for local flying, flight training, and short and extended cross-country flying.

NRV Flyers operated as an informal flying club from KPSK more than 10 years before incorporating in 2013. In 2013, five club members established the corporation in order to ensure continued long-term operation of the club with a well-equipped IFR aircraft, ensure equal investment in the aircraft, and to facilitate transfer of ownership as members join or leave the club from time to time.

Members of the club have owned and operated the Ranger for more than 10 years. N7117V is a 180hp short-body Mooney with electric gear and flaps. Upgrades include a J-model cowl, windscreen, and wingtips. The IFR panel includes a WAAS enabled GNS530, second nav/com, and G3 Insight Engine Monitor. Recent major maintenance includes fuel tank strip/reseal in 2015, new Hartzell Scimitar prop in 2014, and engine overhaul in 2013. 

NRV Flyers is currently seeking a new shareholder to take the place of an owner who has decided to retire from flying. Shareholders should have at least 200hrs flight experience, instrument rating preferred, and an interest in actively maintaining the aircraft in top condition (to include owner-assisted maintenance). Complex/Instrument instruction from a CFI/Mooney owner is available at KPSK.

Current Rates:
- Quarterly Fixed Cost (hanger, insurance, taxes): $350 per shareholder
- Hourly Operating Cost (fuel, maintenance, engine reserve) - $100 per tach hour, wet
- Corporate Shares - based on market value of the club assets

title: Flying Particles, Inc.
name: Flying Particles, Inc.
description:
The University of California “Radiation” Laboratory was founded in 1952 on the site of a Navy Airman’s Training Center on the East side of the town of Livermore, California. That site had been used prior to World War II for one of the original Airmail Postal airports on the East-West route leading through the Salt Lake City area. Even by the 1920?s, it had been realized that the eastern end of the Livermore Valley had the best weather and provided the most reliable terminus for flights into and out of the often foggy San Francisco Bay area.

The earliest beginnings of the Flying Particles go back to 1957, when the Livermore Airport was located at the site of a present day trailer park at the Portola Avenue exit from Highway 580. The club was founded by five lab employees who wished to share the costs of airplane ownership. The first airplane was a Piper Cub, which rented for $3.00 per hour (fuel included!) Flight instruction was $2.00 per hour. The club expanded over the next few years, with the next major acquisition being a Piper Tri-Pacer (4 seats – the “Queen of the Fleet”.) At some point, a Luscombe was added to the collection. The airplanes were effectively bought by the club, although it is unclear how title was held. In the very early 1960?s, the Flying Particles, Inc. (FPI) was incorporated as a not-for-profit California corporation. This allowed a clear avenue for joint ownership, as well as the usual limitation of liability for club members.

www.flyingparticles.org/

title: Gastonia Aero Club
name: Gastonia Aero Club
description:
Gastonia Aero Club was formed in 1987 for the express purpose of "promoting an interest in flying and recreational aviation...and to do all other things necessary or expedient" [in fostering that interest].  That's the legal version out of the club' by laws.  The "plain English" version is that we've been in the business of buying and maintaining good quality airplanes and matching them up with good pilots who both enjoy aviation and are safety focused for almost 20 years!
 
We own three aircraft with differences that reflect the variety of missions for which they are suited and the operational desires of the club.  Our aircraft are:

         N80641 - A Cessna 172M, this  aircraft represents the trusted friend that many pilots first took to the skies with.  She's not a fancy bird, but she's clean and well maintained and capable, with good "steam gauge" avionics and IFR certification. Also, with the Penn Yan Aero 180 HP conversion, she's got a lot of giddyup-go in her!
         N9321J - A Piper Cherokee 180, this one is our prima donna.  She's cute and fast, and attracts lots of attention at every airport. This jewel has a 50 gallon fuel capacity,and a 180 HP engine.  She flies like a dream.

Gastonia Aero Club is organized as a "C" Corporation in North Carolina in 1987, and is registered with the North Carolina Secretary of State.  We are a membership organization with a maximum of 33 memberships outstanding.  Our members include both professional aviators (including a retired Eastern Airlines Captain), business professionals and entrepreneurs, retired folks and others--a broad mix of members.

name: Sporty's Flying Club
description:
Sporty's Flying Club is the perfect venue to engage in the fun, thrilling adventures general aviation provides.  The Club setting offers a perfect balance of convenience and value - the ideal alternative to the headaches of airplane ownership and unpredictable "rentals".

The Club is managed by Sporty's Eastern Cincinnati Aviation. Members must complete an application and possess a Recreational Pilot Certificate or higher and valid FAA Medical Certificate to join.  Membership is limited to 15. Members must receive an airplane checkout from a Sporty's Academy instructor for the applicable airplane and complete an annual proficiency check. Members must possess a minimum of $50,000 of non-owners (hull) insurance coverage.

Airplane rental rates are guaranteed for the Club year June 1 - May 31. Membership commitment is 1 year with automatic monthly renewals.

title: Fruit Belt Flyers Inc
name: Fruit Belt Flyers Inc
description: Incorporated in 1947, Fruit Belt Flyers Inc, is flying club consisting of a small number of members who own and operate a Cessna Skyhawk 172N. The airplane has recently been outfitted with a Garmin GPS and is certified for IFR flight. The club is open to both private and student pilots. If interested, contact Christian Gianni at (269) 277-9586.

title: Greene County Flying Club
name: Greene County Flying Club
description:
The Greene County Flying Club was started by SOAR in 2017. SOAR stands for Support Our Aviation Resources. SOAR is a 501C3, tax exempt foundation and was founded by a group of pilots and aviation enthusiasts several years ago who wanted to make sure we didn’t lose our little airport to a giant shopping center. SOAR sponsored the Greene County Flying Club in 2017 with the understanding that we would spin off as our own entity in two years.
We are located at KWAY, Waynesburg, PA.

Early in 2019 we learned we were approved by the IRS as a 501C3 charity and we continued as a flying club with our new mission: To provide access to safe and affordable flight and flight training to club members and to promote and support experimentation in all forms of aviation including drones, electric aircraft, ultra-lights and alternative airborne vehicles.  

We have three planes. For the Piper Challenger, we charge $94 per Hobbs hour, wet. The Taylorcraft F22A is a rare bird. This is one of six planes that were manufactured by Taylorcraft before they went bankrupt. We charge $74 per Hobbs hour and  this is also wet. Finally, we have the Ercoupe 415D which gets $54 per Hobbs hour, wet.

title: Sky-Vu Flyers, Inc.
name: Sky-Vu Flyers, Inc.
description: With airplanes located at Eagle Creek Airpark Airport (KEYE) and Indianapolis Metropolitan Airport (KUMP), Sky-Vu Flyers is the premier, not-for-profit flying club in the Indianapolis metro area and one of the oldest in the country.  This club has been in continuous operation since 1956 and currently boasts 3 great Cessna aircraft and 2 Cirrus aircraft.  This is an equity-based flying club where members purchase a share in the club and pay very reasonable monthly dues, and the lowest hourly costs anywhere.  If you're looking for a low-cost, HIGH-VALUE experience in aircraft ownership (all the fun without the shock of unanticipated major repair expenses), then you need to check out a membership in Sky-Vu Flyers!

title: Mohawk Soaring Club, Inc.
name: Mohawk Soaring Club, Inc.
description: Located in the Berkshires the Mohawk Soaring Club is dedicated to Glider Flight Instruction and flying Sailplanes (gliders) over western Massachusetts, Eastern New York, and Southern VT. We have a ridge located close by which offers many opportunities for extended flight.

title: Alman Bonanza Club
name: Alman Bonanza Club
description:

The club operates two Beechcraft Bonanza aircraft; a 1979 Bonanza A 36 and a 1992 Bonanza F33. Both aircraft are IFR equipped (including WAAS enabled Garmin navigators, GFC500 autopilot, G5 ADI/HSI) and are hangared at Miami Executive Airport (KTMB) in Miami, Florida.

Club membership is limited to 25 individuals. Each member owns an equal interest in the corporation.

Our club is the most economical way to fly a high performance Bonanza !

title: Mockingbird Flying Club
name: Mockingbird Flying Club
description:
For over 50 years the Mockingbird Flying Club, based at the Sioux Falls Airport, has provided area pilots with safe and affordable personal aviation.  �

The 35 member Mockingbird flying club owns three IFR equipped, professionally maintained and insured planes. The hangers are equipped with electric doors and are easily accessible. Scheduling and billing is convenient using your computer or smart phone. The financially sound club offers low rates, consistent leadership, instructors, safety pilots and the camaraderie of fellow aviation enthusiasts.

Social opportunities include fall and spring "birdie parties" where members and their families have a picnic and wash and wax club airplanes. An annual business meeting is held in January and a Spring Banquet and Awards Ceremony in March. There are safety seminars, group flight reviews, and flying activities to interesting airports

title: AeroFlyte of Pomona, Inc
name: AeroFlyte of Pomona, Inc
description: Club was incorpoated in 1970 and has called Cable Airport home since its beginning. We own a beautiful IFR equipped Cessna 182 Skylane with new paint since 2020. The interior is rated 8 and very comfortable with a nice suite of avionics, Rosen Visors, 3 point seat belt harnesses and is well maintained. All club members treat our airplane as if we were individual owners. Airplane is always kept in a hanger with a great view of the runway and pattern traffic. Ideal place for members to hang out and share flying stories and experiences. Call for a membership application to join our private club and learn about all the benefits of being an owner at a fraction of the expense.

title: Puget Sound Flyers, NP
name: Puget Sound Flyers, NP
description: Puget Sound Flyers is a new non profit flying club located at Paine Field (KPAE). We have highly maintained Aircraft that any pilot would enjoy to fly and affordable rental rates to compare to flight schools around the Sound. description:

name: Elkhart Wings

We have Regular Members who have paid more to be able to fly the aircraft, and we have an Associate Member level for family members and social members. We work to limit our Regular Membership to a number that results in around 200 hours per year put on each aircraft and never more than 100 regular members. title: Chandelle Flying Club
name: Chandelle Flying Club
description:
Chandelle Flying Club, Inc., is an incorporated not-for-profit club based in Austin, Texas that was established for the flying pleasure of its members (shareholders). Chandelle operates similar to an aircraft partnership in that each member is a partial owner of the corporation that owns the aircraft. Our bylaws limit the membership to a maximum of thirty (30), however we have have limited membership to 28 owner pilots for the foreseeable future. Each owner/pilot owns a share of our 'C Corp' which in turn owns the club assets.  

Currently, we own a 1980 Piper Dakota, a 1978 Piper Archer II, and a 1976 Piper Warrior. All three aircraft are IFR certified with IFR GPS units, and are based at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) at Signature flight support. The Dakota qualifies as a Technically Advanced Airplane.  All three planes are kept in hangars.

Presently all airplanes are owned  by the club, we have never done a leaseback.  Only our owner pilots can fly our aircraft, we do not rent to nonmembers.    There are no required minimum overnight charges.   Owner/pilots can schedule an airplane for up to seven days, 30 days in advance.   Owner/pilots can schedule longer flights more than 30 days in advance  with Board of Directors approval.    For example on most years you'll see at least one of our airplanes at AirVenture.

Joining Chandelle Flying Club is a much less expensive way to Fly General Aviation Aircraft than your traditional flight school. There is no better way to fly airplanes in Austin, TX than Chandelle Flying Club.

Operations of the club are delegated to elected members who run for positions of officers, board of directors, and maintenance officers.Basic aircraft maintenance is performed by volunteer members, and more extensive aircraft maintenance is outsourced to professionals.

To become a member of Chandelle, you must purchase a share from an existing member and be approved by our board of directors.  Shares are usually available.

title: The High Flying Club, Inc
name: The High Flying Club, Inc
description:
Looking for a 6-place plane?

The High Flying Club based at Smith Field in Fort Wayne Indiana since 1972, is 100% member-owned.   The High Flying Club owns a well-maintained 1973 Piper Cherokee Six.  Model number PA-32-300. Tail number N40784.  The plane has six forward-facing seats and a useful load of 1400 lbs.  It has a fuel-injected 300-hp Lycoming IO-540 engine.  This IFR-certified craft has a beautiful modern panel with two Garmin G5 units, GFC 500 Auto-pilot, Flight Stream 210, Garmin WAAS 430, and Garmin GTX 345 ADS-B Transponder.  

We recently added a Piper Arrow Turbo.  The Arrow is a four-place, retractable-gear turbo, PA-28RT-201T.  It has a fuel-injected Continental TSIO-360-FB engine.   This plane has a useful load of 950 pounds.  Climbs at 900 FPM at sea level and has a service ceiling of 20,000'.  The plane can cruise at 168 knots at altitude, sipping 11 GPH, at 75% power.  Auburn DeKalb County Airport will be its home.

Potential members can join our waitlist.  With a limited number of owners, the plane's availability is not a problem.  Our member meetings are on the 3rd Saturday of each month beginning at 9:00 AM at the Smith Field FBO.  We discuss regular maintenance and safety. During the warmer months, the club plans periodic social events.

Our formal onboarding process includes meeting the current members, completing an application, viewing the craft, and voting by the club.  Once accepted, potential members will have a detailed procedure review, and complete a safety checkout.

title: Land-O-Lakes Flying Club, Inc.

description:
The Land-O-Lakes Flying Club formed on December 1, 1958 is one of Michigan's oldest and most distinguished flying clubs.  

Land-O-Lakes Flying Club, based at Oakland County International Airport (KPTK), is very proud of its rich flying heritage serving pilots across southeast Michigan for more than 61 years with the flying experience they want at a price they can afford.  

Flying club aircraft are a Piper Archer II and a Piper Dakota. We chose the Piper Archer and the Piper Dakota because they are good, safe, and reliable aircraft with proven safety records. Both aircraft are similarly equipped with comparable electronics to enhance pilot familiarity and safety.

Visit us at www.lolflyingclub.org

title: Skypark Aero Club
name: Skypark Aero Club
description:
Founded in 1973 as a nonprofit, Skypark Aero Club offers affordable flying opportunities, with reasonable hourly rates and modest monthly dues. Our club is committed to sharing the passion and enjoyment of aviation, building camaraderie, and supporting members in becoming better pilots. 

The Club owns one airplane, an IFR equipped Piper Archer II based at the Piqua Ohio airport (I17). 

Club members reserve the airplane online on a first-come, first served basis.  The hourly rate includes all operating costs (fuel, oil, maintenance). Membership dues include an equal share of monthly costs for fixed expenses (hangar rent, insurance, annual inspection). There is a small membership deposit required - refunded should you ever want to leave the club - and a nominal initiation fee. 

Monthly meetings are held at 7:00 pm on the 3rd Wednesday of each month.  Guests are always welcome. 

We welcome further membership inquiries, which may be submitted through the club's official email address at: skyparkaeroclub@gmail.com

title: Lakeway Flying Club (Closed)

The Lakeway Flying Club, Inc. is a not-for-profit corporation organized for the express purpose of providing its members with aircraft for their personal use and enjoyment. 

No need for you to buy a large chunk of an airplane and incur the costs of a partial owner. With low monthly fees and very competitive hourly rates, Lakeway Flying club makes it affordable for you to fly. The monthly membership fee, currently set at $125.00, gives you access to two airplanes, and covers all the necessary costs such as maintenance, insurance, storage and incidentals. 

Current inventory includes  1177F Skyhawk, 6496B Skyhawk, 121EM Skylane, 77HM Beech Debonair and 763CD Cirrus SR22 . The club averages 50 hrs per month, so there is a generous amount of flying time to schedule. Scheduling is managed through the Flight Schedule Pro app. 

Please feel free to call or email for more information. Flying club bylaws and rates available on request. Happy Flying!
