name: Hostess City Aviators, Inc.
description: The Hostess City Aviators, Inc. (HCA) is a not-for-profit, equity-based flying club that facilitates the ownership and operation of well-maintained aircraft by passionate aviators who wish to exercise their pilot certifications in a safe and cost-effective manner. The Hostess City Aviators, Inc. also takes special interest in energizing grassroots flying in the Savannah, GA region and exposing Gulfstream Aerospace employees to the general aviation environment in order to supplement their technical knowledge with operational experience.

title: The 150th Aero Flying Club, Inc.
name: The 150th Aero Flying Club, Inc.
description: The 150th Aero Flying Club was formed in 1960 by a group of light plane fliers associated with the 150th Air National Guard, thus the origin of the name. The Club now has no connection whatsoever with the Air National Guard. Until 1969, the Club was located at Hanover Airport in Hanover, NJ. It is now based at Morristown Municipal Airport in Morristown, NJ. Club Aircraft are currently located at KMMU and KSMQ.  It is a member-owned, not-for-profit club.

title: Orlando Aviators Flying Club, Inc.
name: Orlando Aviators Flying Club, Inc.
description:
Orlando Aviators Flying Club allows certified pilots and student pilots access to aircraft at Orlando Executive Airport (KORL) for very reasonable hourly rates. We have four very clean and well-maintained airplanes: a 1983 Cessna 172P, a 1973 PA-28-180 Archer, a 1982 PA-28-181 Archer, and an Alarus CH-2000. Our club has two side-by-side shade hangars, room for four airplanes and our portable office.
 
We are currently seeking a more airplanes for the club. You can check out our airplanes here. We are always looking to add the right airplane to the club. Interested in putting an airplane in service with us? Please contact us.
 
OAFC has more than 90 members of all ages and backgrounds.  The club members range from airline/corporate pilots, commercial multiengine pilots, private and instrument rated pilots, flight instructors, and student pilots.  We have six members who are independent Certified Flight Instructors (CFIs) and are available for all of your training questions and needs. Meet all of these instructors in the “Instruction” section of the website. Our instructors may be available to help you with your Private, Instrument, and Commercial training needs. 
 
In addition to flying, we also find the club to be a great way to meet and socialize with other pilots. We encourage participation in club events as well as local FAA sponsored seminars.
 
Contact us anytime to find out more about area flying and how to get started. No matter what your intentions, business or pleasure, we can help you find the right way to become a pilot

title: Bemidji Flying Club
name: Bemidji Flying Club
description: Our goal is simply to get people flying and keep them flying.  And providing both excellent aircraft and a safe, yet fun atmosphere. Bemidji, a lake community with an area population of 40,000, is uniquely located in a region with a rich aviation history. Bemidji is home to AirCorps Aviation, the premier WWII Aircraft restoration company in the United States and Bemidji Aviation an employee owned Freight, FBO, and Charter Service company that was founded in 1947. To the East we have both the headquarters and manufacturing of Cirrus and Kestrel aircraft. To the West we have the University of North Dakota home to the John D Odegard School of Aerospace Sciences which trains pilots, air traffic controllers, space studies, and both computer and atmospheric sciences.

- One C172 & one C182 have recent paint and leather interior.

Our club formed as a result of the joining together of the Birmingham Soaring Society and Sylacauga Soaring Society.

Come and join us at the Sylacauga Airport, a truly great venue for soaring. We operate mostly off the grass between a 5000' runway and the adjacent taxiway.

title: Tradewind Aero Club
name: Tradewind Aero Club
description: The TAC is a group of pilots and student pilots (called members) to be registered with Tradewind Aviation International LLC (TAI), based at Coastal Carolina Regional Airport in New Bern, NC. The TAC offers special conditions for services rendered by TAI. This enables the members to rent and fly well-maintained aircraft for a discounted rate, and to receive instruction.

title: Emporia Flying Club
name: Emporia Flying Club
description:
Providing Accessible & Affordable Flying to the Emporia Area

Our mission is to provide members with a safe, clean, well-equipped airplane at the most economical rates possible.

To join the corporation, you must buy a share of stock for $600 which is refunded when you resign from the corporation in good standing. New members also pay a $60 non-refundable processing fee. Monthly dues are $75.

There are corporation-approved flight instructors available for instruction at various levels of training including a private pilot’s license and a instrument rating. The cost of obtaining a private pilot’s license is dependent on individual ability but will usually total between $4,000 and $5,500.

If you would like to inquire about joining our club, you may E-Mail the Vice President or call him at 620-366-2849 and he will be glad to assist you!

title: River City Aero Club
name: River City Aero Club
description:
River City Aero Club was founded by friends who wanted to make flying more affordable. We still live by the "flying, friends, fun" motto and are looking for new friends to share our passion. If you’re a certificated pilot, current or not, you have easy access to two IFR-certified aircraft that let you choose the one best suited to your mission - adding a rating, $100 hamburger, or serious XC travel.
- 1965 Cessna 172G (N14KM) - GNS530W, TruTrak Vizion autopilot, ADS-B in/out, more - $60/hour
- 1980 Cessna 182Q (N5209N) - GTN650W, S-Tek 50 autopilot, ADS-B in/out, more - $110/hour

$1,000 buy-in and $175 a month is all it takes. What are you waiting for? 

Contact us for details.

title: LeMay Flight Training Center (Offutt Aero Club)
name: LeMay Flight Training Center (Offutt Aero Club)
description: The Offutt Aero Club, now named the LeMay Flight Training Center, was the first flying club in the Armed Forces. The club provides aircraft rental and is also an FAA-approved school for Private Pilot through Airline Transport Pilot certification. The club has several aircraft, ranging from basic single engine types to multi-engine. Nearly all aircraft are certified for instrument flying. Several FAA-certified flight instructors are avail­able and flight instruction is tailored to meet the needs of the members. TDYs and shiftwork schedules can be accommodated. The Aero Club stocks pilot supplies at a discount for members.

title: Hillsboro Flying Club
name: Hillsboro Flying Club
description:
Welcome to the Hillsboro Flying Club.

The Hillsboro Flying Club is a member-owned and operated, not-for-profit organization run by volunteers who love to fly. We are based out of the Portland-Hillsboro (HIO) airport, in Hillsboro Oregon. Member involvement at all levels helps to keep rates low and ensures that the aircraft are clean, well-maintained and carrying the equipment that members want. We own and operate 3 well equipped aircraft. A 1981 Cessna 172, 1975 Cessna 182, and a 1980 Piper Saratoga. Our 182 has dual G5's and a GFC-500 autopilot. The Saratoga has an amazing all glass cockpit with Dual G3X's, GTN 750xi, GFC-500 autopilot, 6 seats and a useful load of almost 1500 lbs. All of our airplanes are IFR equipped. Your membership includes liability insurance. Our rates and plane availability is much better than local FBO's. If you are looking to be part of a fun group of pilots and be able to expand your flying abilities then please reach out to us.

Some members have been in the club for over 30 years! The club continues to provide a safe, convenient, and economical means of flying. The club is set up as a non-profit corporation which provides a more organized and easier membership structure. This allows pilots to become members for less money than most clubs and provides for more organized club decision making. 

We have 3 active mechanics in our club.  The planes are well maintained and we have never had any safety issues with the aircraft.

name: Connecticut Valley Flyers
description:
The Connecticut Valley Flyers is a flying club based at Brainard Airport, in Hartford, CT (KHFD). 15 members together own N46511, a 1969 Cessna 172K Skyhawk with a 180hp/constant speed conversion. Our members range from recent private pilots to instructors and ATP's with decades and thousands of hours experience.

We schedule N46511 online with www.AircraftClubs.com, which has worked out very well. Backup reservations are also welcome. Most flights are for a few hours, but occassionally we'll have a multi-day trip planned.

History: The previous owner (in the early 1970's) did the 180 hp constant speed conversion, and we bought the plane soon after. Several years ago '511 was refurbished with a leather interior and new paint. She looks and flies great! Plan on travelling at 130mph at 9.5 gph in cruise, with a 2-3/4 hour range and 1 hr reserve.  In 2020, the Lycoming 180 hp engine was overhauled with a Pen Yan Super Hawk conversion.

title: Sky-Hi Flying Club (Since 1972)
name: Sky-Hi Flying Club (Since 1972)
description:
Celebrating our 50th Anniversary in 2022

Sky-Hi, Incorporated was originally formed in February, 1972 by a group of 9 flying enthusiasts who worked together at AT&T. Their goal was to create a social flying club that allowed them to pursue a flying license and additional ratings at economical rates, and to utilize the aircraft for pleasure and personal vacations.
 
The club's first airplane, a 1968 Cessna Skyhawk (N35540) was originally delivered from the Wichita, Kansas Cessna factory to a gentleman in East Williston, New York in June of 1968. Since then, an original aircraft bill of sale indicates that Sky-Hi, Inc. obtained the 172I Skyhawk on February 19, 1972 from an aircraft broker in Port Washington, NY. The amount of the purchase was $9,950, and the aircraft had been based at Frederick Municipal Airport (FDK) for over 36 years until a student pilot lost control during landing on November 27, 2008 resulting in extensive damage to the airplane. After the insurance company determined the airplane was a total loss, the club purchased a 1977 Cessna Cardinal (N19783) on January 25, 2009 from the Sarasota WestWind Flyers based at the Sarasota/Bradenton International Airport (SRQ) Florida.

To date, there have been a total of 90 members ranging from student, military and commercial airline pilots to flight engineers and air traffic controllers. Their unique backgrounds have created a rich history for Sky-Hi that continues to be guided in the spirit of the original founding members nearly 50 years ago.

For more information, or to fill out an application, send an email to the club president at the email address listed above.

title: Harrison Social Flites Flying Club
name: Harrison Social Flites Flying Club
description:
As a members owned and operated corporation, each member is a fractional owner of the club's aircraft. Additionally, as a non-profit organization, we operate the Club on the basis of actual operating costs; this allows our members to fly comfortable and well maintained aircraft at very affordable hourly rates.  Fixed costs, such as hangar fees, insurance, and annual inspections, are shared costs amongst all members. Sharing these expenses is what gives flying clubs their financial advantage. Additionally, since insurance is covered by our shared expenses, members are relieved from purchasing individual aircraft rental insurance.

The club is currently at capacity but is building a waitlist and discussing purchasing a second airplane, which would open up membership slots. So please stop by one our monthly meetings, 1st Wednesday every month at I67, to discuss the future of our great flying club.

With flying costs between $50-$90 per hour wet and monthly dues at $25. The club started with a J-2 Taylor Cub and a J-3 Piper Cub that rented for $2 per hour wet. name: Yellowstone Flying Club
description:
We're growing!  YFC was founded in 1997 and has been in continuous operation as an equity Club ever since. We have a Piper Saratoga SP and have recently added a Cessna 172  and an IFR Cessna 182!  Memberships are currently available.  

Our "Tier 1" membership level provides access to both the C-172 & C-182.

Monthly Dues are $100 and include anticipated expenses for Annual Inspection, Routine Maintenance, Insurance and Hangar.

Our "Tier 2" membership level provides access to our Saratoga SP.
Tier 2 Buy-In is currently $21,667, with a maximum of 6 members.

title: Skyhaven Flying Club, Inc
name: Skyhaven Flying Club, Inc
description:
Founded in 1936 as University of New Hampshire Flying Club, Skyhaven Flying Club is a not-for-profit club based at Skyhaven Airport in Rochester, New Hampshire (KDAW).

The club is comprised of a wide variety of members from new Private Pilots to CFI's. Our membership includes aircraft mechanics, flight instructors, Private, Commercial and Airline Transport Pilots, holding nearly every imaginable endorsement. Our members are unified by a common desire to continuously learn about aviation, to do it in a safe and fun manner and to pass the knowledge they possess to future generations of aviators.

Members currently enjoy two aircraft; a Cessna 172 which is IFR certified and equipped with Garmin GNS 430W (WAAS) avionics and a Cirrus SR20-G2 GTS, equipped with dual GNS 430W and Avidyne avionics. The Cirrus was added in 2015.

A FlyThisSim TouchTrainer Simulator is available for members by subscription. It can be configured to represent either a Cessna 172 or Cirrus SR20-G2 (Avidyne) panel and controls. 
Additional details: http://skyhavenflyingclub.org/simulator/

January 2017: Applications are always accepted and encouraged. Unfortunately, we cannot offer memberships or training to Student Pilots at this time. 

Membership details: http://skyhavenflyingclub.org/

Our RV-12 is an excellent platform for local flights and moderate cross countries. It can carry two full size adults, bags and full fuel while cruising at 120+ knots true airspeed for 3 hours with a respectable reserve.

We are excited to share our passion for aviation with you. Get in touch with us through our Contact Us form for more information on joining.

Mike Phillips 314-495-3264 mikeph0001@gmail.com

title: Ann Arbor Flyers
name: Ann Arbor Flyers
description: We’re a non-profit club dedicated to making flying accessible to everyone. As a member, enjoy partial ownership of our advanced fleet through a fully refundable equity purchase, maintaining a 15-to-1 member-to-aircraft ratio. We’re serious about taking full advantage of the ability to fly. Club scheduling rules are very flexible, and we encourage cross-county trips with no minimum hours and extended reservation lengths. We are one of the only clubs with 6-place aircraft - yes you can take your whole family flying, with enough fuel to get to your destination!

title: Air-Spacers Flying Club
name: Air-Spacers Flying Club
description:
This is Air-Spacers Flying Club @ KSMO. We are a community of pilots of all kinds and experience - from students to airline pilots.

Our membership is capped at 65 members. We are always happy to welcome contact or applications from pilots who are interested in joining our club. We do have a wait list at the moment, but with 65 members there is regular movement in and out of the club.

We are an equity ownership club and upon joining you will be a part owner of our 5 exceptional aircraft. We have a modern fleet including a Cessna 172M, Cessna 172S with dual GI-275s, Diamond DA40-180 with PowerFlow exhaust, Cessna 182P with a GFC500 autopilot and dual G5s, and a G3 SR20 with G1000. We also have an incredible performer - a Cirrus SR22 on leaseback at an attractive dry rate!

Membership in our club comes with a load of privileges that provides a completely different experience from just renting. We do not have minimum charges and our rates are significantly less expensive than occasionally renting from an FBO. You'll get a gate key - so you can simply drive up to your aircraft and go! If you decide to leave the club, you can have the club sell your membership for a small fee or find somebody on your own at no expense to you.

We have a Cessna 172 that is certified for IFR Flight.

It is kept at Dooney Aviation at KWST.

We are a non-profit club of flying enthusiasts that strive to keep flying affordable. Our Club can accommodate a maximum of 25 members but we average 19 members. 

To join, there is a $250 non-refundable initiation fee, a $500 refundable share deposit, and the first months dues ($80) and special assessment of $20. Totaling $850.

The monthly special assessment of $20/month per member is part of our capital fund towards capital projects e.g. MoH, aircraft replacement...

We meet the third Thursday of every other month (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, & Nov). The meetings are held at Dooney Aviation in Westerly, RI.

Come join us!

title: Connecticut Flight Club, Inc.
name: Connecticut Flight Club, Inc.
description:
NEW ENGLAND’S FASTEST GROWING FLIGHT CLUB

The mission of Connecticut Flight Club is to grow general aviation. We strive to do this through education, training, safety, fellowship, and perhaps most importantly: low-cost recreational flying.

The club always maintains a ratio of 20 members per aircraft or better, meaning that aircraft availability is never a concern. Once per year, you can even take an aircraft on vacation for two weeks! Wet hourly aircraft rates ensure you always know what to expect.

Our home field is Hartford-Brainard Airport. Nestled on the bank the Connecticut River, Brainard is a great jumping-off point for many popular New England destinations. Hop over to Montauk or Cape Cod for a bite of seafood. Spend a warm summer’s day at Block Island without the hassle of the ferry. Tour the New York City skyline down the Hudson River. Head up north and peep the autumn leaves. It’s up to you, PIC!

title: Legacy Flying Club, Inc

description:
Legacy Flying Club Mission Statement
 
The purpose of the club is to promote safe, enjoyable flying and aviation-related activities, and to provide the opportunity for its members to fly aircraft economically and conveniently in a non-profit organization. 

The Club will provide a comfortable, collegial flying environment for interested pilots in order to promote the dissemination of safe habits and an open dialogue for the free exchange of experience and knowledge. Open communication will promote safe operations and goal-directed learning. This collegial atmosphere shall also promote basic as well as advanced training.
 
The Club will provide affordable, clean, well-maintained aircraft for the club members' use. As safety is a priority all maintenance concerns will be addressed in a prompt fashion.
 
The Club will promote the joy of flying to the community by being an organization with a special focus on safety and proficiency.

title: Low Flying Angels
name: Low Flying Angels
description:
The Low Flying Angels is a Sacramento-based flying club that was established in 1966 as a not-for-profit Corporation. It is comprised of 12 shareholders, each who own an equal share in the club’s 1978 Cessna 172 Skyhawk II (C172N). The aircraft is IFR certified and is equipped with ILS, dual NAVCOMS, dual G5s and a Garmin GNX 375 IFR certified WAAS GPS. It is based at KMHR in Rancho Cordova and reserved for use by shareholders via an online calendar.

Shareholders and the club's Board of Directors comprised of a President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Flight Director meet quarterly to discuss club finances, aircraft maintenance, safety, and to make decisions concerning the club’s aircraft and corporate by-laws.

To be eligible to own a share, you must be a current, licensed pilot with a minimum of 100 hours of PIC time. Our club has a maximum of 12 shareholders, each who has the right to own their share for life, but may choose to sell their share at any time, at any price, to an eligible purchaser.  While we have no visibility to when a share may come up for sale, we historically have had one to two transactions per year. Shareholders pay monthly dues, which cover fixed costs and an hourly (wet) use fee. The use fee covers the cost of fuel and is used to replenish the club’s maintenance fund, a portion of which is held in reserve for engine and propeller replacement. Monthly dues are currently set at $230 and the hourly use fee is set at $145.

We toggle the "Memberships Currently Available" flag on if we have a current share for sale, and we toggle it off if there are no current shares available. If there are no shares currently available, eligible, interested pilots may contact us to join our waiting list. We do allow a small number of interested parties to place a fully-refundable $2500 deposit with us to get priority placement on that waitlist if they desire. Recent share sales have transacted for ~$15,000/share.

title: Newton Flying Club
name: Newton Flying Club
description:
Newton Flying Club located at M23 James H Easom Field Airport  

We have a Piper PA-28-180 Challenger IFR certified.
 
To join the club as a Licensed pilot the Club BUY in fee is $500.00. All Licensed pilot members will pay $200.00 per month member dues.  The monthly dues include 2.5 hours of of flying time each month.  If you fly for MORE than 2.5 hours the hourly rate is $60.00 dry. (For example you fly 3.5 hours in a month your bill for that month would be $260.00).

Student pilot monthly dues are $50 per month. in addition to the student dues Flying time is billed at a rate of $60.00 per hour dry. 

Also, as a pilot or a student pilot you will be insured by the clubs insurance policy for accidents in the club plane. There is no additional cost to you for this coverage. A copy of the policy can be provided for your review upon request. 

For more information about being a pilot or student pilot call Rob (CFI) 601-917-0533 or Michael 601-616-5553, email (newtonflying@gmail.com), or text for details. The club uses use's Google calendar to do our scheduling.

title: Connecticut Soaring Association
name: Connecticut Soaring Association
description: Membership provides free instruction and use of the club trainer.

title: Riverside Pilots Flying Club, Inc
name: Riverside Pilots Flying Club, Inc
description:
Riverside Pilots is a Southern California based Non-Profit Flying Club at Riverside Municipal Airport (KRAL).  We are not owned or affiliated with any FBO.  For over 40 years, we have been providing our members with safe and affordable flying with our fleet of three airplanes.  Aircraft are hangered in the 'G' hanger building with private bathroom facilities.  Club meetings are the second Monday of each month at 6:30 PM in the hanger and prospective members are welcomed to join.  

Please visit our website, www.riversidepilotsflyingclub.com for more information on membership and current aircraft rates.

We currently have a Cessna 182RG.   We are considering the addition of a Cessna 172 for students and pilots not needing the cross country and IFR capabilities of the C182RG.

Two of our members are flight instructors.

The aircraft is based at the local FBO, Tri-State Aero, Inc.  We have monthly business meetings and quarterly social events.

title: Ascension Air
name: Ascension Air
description:
Ascension Air is the fastest growing Cirrus Fractional Ownership and Leasing program in the U.S. And for good reason. CNBC, BusinessWeek, and Inc. Magazine are just a few of the respected sources that have recognized Ascension Air for revolutionizing aircraft ownership. And Cirrus Aircraft has awarded us a designation as an Official Partner for Fractional Ownership.
 
Our innovative approach enables us to offer unprecedented availability to a fleet of brand new, optimally-equipped aircraft for a price comparable to sole ownership of a 30-year-old airplane. But that’s only part of what makes us unique. We impeccably maintain the largest fleet of identical turbocharged Cirrus SR22T GTS aircraft in the southeast to give our owners the best access and the best flying experience. And Ascension Air’s Concierge Service is the only one of its kind anywhere. Our staff cleans, preps and even outfits each aircraft with the owner’s personal pilot supplies before each flight. We make hotel and rental car reservations at the owner’s destination and greet the owner inside a warm, dry hangar for the preflight inspection.
 
Is it any wonder we have become the number one personally flown fractional program in the Southeast so quickly? We are currently expanding into other markets, and are well on our way to becoming the number one personally-flown fractional and leasing program in the country.

title: Upper Fifteen Flying Club
name: Upper Fifteen Flying Club
description:
The club has a well equipped 1998 Cessna 182S Skylane N9570A. A solid IFR platorm, it has Aspen glass, Garmin GTN750 with flight stream bluetooth connectivity, ADS-B in/out, and JPI EDM-700 engine monitor. There is excellent availability, and we are accepting new members. With an average of 6 members, this club is like ownership without the cost and hassle.

The plane is hangared at the Albany International Airport.  We have gas tug, and an electric engine preheater for the plane.  

The club charges a wet rate by tach time, and scheduling is done online. 

Upper Fifteen is the oldest flying club in New York State and one of the oldest in the United States. Founded in 1948 as the Siena Flying Club, Upper-Fifteen today provides an opportunity to share a well-equipped Skylane while sharing experiences with other local pilots who love recreational flying. Scheduling policies are liberal and flexible.

title: Key City Fliers
name: Key City Fliers
description:
Key City Fliers was founded in 1960 by a group of three pilots who purchased a Taylorcraft. Since that time, we have owned a variety of aircraft to meet the needs of our members. Currently, our fleet consists of a Piper Cherokee 140/160, Piper Archer, and Piper Dakota. 
Our members include Student Pilots, Private Pilots, Commercial Pilots, ATP's, CFI's and CFII's.

Our mission is to deliver safe access to light aircraft for our members at an affordable rate.

title: Fort Smith Flying Club
name: Fort Smith Flying Club
description:
Fort Smith Flying Club INC. (FSFC) is a non-profit organization created to promote flying and flight training in the Arkansas River Valley region. Pilots and student pilots alike are invited to join. Membership is open to any person who meets the eligibility requirements, subject to approval by current club membership. 

Members may use club approved instructors for initial flight training and advanced ratings.

title: EnginAires Aero Club
name: EnginAires Aero Club
description:
Sub-S Corp club in existence since 1950s.  Based at Flightstar, at KCMI, University of Illinois WIllard Airport.

We have two airplanes for our members' use. One is a late 1970s Piper Archer II with Garmin GTN 650 and autopilot. Second is a mid-1970s Cessna 182, also with GTN 650, autopilot with altitude hold, and a new (2020) three-blade propeller.  

Purchase one of 20 shares from another member at a privately negotiated price or from the club at a stated price.  A member desiring to leave the club can have the club buy back the member's share after one year's notice (at a specified, discounted price).  

Monthly dues cover hangars, insurance, annual inspections, and miscellaneous expenses.  
Tach hour flying charges cover nearly everything else, including fuel, oil changes, contribution to engine and prop overhaul reserves, and repairs. 

We try to price to break even.  
We try to have funds available in reserve for expected big expenses. Thus, when the time comes for an overhaul, the pilots who flew off the old engine have contributed enough to buy a new engine.

title: Upper Valley Flying Club
name: Upper Valley Flying Club

title: Western Flying Club
name: Western Flying Club
description:
The Western Flying Club is a not for profit, member-owned corporation consisting of 30 members who are devoted to flying and maintaining our 3 beautiful aircraft.  Based out of Burlington, NC (KBUY), our members enjoy the geographical benefits of being close to coastal and mountain destinations.  We also have the benefit of CFI members for your training needs. 

Our current aircraft fleet consists of a Beechcraft A36  Bonanza, a Piper PA28 Archer, and a Cessna C182.  These aircraft are all IFR equipped and well maintained. 

Please take a look at our aircraft and contact us for any questions or membership information via our webpage form.

title: Gville Flyers, LLC
name: Gville Flyers, LLC
description:
Gville Flyers is a non-profit flying club in Gainesville, FL, based at Gainesville Regional Airport (KGNV).

Our mission is to build an aviation community where people become safer pilots, fly more economically, make lasting friendships, and share their passion for flying. We seek to make aviation inclusive and accessible to anyone who shares our passion for the sky.

We currently have one airplane and 10 members (our cap ), though we are exploring options to diversify our fleet and enlarge our community. We are an equity club, meaning that members own a share of the club and have pride of ownership in club aircraft. 

Members must hold at least a private pilot certificate. We are not a flight school, but we do encourage members to pursue advanced ratings and certificates as part of an ongoing commitment to become more capable, safer pilots. Our members include several active flight instructors and pilot mentors.

Our airplane, N971DS, is a 2006 Diamond DA40-180 with the Garmin G1000 avionics package and KAP140 autopilot.

We also host a monthly Hangar Hangout on the third Wednesday of each month. This event is open to the whole GA community; you do not need to be a member to attend. At each Hangout, a club CFI presents a safety seminar, which qualifies for credit in the FAA WINGS Pilot Proficiency Program.

Please visit gvilleflyers.org to learn more.

title: 51st Aero Squadron, LLC
name: 51st Aero Squadron, LLC
description: We started our Club in March of 2013 and are located on Mitchell Field in Bessemer, AL (KEKY). The club is comprised of pilots of various experience levels including student pilots, private pilots, commercial pilots and retired airline pilots.  As of December 2023, we operate 3 Piper Archers and a Piper Arrow II. All of our aircraft are IFR equipped and certified.  Two of our Archers and our Arrow II have dual Garmin G5 electronic flight instruments coupled to a Garmin GFC500 auto pilot. During 2024 we expect to upgrade our remaining Archer to this equipment level.  All aircraft are individually hangared and are available 24 hours per day.

title: Skyhawk Flying Club Inc
name: Skyhawk Flying Club Inc
description:
Club is a Shareholder membership, this cost is based on club ASSETS and number of share holders.
Dues based on fixed cost.
Rental rate set to cover Fuel cost and normal fuel consumption and per hour cost of maintenance schedule for service requirements.
1996 Piper PA28-181 Archer III - (2) Garmin GPS 430 & 530, Sandel HSI,

title: Eximious Flying Club
name: Eximious Flying Club
description:
Our club has one very clean Archer II, IFR-capable with a Garmin 430W, based in hangar 9M at Coleman A. Young Municipal Airport (KDET), and part-time at Ray Community Airport (57D).  

We also have one Commander 114 based in hangar D5 at Oakland-Troy Airport (KVLL).  The Commander is a high-performance, retractable-gear aircraft, capable of cruising at 155 knots.  It is the only flying club-owned C114 in North America.

Please go to our website for lots more information and photos (eximiousflyingclub.com).

title: Mohawk Flying Club
name: Mohawk Flying Club
description:
The Mohawk Flying Club is a member-owned, non-profit flying club in continuous operation since 1959 with four (4) aircraft all hangared at the Gerald R. Ford International Airport (GRR):  1975 Cessna 172M,  1971 Cessna 172L (180hp + long range), 1977 Cessna 182Q (long range),  2010 Cirrus SR20-G3 GTS.     

Becoming a member of the Mohawk Club provides the following benefits:

   - Safe, well-maintained aircraft with good availability
   - Online scheduling
   - No overnight minimums
   - Advanced Garmin avionics (GTN650(2), GNX375, and Cirrus Perspective G1000 all with Garmin Connext)
   - Digital autopilots (three aircraft)
   - ADS-B in/out with weather and traffic displays & callouts
   - Insurance and engine reserves included in wet rates
   - Active membership
   - Maintenance officer takes care of all maintenance
   - President and Treasurer take care of licensing and financial issues

All you need to do is FLY!

title: LGE Flying Club
name: LGE Flying Club
description: For more than sixty years, the LGE Flying Club has made flying less expensive, more convenient, less hassle, and more fun for generations of Lockheed Martin employees, their immediate family and retirees. At the end of 2012 Lockheed required that the club separate and operate as an independent club. Our airplanes are conveniently located at Cobb County- McCollum Airport. Check out the many benefits your membership provides.

title: Club Cherokee
name: Club Cherokee
description: Membership is open to students and experienced pilots alike. Club Cherokee is structured as a non-profit corporation, where each member owns one share of corporate stock. Each member is an equal partner in the Club, and has equal input in how the Club is run. A Board of Directors is elected each year and represents Club members in all decisions and policy making. This equal share value allows individuals to experience flying without a long-term financial commitment, such as purchasing an aircraft privately. Club Cherokee maintains a low member-per-airplane ratio, making it easy to schedule a plane through our web-based scheduling system.

name: Brockton Flying Club
description: Each share provides for 1/10 ownership of club plane and assets, including a hangar. Club is limited to 10 members. We currently own an IFR-rated 1979 C-172N with 180hp upgrade, Garmin 430W and GTX-345 ADS-B with Bluetooth connectivity.

title: Wing Nuts Flying Club, LLC
name: Wing Nuts Flying Club, LLC
description: The Wingnuts Flying club was formed in 1980 by 4 members and a C150.  Now we are 51 strong with a C172, and a Columbia 350 (glass).   We are currently flipping our fleet and just sold our Diamond DA40.  We are in the process of buying a Tecnam P2010.   We meet on the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays each month at 7pm in the Boardroom upstairs in the main terminal of KFCI.  We have a program at the end of each meeting about a variety of aviation interests.  There are a handful of memberships available for purchase as a share of stock.  Visit our website:  wingnutsflying.org

title: Yale Aviation, Inc
name: Yale Aviation, Inc
description: Yale Aviation, Inc has been a flying club for more than 100 years. Currently incorporated within the state of Connecticut, it provides its members with access to a Piper Cherokee and a TAA Piper Archer in pursuit of its mission to promote education in aviation.

title: Naperville Flying Club
name: Naperville Flying Club
description: Naperville Flying Club is a well-established flying club based at Naper Aero Club Airport. The club, which has existed since 1958, has always prided itself on having multiple aircraft available. The current fleet includes a Cessna 172, Piper Archer, Beechcraft Debonair, and a Piper Saratoga and are all GPS and IFR-equipped. That variety allows for activities that range from training and burger runs to long cross country flights. Each club member is an equity owner of the airplanes, and membership is capped at 50 members, several of whom have been with the club for many years. Because the members own the aircraft, dues and rates are set to cover expenses rather than make a profit, maintaining NFC's rates among the lowest in the area. Ultimately, what holds the club together is the camaraderie of membership, and we seek members who wish to be long time contriutors to the club. One of the best ways to get an introduction is at a monthly club meeting held on the first Thursday of the month which is held as a hybrid in-person and virtual meeting. More club information, including aircraft photos, membership details, and contact information can be found at www.napervilleflyingclub.com.

title: Wesley Flyers Inc
name: Wesley Flyers Inc
description: Wesley Flyers is a  member owned non-profit LLC operating two Cessna aircraft out of KMBO in Madison, MS. N734AE is a Skyhawk 172N (180HP conversion), N735FC is a Skylane 182Q and N6245S is a Skylane 182RG. Our membership is currently full but we do occasionally have existing memberships for sale. Please inquire if interested. We accept pilots from student to instrument rated and commercial. Our insurance requirements are unique to each plane and will require a CFI sign-off, but students may fly and even conduct their private checkride in the 172. The 182RG requires a Private Pilot license with 100 hours minimum total time and 10 hours in make and model along with complex and high performance endorsements. A resellable equity share in the club costs $6,000. There is also a 172 only membership for $3,500 which can be upgraded. Our monthly dues are $185 for full memberships and $140 for 172 only. Our current wet rates are $90/hr for the 172N and $140/hr for the 182Q and 182RG. Visit our website at: http://www.wesleyflyers.com/

title: Smoke Eagles
name: Smoke Eagles
description:
Smoke Eagles is a non-profit flying club that has been in existence for over seventy years! It was registered as a California corporation in 1954 and is managed by board of five annually elected members.

We have two aircraft (172, 182) and limit our membership to 30. Membership is not open to student pilots, but they may apply in anticipation of becoming private pilots.

Our buy-in and fees are evaluated yearly and adjusted if necessary. Dues cover all fixed costs, and the hourly rate covers all flight related costs. Reserves are established for anticipated future known expenditures such as paint, upholstery, avionics, etc.

We own both aircraft and have cash on-hand for maintenance, annuals, and overhauls. Our aircraft are ADS-B In/Out with GNS 530 and GTN 650, paired with GTX345.

Buy-in fee is refundable in full upon leaving the club.

We have no daily minimums and use TACH time for hourly billing. We have an on-line scheduling system. Members are issued aircraft keys and have 24 hour access. 

Smoke Eagles meets virtually (Zoom) on the first Thursday (2nd if a holiday) of each month at 7 PM. Guests are always welcome. Send an email for the Zoom link 24 hours prior.

A wait list is maintained for potential members. Our website (https://www.smokeeagles.com/) provides more information and an inquiry form that when completed will result in a response email with club details and costs, bylaws, flight regulations, and a link to our application form. Completing the application form will place you on our waitlist. There is no cost to be placed on our waitlist and no obligation to join when invited to do so.

We are on facebook at
 https://www.facebook.com/SmokeEagles

and on the web at
www.Smokeeagles.com



Come check us out.

title: Salem Aero Club
name: Salem Aero Club
description:
Salem Aero Club has helped pilots and those aspiring to be pilots since 1965. Active Club membership offers an affordable opportunity for students and certified pilots to enjoy the freedom of flight and convenience of aircraft ownership through cost sharing with fellow members.   

The Club currently owns a Cessna 150 for building time and inexpensive fun flying, and an IFR equipped Cessna 182 for more serious skill building and personal travel. 

We hold monthly meetings to keep everyone informed on Club activities, finances, maintenance of aircraft, and new membership applicants. Our meetings are open for interested pilots or nonpilots to learn more about Salem Aero Club and the membership application process. We currently have open membership. For more detailed information about Salem Aero Club and our planes go to SALEMAEROCLUB.COM.

title: Twinco Flying Club
name: Twinco Flying Club
description: Is the high cost of flying preventing you from flying as often as you want to? Twinco Flying Club has a Cessna 172 available to our members at $85/Hr dry where members pay for fuel upon returning from flight, monthly dues are only $85/ month and there is a one time $1800 buy in fee of which $1700 is returned to you when you leave the club, subject to club bylaws. Membership is capped at 25, so aircraft availability is always great. Twinco currently is accepting membership applications. If you're a current pilot and interested in joining, please contact us for more information.  Our website:    www.twinco.club

title: Bloomsburg Flying Club
name: Bloomsburg Flying Club
description:
Founded in 1964 and based at N13 in Bloomsburg, PA. We are a non-profit, non-equity club. 

We own a 1998 Cessna 172R that is IFR equipped with a Garmin GTN650 including ADS-B and single axis autopilot and a 
1983 Piper Dakota that is IFR equipped with Gamin 530 WAAS, dual G5s, ADS-B, and dual axis autopilot. 

Our current rates are $150 per hour (wet) for our 172R and $180 per hour (wet) for our Dakota. 

Monthly dues are $80.00. Our initiation fee is only $1200.00.

We accept certificated pilots only, no students.

Applications can be found on our website at flybloomsburg.com.

title: Adrian Soaring Club

description: ASC is a non-profit club focused on teaching new glider pilots.  All glider instruction is FREE to club members & provided by our member CFIG's - you pay only the glider & tow cost like all members.

description:
Air Tech is a 7 member, equity-based flying club based in Richmond, VA at Hanover County Airport (OFP).  We own N63PV, a 1994 Piper Saratoga HP II. Internet Based Scheduling !

As a member managed flying club, we take safe flying seriously and make sure that our aircraft is well equipped, well maintained and ready to go at all times.  Our mission is to make sure that N63PV offers high quality cross country performance and safety at a reasonable price.

title: Eagle Squadron, Inc
name: Eagle Squadron, Inc
description:
Eagle Squadron was created in 1984 as a shared aircraft ownership comprised of individual stockholders, interested in sharing the cost of aircraft ownership. Our strategy is simple, make owning and flying well maintained and upgraded aircraft more affordable through shared ownership.

When you own an aircraft individually, you have all the costs of a loan, hangar, insurance, subscriptions, annual inspection, and those unscheduled maintenance issues.

When you rent an aircraft from a local FBO, you get well used, dirty aircraft that everyone abuses with minimum hour requirements for weekend getaways that turn a 2 hour trip into a 9 hour hit on your wallet.

The solution? Shared aircraft ownership. Eagle Squadron has three aircraft based out of Tampa Executive (KVDF). When you join a partnership, you split fixed costs between multiple individuals, AND get access to multiple well maintained and upgraded aircraft. When you fly, you pay the variable costs of your flight time only. Dividing the fixed expenses among multiple members makes flying much more affordable.

Benefits of shared aircraft ownership:
•	Much cheaper than owning an aircraft individually
•	Access to multiple aircraft
•	Higher quality aircraft than your local FBO
•	Hangared aircraft, flown by owners, not renters
•	No overnight minimums
•	On-line scheduling

title: Hill Flying Club
name: Hill Flying Club
description:
Welcome to the Hill Flying Club. Located in the heart of Northern Utah along the Wasatch Mountain range, the Hill Flying Club (HFC) is based out of the Ogden Hinckley Airport (KOGD). We fly and maintain two Cessna 172's and a Cessna 182, which are owned and operated 100% by our owners. 
HFC was incorporated in 1964 and has been in continuous operation for over 45 years. 

Our goal is to provide safe and affordable flying to all of our pilots. Memberships are available for $3,500.00. $200 of which is refunded upon leaving the club. Memberships can not be sold. 

Monthly member dues are $44.00 per month. Our aircraft rates fluctuate depending on which aircraft you wish to fly and their capabilities. 

Aircraft are available 24 hours a day and are scheduled online or via any touch tone phone toll free.

If you have any questions, please contact Carey Stricker or visit our website http://www.hillflyingclub.com 

Sincerely, 
Carey Stricker 
Hill Flying Club

title: Arizona Flyers Club, Inc.
name: Arizona Flyers Club, Inc.
description: Arizona Flyers has been owned and operated by its members since the 1940s.  The club airplanes and hanger are conveniently located at Tucson International Airport. Our Flying Club is member owned and operated. Each member takes pride in the operation, maintenance, and general condition of the aircraft. Our goal is to economically provide affordable, safe, and convenient aircraft to our members. In addition, we hope to provide an environment where members may be able to stimulate their knowledge, increase their proficiency, and encourage a general interest in the world of aviation. We also take maximum advantage of living in Tucson and having three-day weekends to enjoy Colorado skiing, San Diego, Las Vegas, or The Grand Canyon, most of which are about 3 hours away in our club-owned C-182. Practice instrument work in our inexpensive C-172, or for longer flights, experience the comfort and performance of our Cessna 182RG.

title: Bell Ornithopters Flying Club Inc.
name: Bell Ornithopters Flying Club Inc.
description:
The Bell Ornithopters Flying Club, Inc. was established in September 1974 with employees from then Western Electric and Mountain Bell. Later that same year it was expanded to include all Bell System employees. With the break up of the Bell System the Club is now open to all AT&T, Avaya, Lucent Technologies, and Qwest employees, retired employees and family members. A limited number of special memberships have been extended to contract employees, past employees, and other persons that have a special interest in general aviation. The current membership is approximately 40 active pilots.

The Club owns two IFR equipped Cessna 172 aircraft which are hangared at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport (formerly JeffCo) northwest of Denver. Both upgraded with Garmin FGC 500 autopilots and two G5 instruments, removing the vacuum system.

The purpose of the Club, a nonprofit incorporated club with the State of Colorado, is to promote general aviation and provide low cost flying to Club members and their families.

title: Delaware Valley Aviation
name: Delaware Valley Aviation
description:
Delaware Valley Aviation is one of the oldest flying clubs in the United States, founded 1954.  

Our mission is safe, economical flying in attractive planes.  We own a 1979 Piper Archer II, a 1978 Piper Lance II, and a 1981 Piper Dakota -- all hangared at PNE Jet Center, IFR-equipped, and with coupled autopilots and WAAS-enabled GPS.    
              
Private pilot certificate required for membership.  (Sorry, we do not offer primary training.)   Photos and hourly costs at our web site,  phillyflyingclub.com (see link above).  Club instructors available to our members for advanced training  -- instruments, complex, high performance, etc.!

Northeast Philadelphia airport is convenient to pilots in southeastern Pennsylvania and South Jersey.                   

See  our web site (link above) for additional info.

title: Flywell Flying Club
name: Flywell Flying Club
description:
Flywell Flying Club, known as "Minnesota's Premier Flying Club", was chartered in 1963 as a non-profit social organization and it is the oldest flying club in Minnesota. Its conservative financial management has made them one of the most financially stable clubs in the state. Located at Anoka County Airport (KANE) it is approximately 20 miles north of Minneapolis under the KMSP Class B airspace.

All members are equal owners of four aircraft and a hangar.

title: SkyHawks, Inc.
name: SkyHawks, Inc.
