title: Westchester Flying Club
name: Westchester Flying Club
description:
The Westchester Flying Club provides safe, convenient and economical flying to its members, along with the social and educational benefits of spending time with like minded pilots. Our club is based at Westchester County Airport (HPN), NY.  The Club has been here since the 1960s and currently has approximately 80 members.  Our club is limited to 80 members.  As members go inactive, membership slots become available.

Meetings are held every 2nd Tuesday of each month at 8 pm at the Westchester Hilton and are open to both members and non-members. 

Our fleet includes:  2 V-Tail Bonanzas, 2 Piper Aeros, 2 Piper Archers, and 1 Cirrus SR-20.

title: Air Coeur Flying Club
name: Air Coeur Flying Club
description:
Partner (equity share):
M20C - $85/hr wet


Associate (non-equity member)
M20C - $130/hr wet


Monthly dues vary with membership - currently $115/mo.

title: Pocono Mountains Flying Club
name: Pocono Mountains Flying Club
description: Our mission is to make flying safe, fun and affordable. We have two Cessna 150s, three flight instructors and a great group of folks. We have group events and celebrate every member's accomplishments. We are based at KMPO, a great non-towered airport with two runways and are near both class C and D airspace.

title: Twin Cities Cloud 7
name: Twin Cities Cloud 7
description:
Based out of KFCM in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, Cloud 7 is one of the Twin Cities' premier flying organizations.  Our pilots share ownership and great flying memories in our fleet of six fully-equipped, well maintained Cessnas. Our member-owners range from student pilots working towards their private rating to commercial airline pilots, all with one thing in common: a shared passion for aviation.

We own two hangars at Flying Cloud field, complete with a heated maintenance hangar, and new club room. Our club room is equipped with television, wireless Internet access, and a computer with weather briefing access, flight planning and flight simulation software.

Cloud 7 instructors provide an excellent support resource for continuing knowledge and flight review for our pilots. Pilot social gatherings are also spread throughout the year, as a way to exchange stories and get to know other Cloud 7 member-owners.

title: York Travelers Inc
name: York Travelers Inc
description:
PENNSYLVANIA...York, Harrisburg, Lancaster. 
Based at N71 – Mt. Joy, PA / 

Incorporated in 1996 / 

*******1978 Grumman Tiger – New Paint 2020 / New Penn Yan overhaul Sept 2017 / 
IFR equipped and certified /
Garmin GTN 650 /
Garmin GFC 500 Autopilot /
Garmin GTX 345 ADS-B Transponder outputs to Foreflight /
PS Engineering PMA 450B audio panel /
JPI EDM 830 color engine monitor /

$6100 share (refundable), 
$109 / month dues, 
$112.00 / tach hour wet. 

*Updated February 2023

title: True Airspeed Flying Club
name: True Airspeed Flying Club
description:
True Airspeed Flying Club is designed for pilots who want the reality of their pilots license to live up to their dreams of flight.  With packages to fit any dream and any budget, now is the time to step up to a better way of flying.

True Airspeed was built from the ground up with the idea that pilots want to fly well equipped, well maintained aircraft, without having to spend a lot for ownership or sacrifice quality and convenience to fly flight school rentals. 

Our aircraft are independent of our training fleet and are never used for instruction.  The aircraft are kept as an owner would with wheel pants on, clean, fully fueled, and available when you want.

title: Syracuse Flying Club
name: Syracuse Flying Club
description:
The Syracuse Flying Club has been in operation for over 50 years.  We presently own four aircraft, a 1978 Piper Dakota, a 1983 Piper Archer II, a 1977 Piper Archer II, and a 1984 Socata Trinidad TB-20.  The airplanes are IFR equipped and certified.  We have approximately 46 members and are always open to new students or certificated pilots.  We have affiliated instructors for private pilot through ATP instruction.  Our club charges a non-refundable $700 initiation fee, a variable ground fee based on expenses, and very reasonable hourly rates.  We also have online scheduling. 

For more information, contact membership chairman Tom Forleo by e-mail at tforleo1@gmail.com.

title: Tiger Flight Foundation
name: Tiger Flight Foundation
description: The Foundation is a 501C3 non profit foundation based in Rome, Georgia at Richard B. Russell Airport. It was founded in 2000 by two Atlanta-area pilots to enjoy the challenge of formation flying and to promote a unique aircraft, and a decade later is dedicated to promoting science, math and leadership in area youth.
airportName: Richard B Russell Regional - J H Towers Field

title: 81 Escadrille, Inc.
name: 81 Escadrille, Inc.
description: The 81 Escadrille has been around since 1968, when 10 local area pilots pooled resources and bought a brand new 1969 Cessna 172 Skyhawk, N78266.

title: PML Aero Club
name: PML Aero Club
description: Memberships are available. Club operates a Cessna 172M "SuperHawk" PennYan 180 HP STC conversion.

title: United Flying Club
name: United Flying Club
description:
The United Flying Club

The United Flying Club is a general aviation flying club established in 1947 and based at San Carlos Airport, approximately 10 miles south of San Francisco International airport.

We are a Cooperative, Non-profit, organization operated by our members and limited to employees of United Airlines and their immediate family. 

The Club is administered by Club member volunteers, and offers enjoyable recreational flying for its members.

title: Albany Flying Club
name: Albany Flying Club
description: The Albany Flying Club was established in 1970. Currently, we have 34 members. AFC continues its long standing tradition of training the majority of new pilots in the South West Georgia area. AFC club meetings are held every 2nd Monday of the month at 5:30 pm in the KABY Terminal conference room. AFC currently has a C-172 and a Cirrus SR20.

title: Illinois Valley Flying Club
name: Illinois Valley Flying Club
description:
Illinois Valley Flying club is the largest club in the Illinois central valley.

We are a not for profit club that has been around for over 30 years, and also assist with community activities such as a fly in breakfast, airplane wash and wax, young eagles, and assit with the annual TBM
avengers reunion at the airport.

Our 3 club aircraft are a Cessna Skyhawk, a Piper Archer, and a Piper Arrow. 

We are open to new members, and have equity memberships available, and each member pays annual dues, in return in order to get attractive club rental rates and access to club instructors.

See our website illinoisvalleyflyingclub.com for more information.

We are also on facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/groups/475447045977000/
airportName: Illinois Valley Regional-Walter A Duncan Field

title: Skyhawk Flying Club
name: Skyhawk Flying Club
description: Founded in 1971, the Skyhawk Flying Club is a well-established, not-for-profit organization with three aircraft to meet a variety of flying missions.  Our goal is to provide our members with the ability to fly in an economical fashion.  See our rates under "Aircraft", and I think you will see we offer a very attractive option for flying.  We are based out of the Omaha/Millard Municipal Airport (KMLE) in Omaha, Nebraska.

title: University Flying Club
name: University Flying Club
description:
The University Flying club is a non-profit flying club formed in 1969. Our goal is to provide an affordable means of flying for University of Maine students and community members. We own a Cessna 152 and have access to a Cessna 172SP with a Garmin G1000 glass cockpit, owned by the University of Maine. Both aircraft are based at Bangor International Airport. 

Membership is open to the public. See our website for meeting details.

title: WESTERN AERO CLUB
name: WESTERN AERO CLUB
description:
The Western Aero Club is organized as a recreational flying club with social activities organization to provide its members with the opportunities for fellowship and affordable flying. Members enjoy social activities and flying club aircraft.

We meet on the first Saturday of each month at the Riverside Airport Aero Club Hangar number 11. Meeting time is 10 AM.  Whatever happens, it's all good, clean, family fun, with nice people who all share one basic thought, "Isn't it time to go flying?"

There is a one time $100 set-up fees. Dues are simply $20 a month, paid monthly by automatic payment using the club PayPal account through the internet website. Airplanes are rented dry. The club offers tail wheel training and light sport training in an SLSA airplane.  Private Pilot, Commercial Pilot, Instrument Rating training is available. Our mission is to be the most fun and affordable way to fly in SoCal. 

Visit us at www.westernaeroclub.com
Contact Walter Wasowski club president at flybiplanes4fun@gmail.com or send a text message to 909 565 8099

title: Cape Fear Flying Club, Inc
name: Cape Fear Flying Club, Inc
description:
The Cape Fear Flying Club was founded in September 2013 and is based at Modern Aviation FBO at Wilmington International Airport (ILM).  Modern Aviation is a full-service, state of the art FBO with over 10 acres of ramp space.  The club currently has 1 Diamond DA20, 2 Diamond DA40s (one with A/C) and 3 Cessna 172s.  Three of our aircraft are hangared and two are tied down on the ramp at Modern Aviation. We currently have just over 80 members.

The mission of the Cape Fear Flying Club is to provide a venue for members to actively participate and share their collective passion for aviation and flight by: 

- Providing members with safe, modern, technically advanced, and well maintained aircraft to fly. 
- Providing opportunities to advance members' knowledge, safety and piloting skills. 
- Providing the camaraderie and sharing of experience with fellow members. 
- Encouraging club members to participate actively to ensure the long term strength of the club.
- Encouraging club membership interaction with the general aviation community.

title: Skyhawk Five
name: Skyhawk Five
description: Well maintained 1964 Cessna 172E w/a O-360 upgrade.  Based in Claremont, NH (CNH).

title: FAA Flying Club of Washington DC
name: FAA Flying Club of Washington DC
description:
The FAA Flying Club, Washington, DC, was organized in 1962 “…as a nonprofit corporation in order to stimulate and encourage interest in aviation, to advance the knowledge of its members in aviation and aviation related subjects, to sustain and improve the proficiency of its members in flying, to provide the opportunity for its members to fly aircraft economically and conveniently…”

The original membership was geared toward government employees and their families. The current focus is on the general aviation community in an effort to promote aviation safety and wider participation. Therefore, membership in the Club is open to individuals as the Board of Directors may determine. We truly welcome new members. Call or Email us today. We welcome students and will gladly recommend a Club member instructor, although you can use your own instructor, subject to a Club checkout.

The FAA Flying Club currently owns a 1976 Piper Warrior (PA28-150) with the 180hp "Bold Warrior" upgraded engine, a high performance 1968 Piper Cherokee 235 with a 235hp engine, and a 1968 Piper Warrior (PA28-180) with a 180 hp engine. The aircraft are based at Manassas Regional Airport (KHEF) on the east side of the field in Manassas, VA.

title: Frederick Aero Club
name: Frederick Aero Club
description:
To experience the joy of flying in a safe and friendly environment that will allow you to utilize your pilot certificate, in a trusted piece of well maintained, and equipment that you can become comfortable in. Experience the joy of aircraft ownership without the large expense. The Frederick Aero club allows you to share ownership with like minded others at a much lower cost than renting. Make new friends and enjoy flying with other club members

    Based at KFDK Frederick, Maryland
    Just outside the SFRA
    Low Monthly costs
    1984 Archer II WAAS Garmin 530 GPS
    Auto Pilot
    WX Weather and Radio
    Traffic Alerter
    Standby Electric Vac Pump
    Medco Door Locks
    Rosen Sun Screens
    IFR Certifited
    Online Scheduling

 Meetings held every second Thursday of the month at Airways Cafe on the field at 1900. Come joins us

title: Redlands Flying Club
name: Redlands Flying Club
description: Redlands Flying Club was founded in early 2005 by four pilots who felt that there was a need to bring affordable and safe flying opportunities in well-maintained late-model aircraft to the pilot and would-be pilot community of the Inland Empire. The objective is to build up a multi-airplane club with a pilot-to-aircraft ratio (currently limited to 10:1) that we feel is a good compromise between affordability and airplane availability for the individual member. New members do not need to be licensed pilots to join. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic about flying and about continuing to improve their flying skills and experience. Safe and affordable flying is our goal.

title: Capitol City Flyers,Inc.
name: Capitol City Flyers,Inc.
description:
Capitol City Flyers is Madison's premier equity flying club established in 1959. We have 30 members that own and operate 3 IFR aircraft:  a 1980 Piper Archer PA-28-181, a 1978 Cessna Skylane R182 with retractable landing gear and a 2006 Diamond DA-40 with the G-1000 avionics package. Our motto is "A Plane for Any Mission".

The purpose of the club is to promote safe, enjoyable flying and aviation-related activities, and to provide the opportunity for its members to fly aircraft economically and conveniently, supported by excellent service.

We have a free social membership for anyone wishing to learn more about the club, share a flight with a club member, participate in club activities such as plane wash/wax events, maintenance seminars, club fly-outs, hangar-flying happy hours and club BBQ's.

title: Pineywoods Flyers
name: Pineywoods Flyers
description:
We are a group of "Aviation Enthusiast"
We have instructors with rental planes available. 
We are a social flight club. 
Only Two requirements
1) Like airplanes
2) Like people who like airplanes 
Working hard to keep the $100 hamburger runs alive. 
Home Base is  F17 Center Texas.
Check us out or drop us a-line.

~ Keith Martin

title: Crosswinds Flying Club, Inc.
name: Crosswinds Flying Club, Inc.
description: Club Fly Out Trips, Club Meetings, Hangars for all planes. We currently have a Piper Warrior, Piper Archer, Piper Dakota, and a Piper Arrow II based @ BMI.  We also have a Piper Archer and Piper Dakota based @ CMI.

title: Dal-Tex Flyers
name: Dal-Tex Flyers
description:
C182 w/Northpoint XP470 & MT scimitar prop. Mostly GARMIN panel.
Limited to 10 members PPL or greater.

title: West Kentucky Flyers
name: West Kentucky Flyers
description: West Kentucky Flyers (Est. 1993) is a flying club based at KCEY in Murray, KY. Our goal is to provide safe, well maintained and equipped aircraft for our members while keeping flying cost as economical as possible The club's fleet consists of a Cessna 172 and a Piper Arrow PA28R-200. Both planes are very well equipped and IFR certified. Member shares are available and student pilots are welcome! Contact us for more info!

title: Del-Penn Flyers, Inc
name: Del-Penn Flyers, Inc
description:
Del-Penn Flyers Inc. was organized in 1973 for the purpose of safe economical flying. The original club, based at Toughkenamon airport, was founded by 5 members and a Piper TriPacer. In 1975 a Cessna 120 taildragger was added. Since that time various planes have been in our club; a Cessna Skylane, Mooney Mark 20, Piper 180, Piper Archer, two Skyhawks and two Cardinal RGs.

We currently own a Garmin equipped 1978 Cessna 180HP Skyhawk with a leather interior.  We additionally lease a very well equipped 1981 Cessna 182R.

title: Salem Pilots Association
name: Salem Pilots Association
description:
A Flying Club based at McNary Field in Salem, Oregon (SLE)

The oldest continuously operating flying club west of the Mississippi, SPA was formed in 1952 by 4 charter members who purchased a Cessna 140.
 
Today, there are 30 members, and the club operates a Cessna 172 and a Grumman Tiger. The club's hanger has been modernized and includes a pilot lounge/meeting space. Members are able to schedule use of the aircraft via a web-based scheduling system (Aircraftclubs.com).

Our web site is salempilots.org

title: Flying Veterans Club, Inc.
name: Flying Veterans Club, Inc.
description:
The Flying Veterans Club of San Francisco is a California Tax Exempt Corporation that was formed by seven air force veterans in March 1946 at the former Bay Meadows airport. The club is now based at San Carlos Airport (KSQL) and has been continuously operating since shortly after the end of World War II. Membership in the club is not limited to military veterans. Over the years the aircraft have changed, as has the membership, but the club's aviation spirit remains strong. The club has ten members.

The Club owns and operates a Piper Cherokee 180, with a Garmin GNS 430W, an Aspen E5 PFD, a Lynx NGT-9000 ADS-B In/Out transponder, a second NAV/COM, and a full complement of engine monitoring instruments. The control surfaces and landing gear have speed enhancements.

The club has a hangar at San Carlos with an attached office used for member meetings and other functions.
Anyone interested in becoming a member of the Flying Vets is encouraged to contact us.

Website:  http://www.flyingvets.club

title: Rangers Flying Club
name: Rangers Flying Club
description:
The Rangers have been active at Flying Cloud Airport for more then 50 years.  Over the years, the club built a hanger, has owned a number of aircraft and assisted many pilots in starting careers in aviation.  In 2003, we re-organized and the members became equity owners of the club's 1979 172N (Skyhawk).  In 2009, we added a 177RG (Cardinal) to our fleet to provide a more comfortable cross-country airplane.  We are very proud of our aircraft, our hanger and our great group of pilots.

Today, we are a growing, thriving club with many social and aviation related activities.  We have pilots from age 16 through retirement.  We meet each month to review maintenance issues, financial reports and any club business.  Our members include airline pilots, retried military aviators and many private pilots just like you!

We are located in Eden Prairie, MN at Flying Cloud Airport (KFCM).  Our hanger is on the south end of Charlie Lane with a wonderful view of the whole airfield.  Please come by and see us!

title: Aero Association of Caltech (AACIT)
name: Aero Association of Caltech (AACIT)
description: The Aero Association of Caltech (AACIT) is a flying club established in 1966 by students and faculty of Caltech. Membership is open to all members of the Caltech/JPL community (students, faculty, staff, alum, retirees, and contractors). A limited number of membership slots are available those not part of the Caltech community. As of 2023, there is a waiting list for those slots.

title: K-State Flying Club, Inc
name: K-State Flying Club, Inc
description: Low rates and dues

title: Concord Flying Club
name: Concord Flying Club
description:
Concord Flying Club provides both a fleet of excellent airplanes as well as a unique social environment.

The club currently has a 6-seat Bonanza, 4-seat C182, and 2-seat RV7-A, so that the widest range of missions are covered.

CFC does not provide primary instruction, but with 9 CFI's, IFR and commercial ratings are possible.  The club also has an FAA approved FTD for instrument practice.

No initiation fee.  Equity buy-in 100% refundable.  Monthly dues about $100.

title: South Jersey Aero Club (SOJAC)
name: South Jersey Aero Club  (SOJAC)
description: The South Jersey Aero Club (SOJAC) is based at Cross Keys Airport (17N) in Williamstown, NJ.  Our aircraft is a 1978 Piper Cherokee "Archer II" (N2841V).  In the fall of 2014 the aircraft was given a complete avionics upgrade which now includes a Garmin GTN-750 GPS Transceiver, a GDL-88 ADS B Transceiver, and a GTX-327 integrated transponder.  The Club holds monthly meetings on the second Wednesday of each month and twice each year the Club members assemble for a "Wash & Wax" event at the airport.  Current charges include a one-time, $750 membership fee, $100 per month membership dues,  and $100 per hour aircraft use charge (wet wing).  For more information visit our web site, www.sojac.org

title: West Valley Flying Club
name: West Valley Flying Club
description:
FLYOUTS FOR BREAKFAST OR BRUNCH
Twice monthly during the months of November through April, there are group fly outs to some Arizona airport location where the group of pilots and club member passengers have breakfast and social time together. A complete schedule of dates and destinations for the entire year is available on or before the November meeting.  Normally, there is a long flight and a short flight each month.  Passenger seating and costs are set   by each pilot as airplanes have different seating, speeds, load capacities, and fuel costs.

title: Black Forest Soaring Society
name: Black Forest Soaring Society
description:
Black Forest Soaring Society was founded in the spring of 1986. The original location was just northeast of Colorado Springs near the intersection of Woodmen Road and Black Forest Road. The commercial operation at this site, Wave Flights was legendary for the number of high altitude flights achieved in the Pikes Peak wave. This airport was closed in late 1986, and in 1988, the first flights at the current location began.

Originally named Black Forest Glider Park, it was renamed to Kelly Airpark after the owner and developer of the airpark we enjoy today.

Black Forest Soaring Society is a membership organization dedicated to the fostering and promotion of teh sport of soaring. The club is a chapter of Soaring Society of America so all our members belong to SSA as well.

title: Cumberland Soaring Group
name: Cumberland Soaring Group
description:
The Cumberland Soaring Group (CSG, INC.) is a non-profit organization which exists for the purpose of promoting the sport of soaring by providing an organization and facilities for introduction to, training in, and the safe flying of sailplanes for fun, and with a minimum of restrictions, regulations, and cost.

Membership in this organization is open to all those interested in participating in the sport of soaring, and willing to observe the rules and regulations established by the group.

title: Decatur Aero Club
name: Decatur Aero Club
description:
We are a flying club based out of Decatur Illinois KDEC. 

We currently operate 3 aircraft and have approximately 80 members.

Our club office is located in hangar 104 located in the south T hangars

title: Tyler Flyers, Inc.
name: Tyler Flyers, Inc.
description: Tyler Flyers, Inc. has been a not-for-profit, equal share owner, flying club based at Tyler Pounds Field (KTYR) since 1984.  We currently have a 1980 Cessna 172N with a 180HP engine.  Plane is IFR certified and hangared at Johnson Aviation.  We use online scheduling.  Membership is available.

title: Red Lodge Flying Club
name: Red Lodge Flying Club
description: The club has two memberships: one for students and another for licensed pilots. Students pay $200 to start flying at current rates for an instructor and the club’s 172. After soloing, another $400 is due. Upon getting a license, a student must join the club as a full member to continue flying. Full membership entitles members to fly our 172 and, with 100 hours, our 182. The price of club membership is negotiable with members who wish to sell but is approximately $2,300. Students who join as full members within two years of getting their license, are reimbursed $400 of their student membership. In addition to hourly flight costs, full members pay monthly dues to support non-operational expenses such as insurance and hanger rental.

title: Piedmont Aero Club
name: Piedmont Aero Club
description:
We welcome you to our Piedmont Aero Club Website.  The P.A.C. was officially formed in 2012, after what was an employee only Flying Club since 2009, and we saw the need to offer up the gift and excitement of aviation to the entire Community.   We offer an opportunity for aviation enthusiasts in the Triad to meet and share aviation.
 
Whether you are a pilot, flight instructor or someone who just has a passion for aviation, this is the right Club for you.   We have engaged in many activities over the past four years, and have many members who own aircraft and often have empty seats for our many fly-ins, offering many of our non-pilot, or inspiring pilots, to engage in flying activities.
 
We encourage you to visit our site, as we are constantly updating the site.  Look for activities that interest you, and become a member (Visit how to join the Club).

title: Magic Valley Aero Club
name: Magic Valley Aero Club
description: We are a flying club located in Twin Falls Idaho.  We have two planes of which one is a Piper Cherokee and the other is a Cessna 182.  We have memberships available to people that already have a pilot license and we currently have an instructor that is working this students learning to get their private pilot license.

title: BFC Flying Club
name: BFC Flying Club
description:
Our club was founded in 1957 in Naperville, Illinois. We feature late model Cessna aircraft at the lowest prices in the area. Our philosophy is to provide expertly maintained, safe aircraft at the lowest prices for the safe recreational flying of our members.

We are located at Naper Aero Estates (LL10) on 83rd street one block east of Route 59, a private airport community in Naperville, Illinois. Our fleet consists of three beautifully maintained aircraft featuring a 2007 Cessna 182T G1000, a 1999 Cessna 172SP, and a 2007 Cessna 172S G1000. All aircraft are kept inside hangars. Our rental rates, dues structure, and equity buy-in costs are competitive and offer the best value in flying you can find anywhere. We are a non-profit aviation sport Club - not a commercial operation under the guise of a club.

BFC members are a diverse group of men and women with all levels of flying experience. We welcome all pilots of any experience level or rating. We also welcome student pilots with no requirement for minimum hours flown. We have flight instructors in the club who will teach a student with no hours and lead that student to the private pilot rating. Instructors are also available to teach the instrument, commercial, and CFI ratings.

We hold our General Meetings at the airport club house on the south end of the field on the first Tuesday of each month. During the winter, we start at 7:30 PM. During the months encompassing daylight savings time, we start at 5:00 PM with a work night which consists of washing and waxing the airplanes. We then break at 7:00 for a cookout, then start the business meeting at 7:30.

You are welcome to join us for the regular meeting or for the work-night and cookout.

If you are an experienced pilot or have always dreamed of being a pilot, come to our meeting to meet the members and check out the aircraft.

We look forward to meeting you.

Take care, and safe flying!

 
Learn more at https://www.flybfc.org

title: Skycrafters
name: Skycrafters
description: Tennessee’s oldest continuously operating flying club. Equity ownership by members and limited to 38. Generous and flexible reservations policy. Cost-effective primary and instrument training and cross-country flying.

title: Yakima Aero Club
name: Yakima Aero Club
description:
Yakima Aero Club is an affordable way to fly, offering three Cessna aircraft for rent. The club is based at Yakima's McAllister Field, located 3 miles southwest of downtown. 

Our airport has two paved runways, a great mix of air traffic, and a control tower that operates 7 days a week, from 6am to 8pm. 

We operate on a membership basis, and require a small non-refundable fee for joining, and low monthly dues. See our Prices tab for further information.

There are several CFIs in our club who are more than willing to help you brush up on techniques or learn to fly. New members shall be checked out in each aircraft they intend to fly by a club CFI.

title: Atlantic Soaring Club
name: Atlantic Soaring Club
description:
We are a small, friendly soaring club based at Harford County Airpark (0W3) near Churchville, Maryland. ASC is a Soaring Society of America affiliated club. We provide glider flight time, glider flight instruction, and aerotow services to our members as well as one day guest memberships for those interested in an introduction to flying gliders. The club aircraft include a Schweitzer SGS 1-23, a Schweitzer SGS 2-33 trainer, and a Blanik L-13.  Our tow plane is a Belanca Scout.

If you are interested in learning more about us, please call (410) 734-9170 and leave a message. We will call you back as quickly as we can. Our phone is manned on weekends and most holidays during good weather, so if you prefer to speak to us directly, call between 11 AM and 5 PM. We normally answer calls on the weekends.

You also may email your inquiry to the club: info@atlanticsoaring.org

The club flies most Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays (weather permitting). Gift Certificates for introductory flights are available. Please call us to schedule your introductory glider flight.

title: Red-Tailed Hawks - Black Pilots of America, Inc.
name: Red-Tailed Hawks - Black Pilots of America, Inc.
description:
Red-Tailed Hawks Flying Club (RTH) is chartered by Black Pilots of America, Inc. (BPA) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) charitable organization EIN 86-0852905.   RTH has a mission to introduce underserved and underrepresented youths to the world of aviation, engage their minds in practical applications of STEM, ground them in history, inspire them towards aerospace related career paths and help them learn to fly.

RTH is an action-based organization that serves communities and promotes aviation excellence and safety among its membership.  RTH operates two public outreach events: RTH Aviation Experience and RTH Aviation Day Camp.  RTH also operates a year-round youth program and is a partner in the Northwest Earth and Space Sciences Pathways.  The RTH Youth Program engages, exposes, educates and empowers students in grades 6-12 in more than just flying.  Students participate in RTH Aerospace Science Camp and national challenges like Rover Observation and Discoveries in Space (ROADS). 

RTH also conducts formal flight training and pilot development with the assistance of Red-Tailed Hawks Aviation Academy, Inc., which is also a non-profit 501(c)(3) charitable organization EIN 87-1787328.  Red-Tailed Hawks Flight Lesson for Youth (FLY) trains 8-10 cadets annually.  We also sponsor two scholarships for our membership: Jasper Harris, Jr. Aviation Scholarship and Jesse D. Hayes, Jr. STEM Scholarship.

RTH also supports BPA national programs.  Each year RTH competes in Operation Skyhook and has flown home victorious in 2023, 2024 and 2025. The hallmark of the national education effort is the BPA "Les Morris" Summer Flight Academy.  Both events have been in operation since 1971.
 
On November 23, 2013, RTH held its first meeting and provided discovery flight on December 7, 20213. Since then, RTH has grown to be the largest chapter of BPA and impacts youth nationwide.   RTH has engaged with over 9,000 students and produce over 70 pilot certificates and ratings.  Come fly with us!

title: Kittyhawk Squadron 3
name: Kittyhawk Squadron 3
description:
Since its foundation in 1951, Kitty Hawk Squadron 3 has trained hundreds of young men
and women to fly.  If you are between the ages of 14 and 21, you are eligible to participate in this exciting program.  Ground and Flight Instruction are provided at no charge by our volunteer Certified Flight Instructors.  Flight Training is performed in a Cessna 172 provided by the North Hollywood Optimist Club, the primary sponsor of Squadron 3 since 1951.

title: ORANGE COUNTY FLYERS, INC
name: ORANGE COUNTY FLYERS, INC
description:
Orange County Flyers, Inc. was founded in 1959, making it one of the oldest flying clubs in Southern California.  

The original members formed the flying club to encourage interest in aviation; to promote safe and economical flying for its members; to assist its members to advance in the field of aviation, and these are the goals we still maintain.

Orange County Flyers currently has an active group of members utilizing the club’s meticulously maintained Cessna 172N, which is hangered on the east side of John Wayne Airport (KSNA), Orange County, Southern California.

Our AOPA listed flying club usually holds a meeting at 7:00 p.m. on the 2nd Thursday of each month.  Contact our club officers for the next meeting date and time.  

Are you looking to become part of an energetic group of pilots; participate in club activities; increase your flight proficiency, and would enjoy flying in the skies over beautiful Southern California?  If flying was in your past and you wish you could fly again, then Orange County Flyers might be the ideal club for you.

We have a cross section of members from varying backgrounds and levels of experience -  private pilots, instrument rated pilots, through to commercial pilots and active flight instructors.

title: Milco Airways Flying Club
name: Milco Airways Flying Club
description:
MILCO Airways Incorporated is a non-profit 501 (c) (7) corporation founded in March 1944, and are currently based out of Milwaukee’s Timmerman Field (KMWC). We are a tight knit flying club comprised of private, instrument, and commercially rated pilots that not only share the use of the club’s aircraft, but enjoy spending time flying together, learning from one another, supporting each other as safety pilots, promoting a safety culture, planning and attending social events, and the general camaraderie that comes from belonging to such a great group of people.

Our aircraft is a 1979 Cessna 172N, which has been recently upgraded with Garmin ADS-B in/out, a GTN-750, Garmin Bluetooth audio panel, JPI engine monitor, and G5 AI and DG.  It is an very clean plane given her age, and is cared for and loved by our fastidious and safety oriented club members.

title: Skyline Soaring Club
name: Skyline Soaring Club
description:
Come soar with us over the beautiful and historic Shenandoah Valley. Skyline Soaring Club at the Front Royal - Warren County Airport (FRR) near Front Royal, Virginia. Located about 50 miles west of Dulles International Airport and about 70 miles west of downtown Washington, DC, we are situated conveniently to residents and visitors to the nation's capital.

Front Royal marks the northern end of the famous Skyline Drive, a splendid scenic route that runs south down the spine of the Blue Ridge Mountains.  Several of the Shenandoah Valley's famous limestone caverns are nearby, including Skyline Caverns just a few miles south of the airport.  There are many other tourist attractions in the area, including dozens of Civil War battlefields - the town of Winchester, 17 miles north, changed hands more than a dozen times!  

Located between the Blue Ridge Mountains to the east and the northern tip of the Massanutten Ridge on the west, we have excellent soaring conditions - thermal, ridge, and wave; it's not unusual for a soaring pilot to experience all three in a single flight!

title: Rogue Valley Flying Club
name: Rogue Valley Flying Club
description: The Rogue Valley Flying Club (RVFC) is organized as a not-for-profit 501(c)7 organization. Pilots, student pilots, and aviation enthusiasts of all experience levels are welcome to join.

title: NEFC, Inc.
name: NEFC, Inc.
description:
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
NEFC, Inc. is a not-for-profit club, with two well-equipped aircraft: a four-place Piper Archer II (PA-28-181), and a Cessna Cardinal (C177B fixed gear). We promote safe and economical flying for the fun of it. The governing board meets once a month and all members are welcome to attend. In late fall, a Winter Flying Seminar is held and in late summer the Annual Club meeting is held, usually with a BBQ. We have a bi-annual wash & wax of the club aircraft, where members get to talk airplanes and keep our aircraft looking good. We use an on-line scheduling system which also provides contact information to support good communications between club members.

title: North Star Flyers Flying Club
name: North Star Flyers Flying Club
description:
North Star Flyers is an active, growing club based at Anoka County-Blaine Airport (KANE) in the northern suburbs of Minneapolis.  We have six airplanes:

1982 Beechcraft Sundowner
1969 Cessna 172 Skyhawk
1978 Piper PA28-161 Warrior
1979 Bellanca 7ECA Citabria
1972 Piper PA28R-200 Arrow II
1969 Rockwell Lark 100-180

Flying is year-round from our heated hangar.  We offer many educational programs including seminars, courses, and flight instruction to members.

Please note:  As of January 2024 we are full with a significant wait list.  We are happy to talk with you and show you the club facilities and aircraft but will not be able to provide a spot or timeline for an opening for the foreseeable future.

title: Clear Skies Flying Club, LLC
name: Clear Skies Flying Club, LLC
description: Small local flying club, always fewer than 10 members so availability thru online scheduling never a problem. 2008 Flight Design CTLS ‘light sport’ plane with all the bells & whistles includes glass panel and auto-pilot. 35 gal. tanks and a 5.5 gph. cruise (110 kph capable) ensures long range with 600 mile legs possible! Structure of club perfect for ‘time builders,’ $580 initiation fee & $300 monthly furnishes you 5 hrs. flying time, and although you buy fuel the engine prefers (and we encourage) 91 octane auto gas over avgas.

title: Aero Valkaria LLC
name: Aero  Valkaria LLC
description:
We are a social flying club located at X59, Valkaria Florida, which is 10 miles south of Melbourne International Airport, in the Space Coast region of central Florida.
 
This club is the dream of Frank Gallagher. Frank, a professional pilot and flight instructor, is dismayed by the number of pilots who get their Private Pilot license, and then within a year, leave flying. He realized that after the thrill of obtaining the license has passed, pilots get bored with flying for the $100 hamburger. Using the yacht clubs as a model, whose membership only includes 10% boat owners, Frank realized that pilots were lacking the social aspects of flying.
 
Our club concept is unique. Aero Club Valkaria is a business, incorporated as Aero Valkaria, LLC in the State of Florida. Members pay an annual fee, and then an hourly fee for aircraft usage. Members pay their own gas. There are no monthly dues, or aircraft ownership involved. The annual fee covers the fixed costs and the hourly fee covers the operating costs of the aircraft. Rates are adjusted on an annual basis. There are currently five aircraft available for club members, a Cessna 172, a Cessna 182, a Piper Cherokee PA-28-180, a Piper PA-12, and a Light Sport Aircraft Paradise P-1. The Piper Cherokee PA-28-180 is being used by our sister club, which is located in Hartford, CT (KHFD), Aircraft chosen for the club are based on low operating costs, low fuel consumption, safety, and fun factor.
 
Aero Valkaria LLC also performs aircraft maintenance and has the facilities at X59 to address all aspects of General Aviation aircraft maintenance. Our expertise and rates are the most attractive in the area.
 
Flight instruction is also available to both club and non club members, for all ratings from the Light Sport to the Airline Transport Rating, airplane and helicopter, including Certified Flight Instructor-airplane and helicopter,

title: Prescott Flying Club, Inc.
name: Prescott Flying Club, Inc.
description:
Prescott Flying Club is an equity-based flying club based at South Saint Paul's Fleming Field (KSGS).  Our mission is to make aircraft ownership available to the common person.  Our fleet of a Cirrus SR-20, a Piper Arrow, a Piper Warrior, and a Piper Archer have been substantially updated (2020 compliant, Garmin 650's in all aircraft) to provide our members with the best aircraft possible at an affordable rate.  

Student pilots and seasoned pilots are all welcome.  Belonging to Prescott Flying Club gives you the freedom to check out a plane for a long cross country or just enjoy cheap rental rates in the local area.  You can earn your private pilot's license with one of our club's CFIs or take a family trip in one of our planes.  Our aircraft are maintained to the highest standards and we encourage active participation in club events throughout the year.  Our policies and bylaws are structured to keep our members in the air. The number of memberships is limited to ensure aircraft availability.  Go flying when you want to instead of planning around aircraft availability at the FBO or other clubs that have oversold their memberships.  Prescott Flying Club has been committed to maintaining a safe, reliable fleet since our inception in 1968.  Contact one of our board members today for a tour of our facilities and you will see why we have a membership full of happy pilots.
airportName: South St Paul Muni/Richard E Fleming Field

title: Red Wing Soaring Association
name: Red Wing Soaring Association
description: We are a soaring club and a chapter of the Soaring Society of America, providing instruction, glider rental and tow services for members, and scenic and demo flights for non-members.  Individual and family membership is available via a one time buy-in and an annual fee.

title: Alameda Flying Club, Inc.
name: Alameda Flying Club, Inc.
description: Membership is conditional

title: Congressional Flying Club
name: Congressional Flying Club
description:
Congressional Flying Club (CFC) is a non-profit social flying club. CFC provides its members a safe, reliable, and affordable access to general aviation aircraft. 

Our name originates from Congressional Airport in Rockville, MD (now Congressional Shopping Center) where a group of Civil Air Patrol members, including Eberhard Trams, founded the Congressional Flying Club in the late 1940's. To this day, our flying club continues to be collocated  with the the Montgomery Senior Squadron of Civil Air Patrol at Montgomery County Airpark (KGAI). 

When Congressional Airport was closed to make way for the shopping center in 1956, the Congressional Flying Club and Civil Air Patrol squadron moved out to Davis Airport (W50) in Laytonsville, MD. A few years later, CFC moved to the newly opened Montgomery County Airpark (KGAI) where the club and the CAP squadron still thrive today. 

Today, the Congressional Flying Club and Montgomery Senior Squadron are active and vibrant organizations. Many members participate in the monthly fly-ins to interesting destinations. The majority of the club's airplanes make the annual journey to Oshkosh, Wisconsin, the mecca of American General Aviation, for the AirVenture air show. You can always find a crew of pilots at our weekly meetings sharing the infamous "there I was at 12,000 feet" hangar stories.    

Current CFC aircraft and rates (per TACH hour wet):

Cessna 172N - N6269D and Cessna 172M - N23GV
$170
Cessna 177B - N20300
$185 
Cessna 182Q - N5244N
$200

Monthly dues:   $140
Initiation fee:  $1,000

title: North Shore Aero Club
name: North Shore Aero Club
description: Whether you are an active pilot looking for a better deal, an inactive pilot that would like to get current, or someone that would like to explore what being a pilot is all about, the best deal in the air is right here at the North Shore Aero Club!

title: Leading Edge Flying Club
name: Leading Edge Flying Club
description:
Leading Edge Flying Club has earned a reputation for being one of the most exciting flying clubs in Chicagoland. Based out of Chicago Executive Airport (KPWK), we enjoy monthly aviation breakfast meetings and during the summer months, our periodic "Dog Day Afternoon" hot dog socials provide plenty of opportunity to log "hangar flying" hours.

While many of our 90+ members have decided to acquire their own planes, others enjoy exclusive access to aircraft, such as our glass cockpit Piper Archer III and Cirrus SR22. We are always looking for new planes to add to our fleet, which presents an opportunity for members to place their planes into our fleet and reduce their cost of flying.  Besides access to great airplanes, our members also enjoy a family atmosphere, weekly hangar flying, periodic safety meetings, monthly breakfast meetings, and two events that really brings our extended families and "significant others" together.  That includes our annual "Thank You BBQ" and the always memorable Holiday Celebration.

Our membership boasts the presence of novice pilots, airline captains, high-time pilots, aviation enthusiasts, military veterans and a line-up of top flight instructors including an FAA Designated Pilot Examiner.

Members are commonly found flying our simulator (no charge), prepping for a flight, or snacking at the "L'Edge" clubhouse (It's really a Pilot Cave) located on the second floor of our community hangar. We encourage you to drop by and get to know our flying family.  Tailwinds!!!

Our Motto: Great Planes; Great People!

title: Octopus Flying Club
name: Octopus Flying Club
description:
The Octopus Flying Club was formed on September 27, 1962, and operates as a non-profit corporation.  We have a Socata TB-20 Trinidad and a Socata TB-200 Tobago XL at GAI.  We've branched out to KHWO in Florida with a Piper Archer PA-28-181 and a Socata Trinidad TB20 at KHWO. More convenient than renting, more affordable than owning, our Club has distinct advantages that are similar to owning your own aircraft. 24/7 access. Online scheduling. No minimum flight times. No risk of large unexpected expenses. Expertly maintained. Learn and practice in your very own aircraft, equipped with the latest avionics. Available 24 hours per day, 7 days a week. Work with your own instructor. 
Visit us at https://www.octopusflyingclub.com to see our fleet and how to join.

title: Lowcountry Soaring Association
name: Lowcountry Soaring Association
description:
The Lowcountry Soaring Association, LSA, was establised in 1990 by a group of local 
soaring enthusiasts. We have three club owned gliders and a tow plane for aero launch. 
Based at the Ridgeland, SC, Airport, 3J1, we fly every weekend when weather allows.

title: Tahoe Flying Club, Inc.
name: Tahoe Flying Club, Inc.
description: Flying club at Truckee-Tahoe Airport that owns a 1981 Cessna 182R.  Memberships available. If interested, please email us at info@tahoeflyingclub.org.

title: Caprock Soaring Club
name: Caprock Soaring Club
description: Caprock Soaring has about twenty-five members, ranging from student pilots to seasoned instructors and World War II flight veterans. Membership requires an initiation fee and regular monthly dues. Although there are no set schedules or duties, everyone is expected to contribute to flight operations, as appropriate for his or her experience and training. Flight instruction is available as a membership benefit from certified flight instructors in the club. Upon completion of their training, student pilots are examined and licensed by the Federal Aviation Administration.

title: Wabash Valley Soaring
name: Wabash Valley Soaring
description:
We have been flying over the beautiful Wabash River valley for over 45 years.  We are an educational soaring club, dedicated to helping others learn the art and skills of soaring safely.

The club owns a fleet of six club gliders, three of which are two place trainers as well as two tow planes.  There are also over 25 private sailplanes based at the field.  The club has two hangars with a clubroom attached to the main hangar, and a climate controlled shop for maintaining the club fleet.  The shop is used also for restoration of member projects.  
 
We fly mainly on weekends, weather permitting, from March through November.  Weekday flying is often possible as well.

title: Evergreen Flying Club
name: Evergreen Flying Club
description:
The Evergreen Flying Club was established in 1957 to provide our members with affordable aircraft to enjoy for educational, social and recreational purposes.  EFC is Washington State’s longest-standing flying club with aircraft located at Renton Municipal Airport / Clayton Scott Field (KRNT). 

The club presently operates the following aircraft:

1976 Cessna 172M Skyhawk

1974 Cessna 172M Skyhawk

1975 Cessna 182P Skylane

title: Sarasota Westwind Flyers, Inc.
name: Sarasota Westwind Flyers, Inc.
description:
Based in Sarasota, FL (SRQ), Sarasota Westwind Flyers, Inc is a member owned flying club dedicated to safe and affordable flying.

Sarasota West Wind Flyers was formed in 2006 to allow pilots to share in the excitement and benefits of aircraft ownership without the cost and responsibility of being a sole owner. While the club is relatively new our 12 members collectively have decades of experiences as pilots, as owners, and as members of other flying clubs.

Each member owns an equal share of SWWF.  The price of each share is negotiated between the selling members (if any) and the potential buyer.   If you are interested please email and someone will get back to you.  All prospective members of the club have to be voted upon following a meeting with the members, which occurs during one of our monthly meetings.  Those meetings, which are held on the second Wednesday of each month.

title: Condor Aero Club
name: Condor Aero Club
description:
Our Club was founded on March 19, 1957 for the purpose of promoting personal flying and general aviation.  The Club is operated under a charter and set of operating rules approved by a board of trustees who are elected by the membership

Meetings, open to the public, are held on the first Tuesday of each month at 7:30 PM at airport in Zelienople.  Topics include Club business and feature a program covering general aviation interest & safety topics.  Each month, we also hold a "social" starting at 7PM before the meeting.  This is a great way to meet other members and learn more about our Club!    

Each year, we also hold a summer picnic and a "Celebration of First Flight" holiday party.  It's a safe bet that on weekends and the occasional weekday evening, you'll find a group of "hangar flyers" sharing the details of their day's mission.

To join the Club, there is a one-time $1000 initiation fee - after the first year, annual dues are $375.  Additionally, the Club has a group insurance policy, which is divided equally among the flying members.  The insurance cost is usually $500/year for flying members; however, it varies based on the actual policy premium.  For new members, the rate is prorated, so if you join in July, for example, you'd only pay half the rate for your first year.

title: Flying 20 Club
name: Flying 20 Club
description: This Club is interested in promoting a fun, safe environment for beginning to advanced single engine flying, and training.  This is a big and active equity club almost 50 years old.

title: Discover Aviation Center Flying Club
name: Discover Aviation Center Flying Club
description:
The Discover Aviation Center Flying Club (DACFC) was founded in 2013.

Our club currently has 30+ members. We lease 3 aircraft: a Cessna SP172D Skyhawk (TAA), Piper Archer and Piper Tomahawk.  

One Mission: Our members grow the pilot community with public outreach, a shared safety culture, affordable flying in well maintained aircraft and continual aviation education and exploration.  

We have affordable rental rates, and a variety of aircraft to chose from including a basic trainer, VFR cruiser and IFR glass panel cross-country Technologically Advanced Aircraft (TAA).

One Vision: Our members make safety their priority, share their experiences, both good and bad and utilize all resources including the FAA Wings Program to remain proficient and confident through continued education.  

We have an active Safety Management System and an non-punitive reporting system that promotes sharing flights that go well and not so well by training threat, error and undesired aircraft state management. 

Our members come from a wide variety of backgrounds including professional aviation, manufacturing, technology, education, etc.  We actively promote general aviation safety by holding public events several times a year as well as work in coordination with other local aviation groups.  Please visit our website at www.dacfc.org for more information.

title: Clemson Flying Club
name: Clemson Flying Club
description: Located at the Oconee County Regional Airport (KCEU), the Clemson Flying Club has been around since 1927, making us the nation’s oldest continually operated flying club! Today, the Club offers area residents in addition to Clemson University students, faculty, staff, and alumni the opportunity to become members and experience the world of general aviation. The Clemson Flying Club hosts several club related functions throughout the year. Please visit our website as listed above for more information.

title: Cypress Soaring Glider Club
name: Cypress Soaring Glider Club
description:
Aircraft based at both Skylark field in Lake Elsinore and Hemet-Ryan airport in Hemet (Southern California).
  
  Gliders ranging from basic trainers to high performance single seat.

  See website (www.cypresssoaring.org) for contact info and additional details.
  Also find/follow us on Facebook.

title: The Mentone Flying Club, Inc.
name: The Mentone Flying Club, Inc.
description:
The Mentone Flying Club was incorporated on May 13, 1957 and has operated successfully for a period of over 57 years. The MFC was founded to provide for its members a convenient and economical means of private flying. We are a not-for-profit, incorporated organization that functions under a set of by-laws established by its members.

The Mentone Flying Club presently owns two enclosed, heated hangars and two aircraft: 2 Cessna 172 Skyhawks equipped with Garmin 650s and G5s. The Corporation strives to keep these aircraft in good flying condition. The present wet rates for aircraft usage are $110.00 per hour. Flight Instructors currently charge $45.00 per hour.

title: Central Ohio Flyers Association
name: Central Ohio Flyers Association
description: We have a well equipped steam-gauge Cessna 172N equipped with a GNS430W and S-Tec 50 autopilot. For longer distances, we also have a beautiful 180HP Cessna 172M, with a Garmin 650 and S-Tec 50 autopilot, and a Cessna 182P with a Garmin G3X glass panel and GFC500 autopilot. Both aircraft are outstanding cross-country platforms with great availability.

title: Neo-Flites Flying Club
name: Neo-Flites Flying Club
description:
The Neo-Flites Flying Club is a small, friendly club that we're sure you'll like. Our members generally come from the western suburbs of Chicago and as such, our aircraft is based at easy to reach DuPage Airport (DPA) in West Chicago.   We own and operate a single 1974 Cessna 172, tail number N12791 which has recently been upgraded with a Garmin GTN-650 G5 HSI, G5 AI and a new interior.

The club's primary goal is to provide our members with access to a well maintained general aviation aircraft for proficiency and pleasure. We strive to do this within the friendly and supportive atmosphere of a club at a cost that is reasonable. Our membership is composed of people from varied occupations and backgrounds.  From student pilots to airline pilots, we all share a common love of aviation.

To learn more about us visit www.Neoflites.com.  You're also welcome to attend one of our meetings (currently on zoom, please email Neoflites@comcast.net for a meeting link) and get to know us better. We're always glad to have visitors.

title: Wisconsin Fox River Flyers
name: Wisconsin Fox River Flyers
description:
WELCOME TO THE WISCONSIN FOX RIVER FLYERS FLYING CLUB!

For over thirty years Wisconsin Fox River Flyers, Inc. has been offering its member pilots from Southeast Wisconsin the flying experience they want at a price they can afford. Our flying club is a member owned and operated non-profit alternative to aircraft rental (WFRF is in no way associated with any commercial enterprise or FBO). Club members are equal owners and shareholders.

Our mission is to provide our member pilots with well-maintained, well-equipped airplanes at the lowest possible cost and optimal availability. In addition, we hope to provide a social environment where members are able to stimulate their knowledge, increase their proficiency, and encourage a general interest in aviation.

title: 43rd Aviation Flying Club
name: 43rd Aviation Flying Club
description:
The 43rd Aviation Flying Club is a non-profit corporation which was established in 1962. The club is based at Brainard Airport (KHFD) in Hartford, Connecticut, and has operated as a member-owned association ever since. Over the years, the club as owned and operated several aircraft for the enjoyment of its members. The club has a diverse membership, with a wide range of aviation experience from low-time weekend pilots, to seasoned ATPs with thousands of hours.

Benefits enjoyed by members of the 43rd Aviation:

- We offer the best equipped and maintained planes at the lowest hourly rates in the Northeast
- Hour are charged by tach-time providing the best hourly rate possible
- No minimums on daily or weekend reservations.
- Members are allowed up to a two week reservation for a long trip with no minimum hours.
- Advance online reservations allow for planning special events or trips.
- Airplanes are fully IFR equipped with the latest in Garmin avionics.
- Fuel arrangements, reservation assistance, and other services by our local FBO Hartford Jet Center make for convenient access to the airplanes.
- Each member is a named insured on the policy provided by the club.
- Monthly meetings are held first Wednesday of every month where we discuss club business, safety topics and other flying stuff.
- We have regular fly-outs with our 3 planes to fun places in the northeast!
- Minutes of each meeting are sent to the members house via our online reservation system
- Reminder notices are sent to individual members when their medicals or biennial flight reviews are coming due. 
- Members enjoy the camaraderie of friends who love flying and share their experiences.
- Monthly dues float based on insurance costs, tie-down and number of members in the club

title: North Florida Soaring Society
name: North Florida Soaring Society
description: The mission of North Florida Soaring Society (NFSS) is to promote the sport of soaring both locally and nationally through the provision of safe flying, as well as facilities, equipment, education and training for its members on a not-for-profit basis.

title: Finger Lakes Soaring Club, Inc.
name: Finger Lakes Soaring Club, Inc.
description:
The FLSC is a not-for-profit organization, formed to promote the sport of soaring. The club was founded in 1949 by 10 pilots living in Rochester, NY. Five years later the club moved to Batavia to provide better accessibility to Buffalo-based members.   In 1963 the club moved to its current location in Dansville, NY and changed its name to Finger Lakes Soaring.

We have approximately 30 members, ranging in experience from beginning students to nationally-ranked competition pilots. Membership is open to anyone interested in soaring and willing to participate in the volunteer operation of the club.   We have a fleet of 5 gliders and 2 towplanes, along with about 8 privately-owned aircraft.

We love it when we can help people realize their dream to fly. That's why we have some of the best and most creative people in aviation on hand to help you fulfill your goal. Go to the 'Membership' section of the site to get more details on membership types and fees.

The club operates from the Dansville Airport, which is approximately 50 miles south of Rochester.    Our flying activities begin in early April and extend through November. Weather permitting, flight operations occur on weekends and holidays during these months, with impromptu operations on weekdays.

From April through October there is usually someone available at the airport each Saturday and Sunday between 9 AM and 5 PM.

title: Downwind Corp
name: Downwind Corp
description: Feb. 8, 2026 Downwind Flying Club has closed.  Main reason?––uncertain local/national economy in the current stressed national infrastructure, which includes expensive insurance and access to capital.  The major goal in our business plan was to keep GA flying as affordable as possible.  When that was no longer possible with limited resources we had no other choice.  To avoid high interest debt, you may have to spread your training over a longer timeline.  MOSAIC should help to get that first certificate Sport Pilot in your pocket to start logging PIC time.  Remember perseverance is a virtue.  Keep at it and you'll witness what looks like locked windows and doors open to achieve your flying dreams.

title: Morris Aero Club
name: Morris Aero Club
description: Morris Aero Club offers VFR, IFR, Instructional and Social Flying to its members. We have a very nice 172M w/180hp conversion. Avidyne IFD-440 WAAS GPS, two G5’s and new interior. If we get enough members, we’d like to purchase second plane. Come out and check us out. Very reasonable monthly dues and hourly rate is based on Tach Time  wet.

title: Silver City Flying Club
name: Silver City Flying Club
description:
The Silver City Flying Club Inc was founded in 1946 as a non-profit, 40-member equity ownership flying club. The club members own two aircraft, a 1981 Cessna C-172P and a 1979 Piper Archer PA28-181. Both aircraft are IFR certified and are rotated on a tri-monthly basis between Meriden Markham (MMK) & Robertson (4B8) airports. Rotation of the aircraft allows the members the ability to fly each of the aircraft from their preferred airport. The Meriden Markham (MMK) airport also has instrument approaches.

The Club holds a monthly meeting on the 3rd Thursday at 6:30pm. Members are encouraged to attend.

title: Memphis Soaring Society
name: Memphis Soaring Society
description: The Memphis Soaring Society is a nonprofit corporation, organized under the laws of the State of Tennessee as an organization to promote the art, science and sport of motorless flight.   We receive support from the Mid-South Soaring Foundation, Inc., which the IRS has approved as a 501-C-3 organization.   Membership is required to utilize any club aircraft or facilities.   A one day membership is available for individuals who are interested in the sport.   The cost is $50.00 and includes one flight in one of our two place gliders.

title: Idaho Skyriders
name: Idaho Skyriders
description: Skyriders is a member-owned flying club based at McCarley Field (U02) in Blackfoot, Idaho.  For over 45 years, Skyriders has provided low cost access to general aviation and the freedom that it offers.  Our aircraft are all IFR certified and well maintained.  Skyriders members own shares in the club and therefore share joint ownership of the club's assets.

title: Toledo Buzzards Light Sport Aircraft Club, Inc
name: Toledo Buzzards Light Sport Aircraft Club, Inc

title: Bay de Noc Flying Club
name: Bay de Noc Flying Club
description: One Aircraft - 1978 Piper Archer II; IFR certified, Steam gages, ADS-B Compliant, Transponder is compatible with ForeFlight.

title: Uwharrie Eagles Flying Club, Inc.
name: Uwharrie Eagles Flying Club, Inc.
description: The Uwharrie Eagles Flying Club was formed in 1987 by a small group of flying enthusiasts who desired to share expenses and experiences of owning an aircraft. The club now has 16 members who collectively own a Cirrus SR-22 and a Piper Cherokee 235 (PA-28).

title: Soaring Society of Boulder
name: Soaring Society of Boulder
description: The Soaring Society of Boulder (SSB) is based at Boulder Municipal Airport, Colorado. A not for profit club, it has been in continuous operation since 1959. We provide gliders, tows, training and a great social environment to our 170+ members and their families. Our membership ranges in experience from fresh adoptees of the sport, instructors, national champions to world championship contenders.

title: Valley Flying Club Inc.
name: Valley Flying Club Inc.
description:
OUR AIRCRAFT ARE EQUIPPED WITH PANEL MOUNT IFR, APPROACH CERTIFIED, GPS SYSTEMS, SOPHISTICATED S-TEC AND KING AUTOPILOTS WITH ALTITUDE HOLD, HSI AND FLIGHT DIRECTOR, AS WELL AS STATE-OF-THE -ART COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS. WE HAVE MATURE EXPERIENCED INSTRUCTORS AVAILABLE.
