CLUB ACTIVITIES

title: Sky Bryce Flying Club
name: Sky Bryce Flying Club
description: The Sky Bryce Flying Club has bi-monthly meetings which usually include refreshments. Members and non-members are welcome to attend. To be placed on the email list for upcoming meetings, please send your email address to: skybryceflyingclub@gmail.com. Volunteers are occasionally needed to help with runway maintenance.  If interested in helping, please send an email to the address above.

title: Sky Roamers, LLC
name: Sky Roamers, LLC
description: The Club is organized to provide a means for pilots to fly economically for pleasure and who would not probably have their own personal aircraft.

title: Tailwinds Flying Club
name: Tailwinds Flying Club
description:
Tailwinds Flying Partnership is based at Lake Elmo airport, 21D, in Lake Elmo, MN. We are a non-profit corporation of 39 pilots who equally own three aircraft. Our goal and philosophy are to fly great airplanes inexpensively. We strive for consistency in equipment among our three airplanes. 

Tailwinds was established in 1970 and has continually upgraded its airplanes and hanger facilities. Currently we have three airplanes. The three Piper aircraft are equipped with the same avionics. This spring all of the airplanes are being updated to the Garmin G3x touch screen system and 100% glass panel. Our airplanes are expertly maintained from member A&P's and external services as required. Our philosophy to fly great airplanes as inexpensively as possible has drawn pilots to our club and keeps them flying. We use a web based scheduling system at www.AircraftClubs.com with an additional phone access feature. About once a month during the summer months our members get together and wash and wax the airplanes to keep them looking their best. All members take pride in our planes and care for them accordingly. After each flight, we wash off the bugs, clean the windows, and straighten out the cabin so the next pilot has a clean plane. Our By-Laws and Rules & Regulations are designed to provide structure where needed without being overly restrictive.

title: Park Forest South Aviation Group
name: Park Forest South Aviation Group
description:
Non-profit Chapter of the Soaring Society of America.

Introductory rides and glider instruction for Sport, Private and Commercial Glider ratings. Tow pilot training. Instruction for new or add-on glider rating. Cross-country soaring, aero- and ground-tow instruction is also available. A glider rating is achievable in 1 to 2 seasons for new pilots and within 1 season for add-on pilots.

Membership fee is $129 per year which includes membership in the Soaring Society of America, Inc. www.ssa.org Membership is required. No initiation fee. Scholarships are available. All member tow pilots and instructors are volunteers. Aircraft and towing fees are kept at a minimum.

Aircraft available: Cessna 150H (STOL kit); Schweizer 2-33; Schweizer 1-26; Grob G-103; Rolladen-Schneider LS-1

A Civil Air Patrol Schweizer 2-33 glider is also available for flight instruction at minimal rates (membership in Civil Air Patrol required to access this glider).

Flight operations April through November on weekends (weekdays by appointment). Winter activities include aircraft maintenance and ground instruction.

Overnight facilities and camping is available on the field for a small charge. Bi-weekly cookouts and movie nights in the summer.

title: Indian River Flying Club
name: Indian River Flying Club
description: The Indian River Flying Club was founded in 1991 to provide access to airworthy and dependable aircraft for the member pilots at a low overall cost.

title: Shen Air II
name: Shen Air II
description:
Shen Air II is a small flying club based at the Shenandoah Valley Regional Airport (KSHD). KSHD is about 20 minutes by car from Harrisonburg and Waynesboro, and under an hour from Charlottesville. Shen Air II bylaws limit club membership to 15 people.  The club owns two aircraft, a Piper Archer II and a Cherokee 6 300. Both airplanes are equipped with Garmin GTN 650 touchscreen approach certified GPS units and are hangared at KSHD.  In 2022, we added a Garmin GFC500 autopilot to the Archer, along with two Garmin G5 instruments.  Planes are reserved through an online calendar. 

If you are interested in joining, please contact us to inquire about the availability of shares and current fees.

title: Cascade Flyers, Inc.
name: Cascade Flyers, Inc.
description:
We are Cascade Flyers, a not-for-profit flying club established in 1958 to "promote good sportsmanship in flying recreation."

The Cascade Flyers are based at Paine Field, Everett, Washington (KPAE) and operate two very well maintained IFR-capable Cessna aircraft - a Skyhawk (C172) and a Skylane (C182).

Feel free to contact us by e-mail at info@cascadeflyers.com or by phone at 425-954-3180 and we can discuss more about the club and how to join.

title: Phoenix Flyers, Inc
name: Phoenix Flyers, Inc
description:
Phoenix Flyers is a non-profit, member-owned Flying Club based in Phoenix Arizona. Our Flying Club was founded in 1958 with the goal of providing excellent aircraft at reasonable rates. We have four aircraft: Two Cessna Skylanes and a Piper Archer. All aircraft are owned by Phoenix Flyers Inc., enabling us to keep our flying cost low. Our club members fly some of the nicest and best equipped aircraft in Phoenix.

Our club aircraft are based at Phoenix Deer Valley (KDVT) and Chandler Municipal (KCHD) airports. We rotate our aircraft between Deer Valley and Chandler every four months. See our website for details on our aircraft, operations, and how to join.

title: Vagabond Flying Association
name: Vagabond Flying Association
description: We are an equity club where each member is a vested owner.  Memberships do become available. Feel free to contact us for availability. We have heated hangars and liability insurance

title: The Flying Neutrons, LLC
name: The Flying Neutrons, LLC
description:
The Flying Neutrons is a member-owned, non-profit flying club located in the Cincinnati Area at the Warren County Airport (I68) and has been in existence since 1952, dedicated to providing safe and low-cost flying. 

Our fleet consists of three Cessna 172s, two Cessna 182s, and a Cessna 206. All aircraft are hangered and have IFR-certified Garmin GPS with WAAS and dual Garmin G5s. We also have an IFR-certified PCATD. We offer flight training to our members with our well-equipped aircraft at $15 -$30 an hour below typical commercial rates. Whether you are a seasoned pilot or just starting out, we have something to offer. We have over 15 club-approved, FAA-certified flight instructors in our membership who actively instruct as independent contractors. They have many years of experience and instruct for the love of flying.

The membership supports local high school students interested in aviation careers by providing partial scholarships toward their PPL.

We have monthly club meetings for governance and operations starting with a grill-out to get to know fellow pilots, and we conduct monthly safety meetings and ground schools to maintain safety awareness and camaraderie. Members gather for a semi-annual aircraft wash-and-wax, and we occasionally fly together on breakfast runs when the weather and time permits. You can almost always find someone just hanging around the clubhouse on a nice afternoon.

title: South Shore Flying Club
name: South Shore Flying Club
description:
Fly a like new, 1999 Piper Archer III or a 1976 Cessna 172M Skyhawk each with its own hangar based at Marshfield MA (KGHG) for less than the cost of renting.  Our C182 1965 Skylane is hangared at nearby Plymouth MA (KPYM).  The Archer III and C172 and their hangers are club owned.  The C182 and its hanger are a lease-back.

Low airframe hours, excellent avionics, professionally maintained on site and at local Avionics shop.  

A $2000 initial by-in charge, non refundable, for the Archer III and C172.  A $1000 initial nonrefundable for the C182 only, with an additional $1000 if upgrading to all three planes.

Fixed monthly charge of $160 for the Archer III and C172 only,  $120 for C182 only,  or $220 monthly for all three.  Variable charges below by tach time.

South Shore Flying Club benefits:
-Your own keys to the hangar and aircraft
-Cross country flying with no minimum hours
-No minimum daily hours charge for trips
-Hassle-free online computer scheduling, great flexibility
-IFR certified with excellent avionics
-Professionally maintained - squawks fixed immediately

-Limited membership inquire with questions or availability by email ONLY to SSFCGHG@comcast.net


Website (Not for Application): 
https://www.southshoreflyingclub.com

Facebook for General Events only (Not for Application):
https://www.facebook.com/SouthShoreFlyingClub



1999 Archer III
  Dual Garmin 430W WAAS
  STec 55x Auto Pilot 
  JPI/EDM Engine Analyzer
  GTX 345 ADS-B In and Out
  Panel Mounted iPad Mini with Foreflight, Traffic and Weather
  IFR Certified
  $134/Hr Wet - Varies With Fuel Price at GHG
  
1976 Skyhawk
  Garmin 650
  Aspen EDF100 Pro
  STec 30 Auto Pilot
  GTX 345 ADS-B In and Out
  IFR Certified
  $134/Hr Wet - Varies With Fuel Price at GHG

1965 Cessna 182 Skylane  
  Hangared at PYM.
  Garmin GTN 750 Xi 
  GI 275 Attitude Indicator
  GI 275 HS
  Clock w/ Carbon Monoxide Detector
  IFR Certified
  $171/Hr. Wet - Varies with Fuel Price at PYM

title: Bay Area Aero Club
name: Bay Area Aero Club
description:
The Bay Area Aero Club (BAAC) is a non-profit flying club based at the Pearland Regional Airport since 1979.  Our membership is diverse and includes students working on obtaining a private license, private and commercial pilots, pilots with instrument and multi-engine ratings, CFI and CFII instructors, and airline transport pilots. Each member is covered by a comprehensive insurance policy, and is required to take an annual check ride with a certified Club Instructor.

The BAAC has aircraft agreements with several owners to rent their aircraft exclusively to Club members. The Club's fleet varies from time to time, but we try to maintain a mix that includes primary trainers, instrument trainers, complex aircraft, and single-engine cross country aircraft. Our aircraft are available for local and extended overnight trips.  At this time, we have seven great aircraft in the club.  

The Bay Area Aero Club is located at Darrell Bivens' Hangar between Life Flight and Total Aircraft on the taxi-way off of Malthusian Way. A membership application is available online on our website. When completed it will be reviewed for approval. Fees include an initiation fee of $100 (payable at orientation), and low monthly dues.

The BAAC offers an attractive aircraft agreement program for aircraft owners. The Club pays the standard airport ramp tie-down fees and a portion of the aircraft insurance coverage. The aircraft owners receive a specified dry rate for the rental of their aircraft and all fuel and tax charges are collected from the members and paid by the Club.

title: Connecticut Flyers, Inc.
name: Connecticut Flyers, Inc.
description:
CT Flyers Inc was formed to provide low cost flying opportunities for local pilots who are serious about their flying but also appreciate the benefits of membership in a club. 

Founded in 1993, the CT Flyers flying club is a well established, not for profit organization with two aircraft to meet a variety of flying missions.  Our goal is to provide the members with safe, economical and convenient recreational flight operations.  With on line reservations, members can plan their next flight from any web accessible device.  With a target membership of near 22 pilots, that means that the members are more likely to find a plane available when they are looking to fly, all for significantly less than individual ownership.

CT Flyers members are conscientious pilots from a variety of backgrounds:  small-business owners, engineers, dentists, airport managers, and retirees – but we all share a passion for aviation and treat the aircraft like we own them – because we DO! The club emphasizes safety, preventive maintenance, and respect for fellow members. 

Both planes are flown year-round - well over 150 hours each – and maintenance and inspections are performed at Chester airport, minimizing down-time.   We have tenure as an organization and a solid operational safety record spanning almost 20 years

title: Pinellas Pilots Association
name: Pinellas Pilots Association
description: Reasonable Fees, Meticulously maintained airplane, Easy online scheduling 24 hours a day, Excellent semi private hangar, 24-hour access, Informative safety meetings, Instructors and members who fly for the joy of flying. We have a 1981 Cessna Skyhawk 172P. A partial list of the equipment in N52633: Power Flow tuned exhaust, Garmin GMA 340 Audio Panel w/3 light Marker Beacon', 4 place Intercom, King KX155 Nav/Com, Dual Garmin G5 PFD & DG/HSI, Garmin GNC 355 WAAS IFR GPS/COM, Garmin Aera 510 VFR, Stratus ESGI Transponder w/ADSB IN/OUT, Status 2i GPS, ship powered for WX, Traffic and backup AHRS, Status Power Dual 2.5-amp USB-A charging ports, STEC 40 Single Axis Auto pilot, and a EDM 930 Engine Monitor.

title: Moccasin Flying Club
name: Moccasin Flying Club
description:
Monthly dues provide liability and hull insurance coverage for aircraft and coverage for club members and passengers as well as aircraft maintenance.  Aircraft rental rates are charged from elapsed tachometer time rather than hourly clock (Hobbs) time.  Two long-term members are CFIs and a long-term CFII is available to club members.

Current fleet:
     -1979 Piper Archer II

Visit our webpage at WWW.Mocfly.org

title: Cloud Cappers
name: Cloud Cappers
description: The club also offers VFR and Advanced Flight Training

title: Cloud One Flying Club
name: Cloud One Flying Club
description:
The Cloud One Flying Club is a 25 year old non-profit organization based at the Downtown Airport (KMKC) in Kansas City, MO. The 18 club members each own an equal share of the 1968 Piper Arrow 180 and the 1976 Cessna 172M that make up the club fleet.

Born out of a desire to fly well maintained aircraft economically, the Cloud One Flying Club still makes this possible today.

Because each club member is an owner, unlike the renting environment, care is taken by all to ensure safety, compliance, and quality in both of our aircraft.

The club currently has one member with their CFII and two approved flight instructors who are available to help you pursue that next rating, or just to help you stay current in your flying. Our dynamic scheduling process and rules are fair to everyone who wants to fly for a yearly vacation, training or just poking holes in the sky. As far as our members, we are a diverse and dynamic group of folks who have come together to share their love of flying.

title: CAP Flying Association Inc.
name: CAP Flying Association Inc.
description:
Civil Air Patrol Flying Association Inc (CAPFA), although no longer affiliated with Civil Air Patrol, is one of Connecticut's oldest flying clubs. Established in November of 1946, CAPFA has been operating out of Brainard Airport (HFD), in Hartford, continuously for 76 years. CAPFA has provided educational and recreational flying opportunities for generations of general aviation student and private pilots.

As a not for profit flying club (501c7), CAPFA is dedicated to providing an affordable learning and recreational flying environment for its members. We currently operate and own two aircraft.

CAPFA offers an online scheduling system, reasonable monthly fees and flying rates, liberal booking policies, as well as club CFI's (Certificated Flight Instructors).  In addition to providing high-quality and well-maintained aircraft, CAPFA provides the social camaraderie only aviation enthusiasts can appreciate.  Per our original charter, we are one of few clubs in Connecticut that admit student pilots.  We also sponsor a club dinner, educational events and of course, lots of hangar talk.

Come to a monthly meeting, the third Thursday of each month at 630 PM, usually (unless we're hosting our annual dinner meeting or annual cookout meeting) in the conference room of Hartford Jet Center, located on Lindbergh Drive at Brainard Airport.

title: Mitchell Flying Club
name: Mitchell Flying Club
description: We boast a fine Cessna 172R with the 180 HP upgrade and a freshly overhauled engine and a new Garmin GTN750 with ADS-B out & in. We also have a Cessna 182Q with a Garmin GNS 530W with ADS-B out. Monthly payments are based on fixed costs and split evenly with all members. We maintain an escrow for replacing the engines and upgrading avionics in the future. Rates are dry and figured off the tach and your deposit is refundable. Check out our web site for more info at http://www.mitchellflyingclub.com/

title: Santa Barbara Flying Club
name: Santa Barbara Flying Club
description:
Since 1947, the Santa Barbara Flying Club has made flying less expensive, more convenient, less hassle, and more fun for generations of pilots in the Santa Barbara, California area.  Our club currently has 55 members, running the gamut from those brand new to flying to commercial pilots and retired air force aviators.

The Santa Barbara Flying Club has four aircraft at SBA: a Cessna 172 Skyhawk, a Vans RV-9A, a Grumman Tiger AA-5B, and a Piper PA-32/300 Cherokee 6.  All planes are IFR certified.  The Skyhawk and Cherokee 6 have a GNS 430W, the Tiger a GTN650Xi, and the Vans RV-9A is /U.   

As a not-for-profit flying club, we effectively rent these airplanes to ourselves at cost, so club members are guaranteed the best value for their money.  We use tach time billing.  It's the most accurate way to account for our actual expense, and amounts to as much as a 30% discount when compared with Hobbs billing, especially for those who are practicing maneuvers or "Touch & GOs" and typically have the power back much of the flight.

Club aircraft may be conveniently scheduled online by our members for trips as long as 10 days, with no daily minimum flight time requirement.  This makes them perfect for cross country flights.  Each member receives their own set of keys to each aircraft.  This eliminates any last minute hassle of having to check in and out at a rental desk.  Shared aircraft ownership means the airplane is waiting for us when we arrive… 24/7.

Latest Rates and Dues can be found by visiting our website.

title: Fort Myers Flying Club
name: Fort Myers Flying Club
description:
The Fort Myers Flying Club, originally known as the "Cub Club," was founded in 1959 right here at Page Field (KFMY) in sunny Fort Myers, Florida.

FMFC accommodates any pilot skill level, from the basic beginner just learning to fly, all the way up to a full Instrument rating and beyond! Our Flying Club offers quality aircraft at value-based rates. Come fly with us!

title: Jersey Aero Club
name: Jersey Aero Club
description:
The Jersey Aero Club is a non-profit organization formed and operated for the purpose of providing a way of flying quality aircraft as inexpensively as possible for as many pilots as possible, and therefore, to aid in furthering general aviation.

Founded in 1938, the Jersey Aero Club (JAC) in NJ's oldest active flying club. The JAC is an organization of pilots with a wide range of experience, who have created a club to share in the ownership of 5 airplanes and office and to maintain it.

Interested in ownership of an aircraft, but don't want all the expenses? As a club member you own a share of our airplane. Perfect for a former owner looking for fewer responsibilities and costs but also perfect for the person that has never owned an aircraft and trying to gain some knowledge and/or experience.
Interested in fellowship with pilots who have a wide range of experience? As a club member you are part of a great group of people which are flying enthusiasts just like you. A perfect group for an experienced pilot but also a perfect group for someone just starting out and trying to gain some knowledge and/or experience.

Club membership is always open. Message us here or see a current Club member for details. Join the Club, Jersey Aero Flying Club!

title: Mid-Tenn Aero Club
name: Mid-Tenn Aero Club
description:
Mid Tenn Aero Club has 2 C172s.  Additional information can be found at our Facebook page (https://www.facebook.com/Midtenn.aero.club/).  To be added to our member list and be interviewed by officers please complete the following questionnaire.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdVWiiu4w_5V4lTGIog0CN8EhFiHQFuwI_ro4llWxUrhiZOgw/viewform?usp=sf_link

You may also email bruce.ellard@comcast.net with questions.

The below details are current but can change.
One Cessna 172N based and hangered at KMBT
180 HP conversion
IFR Certified
N1163F has GTN650 - Garmin 430W - STEC 50 Autopilot ADSB compliant


Cost as of Jun 23 2024
$750 to join
$65 per month dues
N1163F $135per hour wet ; this varies based upon fuel costs

title: Northern California Soaring Association
name: Northern California Soaring Association
description:
Our flying club is a glider club..  The Northern California Soaring Association, based in Byron.
Many power pilots join our club to learn to fly gliders and soar, often long distances, depending on the weather.

Starting with an Introductory glider flight, members get a feel for the club and see how they like flying without power, learn how to find and use lift instead of an engine.

title: Florida Chapter Short Wing Piper Club
name: Florida Chapter Short Wing Piper Club

title: Dawn Patrol Flying Club
name: Dawn Patrol Flying Club
description: Equity club with 24 members and 2 Cessna airplanes.  1976 C-177B Cardinal.  1975 Cessna C-172M Skyhawk.   Based at 1D2 - Plymouth Canton Mettetal Airport

title: Queen City Aero Club
name: Queen City Aero Club
description: Queen City Flying Club, one of the oldest flying clubs in the State of NH, operates a 1974 Cessna 172 (N20172) out of KASH, Nashua, NH. There are currently 15 members.   It is located at the electric ramp. Features include a new Penn Yan overhauled engine with 100 hours, a Garmin 430W GPS, dual glideslopes, power flow exhaust, and LED landing light. It is IFR certified and has 4500TT.

title: Dayton Pilots Club
name: Dayton Pilots Club
description:
We are a modern progressive flying club dedicated to the purposes of safe flying, the advancement of general aviation, and to providing economical and reliable aircraft for the use of its members.

In existence since 1958, we have well-maintained, IFR equipped Cessna 182RG based at Dayton Wright Brothers (KMGY). Our highly competitive rates are easy on the wallet, and the fixed monthly costs associated with the Club are minimal. And our membership has a passion – just like you – for flying.

DPC actively promotes aviation safety, offering regular safety meetings and seminars.

title: Tri-County Flyers, LLC.
name: Tri-County Flyers, LLC.
description:
We are a collection of flyers in various stages of our aviation endeavors.  Some are students, some recreational VFR only pilots, some instrument rated, and some CFIs.  We are a casual group of guys, but operate our Club in structured environment in accordance with our By-Laws and Rules, but above all rules, operate with a respect for our fellow members.

The Tri-County Flyers (formally the One-Fifty Club) was organized in December 1999 to allow its members to fly in a cost controlled co-operative environment, while at the same time being able to fly aircraft that are available, and maintained as good as and better than the available rental fleet.  An important by-product of a club environment is the group camaraderie that results in sharing aviation experiences, stories, discussions, and most importantly, friendships.

title: Orlando Aero Club
name: Orlando Aero Club
description:
The Orlando Aero Club (OAC), established in 1967, is one of Florida's largest member-owned flying clubs.  The Orlando Aero Club is strictly an owner/operator organization.  Each active member owns one (1) share of stock ownership in the Club, is entitled to a single vote and is a partial owner of all Club assets.   We are not a flight training organization nor do we rent our aircraft.  While we welcome all who are interested in aviation, we are looking for long term member owners.


 
We are based on the northeast corner of the Atlantic Aviation ramp at Orlando Executive Airport (KORL). The Club currently operates three (3) aircraft with an allowable membership of twenty (20) pilots per aircraft.  One of the more unique aircraft available in the Club is the Citabria (7GCAA), an excellent aircraft for obtaining your tail-wheel endorsement and learning aerobatics.  All aircraft are professionally maintained and serviced by Orlando Aircraft Services.


  

As with all flying organizations, training is an important aspect of the Orlando Aero Club. Yearly check rides for all member-owners are required. In addition, should a member owner desire to advance his ratings, both initial and recurrent training is available for our member/owners from Certified Flight Instructors who are member owners of  the Orlando Aero Club.

title: Southeastern Minnesota Flying Club
name: Southeastern Minnesota Flying Club
description:
For more than 65 years, the Southeastern Minnesota Flying Club has provided area pilots with access to safe, affordable aircraft. From local sightseeing trips to cross country adventures, our members enjoy the freedom to fly a variety of missions.

Our goal is to provide members with affordable access to safe and modern aircraft. But we view ourselves as more than an aircraft rental service. Rather, we also aim to be ambassadors of the broader aviation community, and we take pride in sharing our pursuit with others. Whether through participation in outreach programs such as EAA's Young Eagles, through sponsorship of educational seminars such as AOPA's Rusty Pilots, or through sharing our knowledge and experiences with fellow Club members at our monthly business and safety meetings, our goal is to be visible, active role models for general aviation.

Whether you are an active pilot, a pilot whose experience has lapsed, a pilot who wants to add a new rating, or an aviation enthusiast yearning to become a pilot, you are welcome to join our Club. As co-owners of our aircraft, Club members are allowed to take flight training in our airplanes. The Southeastern Minnesota Flying Club is not a flight school and does not provide flight instruction, but training is available at Rochester and nearby airports.

Join our group of pilot-owners in one of the longest operating and most affordable flying clubs in Minnesota. Visit us at www.semfc.org for more information and to arrange a personal tour of our facilities.

title: Blue Sky Aviation Association
name: Blue Sky Aviation Association
description: Established in 1957, Blue Sky Aviation Association, Inc. is one of New Jersey’s oldest flying clubs. It is a social club that efficiently provides well-equipped, well-maintained aircraft to its members for recreational flying at a reasonable expense.  The Club provides opportunities for members to strengthen flying skills and improve the Club’s operation and social value. We’re based at Solberg-Hunterdon Airport (N51) in Readington.  We have three airplanes: Cessna Skylane 182, Piper Dakota PA28-236, and Cessna Skyhawk 172SP. All airplanes are well maintained with glass panels and 3-axis autopilots, certified for IFR flight.

title: Pompano Senior Squadron Flying Club Inc
name: Pompano Senior Squadron Flying Club Inc
description:
Pompano Beach Flying Club is a non-profit organization based in South Florida at Pompano Beach Airport (KPMP).
Our mission is to promote general aviation and give pilots of any level the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful and unique experience to flying.

Counting on 300 days a year of good weather, three runways, a towered airport, low traffic density, all at a short one hour flight from the Bahamas.

Starting in 2019, the club also allows members to use the club aircrafts for training to earn your wings. Private, instrument, commercial all the way through CFI certification, our club will be able to meet your needs.

Visit our website to become a member: http://pompanobeachflyingclub.com

title: VARS Flying Club
name: VARS Flying Club
description:
Located at Falcon Field in Mesa, Arizona. VARS is non-profit flying club. Our current aircraft is an IFR equipped 1972 Piper Cherokee 235. There is a cap of 10 members in our club. 

Looking for a place to fly at a reasonable cost and be part of a great group of pilots?

Our membership is currently full but if you are interested in being put on our waiting list, please fill out our questionnaire and we will get back to you shortly.

title: Daniel Boone Flying Club
name: Daniel Boone Flying Club
description:
-----Mission: The Daniel Boone Flying Club (DBFC) is organized for the purpose of encouraging and enabling participation in the field of aviation and allowing more people the opportunity to enjoy the experience of flight.

-----History: The Club was formed in 2002 with four original members and one airplane. It has been in continuous operation since that time, calling Boonville, Missouri’s Jesse Viertel Memorial Airport (KVER) its home. It is a member equity, not-for-profit corporation in Missouri. There are seven board members responsible for the Club’s property, finances, and administrative tasks. Five serve in officer roles and two are at-large, voting members. For reasons related to insurance and administrative burden, the Club size is capped at 30 members, where it has remained for several years. A prospective member pool is maintained for individuals who are interested and qualified.

-----Meetings: Meetings take place at KVER on the second Sunday of each month. Likely one of the greatest benefits of membership in the DBFC, this time is set aside to conduct business (the board has that primary responsibility), hold each other accountable to standards, rules, regulations, and best practices, and to communicate with one another on topics that will help members become better pilots. A number of social gatherings take place throughout the year, as well. Visitors are welcome to attend meetings at any time.

-----Planes: The Club has three planes that are all stored in hangars: a Cessna 172K, a Cessna 177B, and a Cessna 182R (an RG aircraft that covers complex/high-performance needs). All three are IFR certified, have WAAS enabled GPS systems, a second NAV/COM, and an ADS-B-Out transponder. Two are equipped with very capable autopilots and digital engine monitoring systems. Additionally, the Club owns a Fly This Sim BATD device that may be used for training and maintaining currency.

title: Blackhawk Flying Club, Inc.
name: Blackhawk Flying Club, Inc.
description:
Celebrated their 70th Anniversary in the Fall 2023. Club Started in 1953. 

"Like" us on Facebook! www.facebook.com/BFCRockford

title: Chuckanut Flying Club
name: Chuckanut Flying Club
description:
The Chuckanut Flying Club is located in the beautiful Pacific Northwest region, and the club is based out of the Bellingham International Airport (KBLI).

The club has two IFR-equipped aircraft: a Cessna 182N Skylane, STC'd fuel-injected 260 h.p., vortex generators, $220/hour wet tach, and a leased Piper Archer, 180 h.p., $165/hour wet tach.

Both are professionally maintained, and each aircraft has its own hangar, and they are available to members without overnight or away charges.

Scheduling is easy to accomplish with your smart phone through an online scheduling system.

Memberships are available. The new membership joining fee is $750.

Monthly dues are $150.

Email info@chuckanutflyingclub.com

Please join us and enjoy flying in the beautiful Pacific Northwest!

title: Okoboji Flyers, LLC
name: Okoboji Flyers, LLC
description: Okoboji Flyers operates a 1979 Piper Dakota (N4044Q) with a STEC 30 Autopilot coupled to a Garmin 530W GPS.  A monthly capital contribution is required, along with an hourly rate for flown hours.

title: Cooperative Crossroads Flying Club
name: Cooperative Crossroads Flying Club
description:
Now this is a club that has affordable flying figured out! Formed in 1954, the long lasting success of this club is testimony to the fact that they've figure out how to make flying affordable!

The Crossroads Cooperative Flying Club of Albuquerque, NM is an equity style club of 16 pilots who share in the joys of flying while splitting the expenses in an effective and affordable way.

The club owns two hangared airplanes based at Double Eagle Airport (KAEG). The first is a Cessna Hawk XP, a well equipped 195 HP high wing aircraft that cruises at 120 knots.  The second is a 300 HP Piper Lance, 6 seater that makes family sized trips in/out with WiFi for integration with tablets,  a comfortable pleasure. Both airplanes are IFR airplanes with GPS WAAS and ADS-B in/out with WiFi for integration with tablets or other devices. They are great for the local flight or the long cross-country. The club also leases a Cessna 170 for tail wheel instruction.

With online scheduling, very open and easy scheduling policies, our members can easily obtain and enjoy the planes for the trips they want to fly. 

Maybe best of all is the opportunity to join a great group of pilots who all truly enjoy flying and sharing the joys of flying with one another. 

Want to learn more about joining the club? Click the Contact Us button and take a step closer to affordable flying today.

title: Big M Flying Club
name: Big M Flying Club
description: The Big M Flying Club's mission is to provide safe, affordable flying for its members.

title: Thompson Flying Club
name: Thompson Flying Club
description: Thompson Flying Club at KCXY is a club of 17 member pilots to further the understanding of all aspects of private pilot aviation and enhance the skills and experience of member pilots. The club owns a Piper Cherokee Archer II.  The aircraft is well maintained, outfitted with modern avionics, and stored in a hangar.

title: Hemacinto Valley Flying Club, Inc.
name: Hemacinto Valley Flying Club, Inc.
description: Our plane is N5954W a PA-28 - 150 with recent STC to 160+hp. Fully IFR (steam gauges) and we have installed ADS-B

title: Inn Flying Club
name: Inn Flying Club
description:
The Inn Flying Club, Inc. (IFC) is a non-profit organization incorporated in the State of Maryland. It was formed over 50 years ago to foster camaraderie among fellow pilots and student pilots, to promote flight safety through education and training, and to provide airworthy and dependable aircraft for use by members at cost effective rates. The IFC continues to operate in this manner today.  Aircraft may be used for business or pleasure, but not for commercial purposes.

Operation of the Club is managed according to the Club's By-Laws and Operating Rules.  The Board of Directors is elected annually and meets monthly to conduct IFC business. General membership meetings are held on the third Wednesday of each month. The Board consists of a President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, Chief Aircraft Maintenance Officer, Chief Flight Instructor and a Membership Officer. The IFC also has an individual Aircraft Maintenance Officer for each of the club aircraft.

title: Joplin Flyers Inc.
name: Joplin Flyers Inc.
description: Joplin Flyers, Inc. is a 501(c)7 social flying club with a Cessna 182 w/dual Aspen, all-glass-panel.

title: Blue Max Aero Club
name: Blue Max Aero Club
description:
Group of pilots sharing expenses 
Beech M23

title: TSS Flying Club, Inc.
name: TSS Flying Club, Inc.
description:
TSS Flying Club is a non-profit flying club located at Montgomery County Airpark (KGAI) in Gaithersburg, MD. We provide our members partial-ownership in a fleet of well-maintained airplanes with modern avionics. In addition to affordable flying, TSS also provides opportunities for shared flights, group trips, and social events.

The club currently owns and operates a fleet of four aircraft including:

1999 Cessna 172 180HP IFR Certified
2014 Vans RV-12 S-LSA
1984 Cessna C172 180hp IFR Certified
2000 Cessna C182S IFR Certified
1981 Cessna C182RG IFR Certified

The club's members span a wide spectrum of ages (from teens on up), occupations, interests, backgrounds, and flying experience - student, private, instrument, commercial, ATP, and flight instructors, from one hour of flight time to tens of thousands). There is more to the club than just a place to add flight hours to your logbook.

Join us and see why TSS has been the best flying club in Maryland for over 50 years!

title: Flying Club of Kansas City
name: Flying Club of Kansas City
description:
The Flying Club of Kansas City is a flying club comprised of approximately 100 members located at Johnson County Executive Airport in Olathe, Kansas and Lee's Summit Municipal in Lee's Summit, Missouri.  We have been operating since 1967 (formally as the Navy Flying Club) and we currently own and operate 7 well-equipped aircraft.  The Club owns two Cessna 172s, a Piper Archer, two Cessna 182s, a Piper Saratoga, and Beechcraft C33A Debonair.  All planes are in great condition and well equipped.

Whether you are looking for a reasonably priced trainer or a fast, high-performance cross-country machine, the Flying Club of Kansas City has you covered.  

The Club's current total initiation fee is $4000, and our dues are currently $125/month (effective 2/27/2023 and subject to change).  Our aircraft rates are very reasonable and our quasi-dry rate structure allows Club members to control some of their costs by purchasing their own fuel.  

The Club hosts monthly meetings, hangar parties, and fly outs where members can socialize.  We also have several safety initiatives that have contributed to the Club's excellent safety record. 

Please see our website for more information (including pictures of the airplanes).

title: Connersville Flying Club
name: Connersville Flying Club
description: The Connersville flying club has been in existence in its current form with our current plane since 2002.  We fly a VFR 1963 172E that is in excellent condition.  Our aircraft is ADS-B compliant and available to members for local and cross country flights.  As of 2021 we are flying for $100 per hour wet with a $60 per month membership fee.  There is a stock buy in for new members.

title: Twin Falls Flyerz, Inc
name: Twin Falls Flyerz, Inc
description:
The Twin Falls Flyers is a modern progressive flying club dedicated to the purposes of flying safety, the advancement of general aviation, and to providing economical, well equipped, and well maintained aircraft for the use of its members.

The club was incorporated under the laws of the State of Idaho as a non-profit corporation in 1941. Today we have 3 planes and 25 members.

title: Rock River Flying Inc.
name: Rock River Flying Inc.
description: The club has a Cessna 172 and a 7AC Champ.

title: Northwest Flyers, Inc
name: Northwest Flyers, Inc
description: Northwest Flyers operates two aircraft, a 1981 Cessna 172 and a 1981 Cessna 182.  We have 15 members as established by our by-laws.  Find more information about us at www.nwflyers.net

title: Carlisle Flying Club
name: Carlisle Flying Club
description: Membership is limited to private pilot or above. The club currently operates a C-182 P model with a p-ponk upgrade conversion. Please call Charles  Wood for membership information and application.

title: Valley Fliers, Inc
name: Valley Fliers, Inc
description:
Valley Fliers is a Washington state non-profit corporation established in 1986 for pilots that want to take advantage of the benefits of aircraft co-ownership. Partnership in Valley Fliers offers access to well equipped, mechanically sound and cost effective aircraft. Our maintenance plans exceed FAA requirements to ensure each aircraft is maintained to the highest standards. We are based at Auburn Municipal Airport (S50).

The daily operations of Valley Fliers are carefully managed by the partner elected executive board, which heavily relies on the input of each partner. As a partner, you have direct input on decisions regarding budget, spending, aircraft modifications and maintenance. A monthly meeting ensures you are afforded the opportunity to provide your input and ask any questions regarding your aircraft. We invite you to explore our site for additional information and contact us directly to inquire about available partnership shares.

title: Yankee Flying Club
name: Yankee Flying Club
description:
Yankee Flying Club was started in 1968 and is based at the Crystal, MN, airport. (KMIC) We have 65 shareholders and four aircraft in our fleet consisting of two Cessna 172s and two Cessna 182RGs.

Membership in the club is open to student and experienced pilots alike. The current insurance minimums for our aircraft are: Cessna 172s, student pilot or higher. Cessna 182RGs, 200 hours total time. In addition, a checkout with a club designated instructor is required for each aircraft type.

All aircraft are rented to the shareholders for a 'wet/Tach' rate. The schedule is kept to ensure an equal opportunity to schedule the airplanes when and how long you want them. Each share is assessed monthly dues that covers all fixed expenses that are incurred whether the aircraft fly or not. (e.g. aircraft insurance, hangar expenses, annual costs, etc).  Current rates and more information can be found on our website, http://www.yankeeflyingclub.org 

Aircraft scheduling, club roster, and billing are managed online using Flight Circle, which provides several different calendar views to choose from as well as maintenance status, aircraft reference documents, and member list with phone and e-mail info club members.

title: KTKV Flyers, Inc.
name: KTKV Flyers, Inc.
description:
KTKV Flyers, Inc. is a well-run organization with a maximum of 15 members per aircraft.

The Club presently owns a Cessna 172 Aircraft and a Redbird FMX Full Motion Simulator.

title: Greater Flint Pilots Association
name: Greater Flint Pilots Association
description:
Are you a pilot looking for other pilots who love to fly as much as you do?

Our club was incorporated on March 19, 1975. Today, as a modern, progressive and professional non-profit corporation, it is dedicated to the safety and advancement of aviation.

We believe that you will find GFPA to be one of the finer flying clubs in the state of Michigan.

Get back into flying: Join Greater Flint Pilots Association and remember why you became a pilot in the first place!

GFPA is a member owned organization where each member owns an equal share of our fleet of aircraft.

For more information, please call our Membership Director Harry Hammond at 810-259–6492 or send email to hammond.harry@gmail.com

title: Associated Pilots, Inc
name: Associated Pilots, Inc
description:
API is currently looking for new members!

When you join API, our Bedford, MA (KBED) flying club, you OWN a share of the airplane you fly and there is no comparison to the pride of taxiing into the ramp when it is YOUR plane. Our buy-in and operations costs are very reasonable. We have great availability of both airplanes through a slick web-based calendar where our small group (14-17) books each plane. You can drive your car right into the hangar. No unloading in the rain and snow!

Since 1948, API has been serving Boston area pilots. The club is run entirely by its members.

Our planes are very well equipped and maintained, with WAAS Garmin GNS systems, G5 glass panels, and GFC500 dual-axis autopilots in each. Over the last few years members of API flew the C-182 and the C-206 from our BED hangars to destinations like Oshkosh, WI, Cleveland, OH, Newfoundland, and even the Cayman Islands! You worked hard for your rating, and now it is time to start really flying. For complete membership details click on our About page, then Contact Us today to start the process of joining one of the longest-running flying partnerships in the United States.

title: N7YM LLC
name: N7YM LLC
description: 4-person club with one membership available for purchase. See web site for details.

title: Eight Ball Flying Club
name: Eight Ball Flying Club
description:
The Eight Ball Flying Club is a California non-profit corporation which has been in continuous operation at the Van Nuys Airport since 1954.

Our mission is to promote the advancement of general aviation, facilitate and encourage members’ common interests in flight.

Our fleet of 5 aircraft includes a 2002 Diamond DA40, a 2002 Cessna 172SP, TWO 2000 Cessna 182s, and a 1981 Piper Saratoga.

We have top-notch maintenance, easy online scheduling and NO OVERNIGHT MINIMUMS.

title: Metro Flyers Flying Club
name: Metro Flyers Flying Club
description: Metro Flyers, Ltd. is a private flying club based at Denton Municipal Airport. We provide club members use of aircraft at reasonable rates without the limitations of normal renting, such as minimum overnight charges. We currently have two aircraft - a 1975 Cessna 182P and a 1966 Beechcraft Bonanza V35.

title: Sugarbush Soaring Association
name: Sugarbush Soaring Association
description:
New members are always welcome!!

Sugarbush Soaring is not just a commercial operation - it is also a vibrant club with an active social scene.  We have 50-60 members from all over the country who love flying in the Green Mountains.  On a good soaring day, the airfield is a hubbub of activity - with families eating in the dining room, kids playing on the grass, various folks relaxing in the gazebo, and of course plenty of gliders circling in the sky above the airfield.  After the day's flying, there is nearly always something going on.  For a description of events happening this summer, click on the Event Calendar link above.

Soaring is a special sport, and if you're interested in joining us in the sky we would love to show you around our beautiful airport.  One way to learn about our club and our sport is to simply drop by.  Anyone on the field would be happy to show you around, answer your questions, introduce you to the instructors and other club members, and let you sit in a glider.

Should you decide to fly with us, you'll find that is considerably cheaper once you join the club.  For details about the rates, click here.

Please explore our website further, and then come and see us!!  Don't hesitate to give us a call at (802) 496-2290 or email us at soar@sugarbushsoaring.com

title: Denver Flyers
name: Denver Flyers
description: Denver Flyers was established in 1967 and offers its members affordable and safe flying opportunities for recreational use and training. Based at Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport (KBJC), we currently own 3 aircraft, a 1965 300HP Cessna 182H, a 1976 Cessna 182 and a 1978 Mooney M20J. We keep membership levels as low as we can so that scheduling remains flexible (around 10-13 members / aircraft). The aircraft serve different purpose including day flying, cross-country and longer trips or IFR. The club also is actively socializing, training and educating its members. Overall, Denver Flyers is a flying club that is dedicated to promoting safe and affordable flying, providing a broad mission envelope to its members, and building a community of aviation enthusiasts. With its well-maintained airplanes, experienced pilots, and welcoming community, it offers a great opportunity for anyone who shares a passion for aviation to explore the skies and connect with others who share that same passion.

title: Lexington Flying Club
name: Lexington Flying Club
description:
Chartered as a nonprofit Kentucky corporation in 1953, the Lexington Flying Club, Inc. owns three Cessna 172's, a Piper Archer II and a Diamond Star, DA-40.

The club is operated to provide its members with low cost flying, safety training and continuing pilot education. All aircraft are based at Lexington's Blue Grass Airport and are maintained by FAA certified maintenance personnel.

The Club has approximately 150 members (approximately 75 active flyers.) Flying experience is not required for membership; in fact, about one fifth of our members are student pilots, taking lessons, and working towards that private pilot certificate.

Although the Club is not a flight school, per se, some 20+ Club approved instructors are available and have helped many of the Club's pilots obtain private, instrument and commercial licenses/ratings. 

There are two available membership levels, Restricted and Full. Restricted members may fly the Cessnas 172's after a one time $300.00 initiation fee. Restricted members pay monthly dues of $45.00. Full members may fly all airplanes after a one time $600.00 initiation fee. Full members pay monthly dues of $64.00.

There is also a membership that bridges the two main membership levels, providing a way to incrementally pay the difference in initiation fees as you continue to fly the Cessna 172's. Once the FULL membership initiation fee is paid off, you can then start flying the Archer and the Diamond Star.

Pilots in the lower (Restricted) level of membership fly the Cessna 172's at $8/hr more than the rate shown below. Other restrictions on the lower membership level include a restriction on how far out in time you may schedule (7 days) and a restriction to single day reservations. See the Bylaws for more information about the club membership levels.

title: Tidewater Flying Club, Inc.
name: Tidewater Flying Club, Inc.
description: We are an Incorporated Non profit Social organization since 1967, located at the Newport News/Williamsburg airport with 40+ members and three aircraft; by virtue of joint ownership, the cost of operating aircraft are significantly reduced from sole ownership at the expense of having to share the aircraft. We have Club meetings on the second Wednesday each month [except December which is when we have our annual meeting] in the terminal building at PHF, in the board room near the USO club. Prospective members need to come to two consecutive meetings to join, one to turn in your application, and the following month to be interviewed and voted on. Aside from that, there are few requirements for membership. People can find a copy of our Bylaws and Rules and Regulations on the club website (http://tidewaterflyingclub.net). Members must be checked out in each aircraft type (Cessna 182, Cessna 172 and a Diamond DA40). All of our aircraft are IFR-equipped. Contact us for a visit to look at our expertly maintained club aircraft in person.

title: Blue Sky Flyers Flying Club
name: Blue Sky Flyers Flying Club
description: Based at Greely-Weld County Airport (KGXY), Blue Sky Flyers is a member-owned private flying club that has been providing its members aircraft for their enjoyment and pursuit of flight for over 40 years.

title: Quad City Area Flying Eagles, Inc.
name: Quad City Area Flying Eagles, Inc.

title: Athens Aero Club
name: Athens Aero Club
description: The Athens Aero Club, Inc. was founded in May, 1968, to provide members with enjoyable, safe, economical flying, for pleasure and business. Currently there are about ten members in the club, who all get together to share the enjoyment of flight.

title: Sierra Soaring Club
name: Sierra Soaring Club
description:
Welcome to the Sierra Soaring Club, located in sunny Inyokern, California -- right at the foot of the southern Sierra Nevada mountains.

The club has several classes of membership to serve the needs of the members.  Because we are a chapter of the Soaring Society of America, SSA membership is required to receive any club services.

1.Basic -- fly the Blanik ($250 initiation, $50/month dues, no charge for sailplane)

2.Advanced -- fly the Blanik and 1-35 ($500 initiation, $50/month dues, no charge for sailplanes)

3.Power -- fly the Cessna 182 (towing tasks primary) ($500 initiation, $75/month dues, $130/hour wet.

4.Premier -- fly the Blanik, 1-35 and 182 ($750 initiation, $100/month dues, $130/hour wet for the 1-82, no charge for sailplanes)

5.Tow Pilot -- must meet FAA requirements, complete a towing course, 500 hours power minimum -- no charges, no salary. Tow pilots earn one hour of Blanik time for each hour of towing.

6.Private Owner -- No charge but tow fees slightly higher

7.Inactive -- no dues, no vote; reactivate by resuming paying dues

8.Distant (greater than 50 miles away) -- initiation fee, monthly dues only when flying.
Note: Instruction fee is arranged between the student and instructor, but typically $30 for club members; $60 for non-members; tow charges additional to all other fees.

title: Mach 1 Flying Club
name: Mach 1 Flying Club
description:
We are a small, non-profit, 50 year old limited membership Cardinal (C-177) flying club dedicated to bringing together pilots and providing a safe flying experience.  Our plane is available 24 hours a day and can be easily scheduled via our online scheduling system.  Members have the flexibility of booking weekends, and even a week without a minimum hourly charge.  

Our airplane panel has been upgraded to a Garmin digital display for the primary instruments, a Garmin touch screen GPS and Garmin's GFC500 2 axis autopilot with an auto trim servo. The autopilot is capable of flying holds and LPV approaches.  

For more information visit our web page at MachFlyingClub.com.  Please note that the minimum requirement to join our Club is a valid  private pilot's license, single engine land.


(This information is subject to change and may contain errors and/or omissions)

title: Silvercreek Glider Club
name: Silvercreek Glider Club
description: The Silvercreek Glider Club is an educational soaring club located just north-east of St. Louis. The club operates at Silvercreek Gliderport year round on weekends and holidays (other days by appointment).

title: Gateway Flying Club
name: Gateway Flying Club
description:
Gateway Flying Club strives to be a club for the pilot who wants to use airplanes to travel and explore at affordable rates. We are a social organization that treats our members like owners and family; because they are! Gateway owns four airplanes and a hangar/clubhouse. Our aircraft mix provides a continuum of performance and payload that allows the pilot to choose the best aircraft for their mission. 

Gateway is an equity membership club. Shares are member property and typically sold privately on Craigslist, Barnstormers, or Facebook Marketplace. Dues are $155/month (including tax). Aircraft usage is charged on a Dry-Tach basis (pilot buys the fuel). An equity member's immediate family members are eligible for Associate Membership status, which include flight privileges, for $45/month. 

The clubs fleet consists of three Cessnas: 1976 C172M Skyhawk, 1976 C177B Cardinal,  1976 C182P Skylane and a 1978 Piper PA-32RT-300 Lance. The planes fly approximately 300 hours each per year. All aircraft are ADSB Compliant and IFR equipped (VOR/ILS) with Garmin WAAS GPS Navigators.  All aircraft have 4/6-place intercoms, JPI engine monitors; the Cessna's have Angle of Attack instruments and 4-point harnesses for the pilot and co-pilot. The 177, 182 and P32T have 2-axis autopilots.

Our planes are suitable learning platforms for certificates and ratings from Private Pilot to CFII. Student pilots are welcome; but must be an equity or family member to receive instruction in the club's planes. 

Club meetings are open to prospective members and are held on the 2nd Thursday of each month starting at 7pm at the club hangar. We recommend that first-time visitors call ahead to confirm meeting time and location.

title: Stick & Rudder Flying Club
name: Stick & Rudder Flying Club
description:
Stick & Rudder Flying Club is one of the oldest flying clubs in the United States. Located at Waukegan Airport (KUGN), the club has been operating continuously since 1948. We offer outstanding flight training and aircraft rentals to club members at affordable rates.

As a not-for-profit club, we strive to keep our dues, flying rates and instructor fees reasonable. Hourly rates are “wet” meaning gas is included as we maintain our own 10,000 gallon fuel tank and purchase fuel in bulk. Another additional benefit of flying at Stick & Rudder – we carry a $1,000,000 smooth insurance policy which will cover you and any passengers while flying our aircraft. No need to purchase renter’s insurance.

We own our fleet of Cessnas – a 172P model and two 172S models. All the 172s are IFR equipped and the S models have IFR GPS capabilities. Our clubhouse and hangar facility offer a comfortable place for ground instruction and an ideal setting to spend time talking and “hangar flying” with other member pilots. Our experienced instructors are always available to offer advice and assistance for student and seasoned pilots alike. The clubhouse is wi-fi equipped and we host many social events throughout the year including holiday parties, poker runs, an annual summer picnic and spot landing contest as well as other get- togethers and impromptu barbecues.

title: Bald Eagle Flying Club
name: Bald Eagle Flying Club
description:
The Bald Eagle Flying Club is located at the Portland International Jetport (KPWM) in Portland, Maine. We are currently 40 members and own one airplane; a 1979 Cessna 172N (N4818D). This aircraft is equipped with an upgraded Lycoming O-360 engine rated @180 HP and is IFR equipped with a Garmin GTN650 and Dynon Skyview HDX. In addition to owning a 1979 Cessna 172N (N4818D), the club also owns a 1968 Piper PA-28-140.  This plane is equipped with a Lycoming 0-320 Series (Reciprocating) engine rated at 180 HP. More info about our aircraft can be found at www.baldeagleflyingclub.org.

We do have a few members who are active CFIs and offer primary flight instruction and IFR instruction to the rest of our club in their spare time. We charge monthly dues and members pay for each hour of tach time, which is a wet rate.

title: International Flying Club
name: International Flying Club
description:
We are a non-equity non-profit flying club with a fleet of four well-maintained aircraft based at DuPage Airport in West Chicago, Illinois. We are well recognized as offering the most affordable flying opportunities in the Chicagoland area. Our goal is to provide safe and enjoyable flying at the best possible value while striving to create a supportive environment for enhancing pilot skills and building a spirit of fellowship amongst aviation enthusiasts.

The club was established in 1975 and is fully operated by the volunteer efforts of members and officers. We are able to realize economical flying rates, low monthly dues, minimal joining fees, and no surprise surcharges. The aircraft fleet is equipped for IFR with navigational upgrades like ADS-B in/out, EFIS, DME, GPS, and auto-pilot. Special emphasis is placed on aircraft safety and preventive maintenance.

Keeping the flying club vibrant and exciting is a key to our success; Members greatly value all the club social aspects. Besides monthly meetings, safety seminars, guest speakers, newsletters, and recreational gatherings, our enthusiastic club pilots are focused on organizing group fly-outs, flight sharing, medical transport, animal rescue, community outreach programs, and joint maintenance activities. Our leadership team is committed to promoting pilot currency and aviation safety, enhancing pilot prowess and proficiency, and supporting club members in achieving their pilot goals.

If you are looking for a rewarding, fun, friendly, and affordable flying club experience with a community of great pilots, we would love to share our passion and joy of flying with you. All are welcome at our club meetings. We'd be glad to meet with you, show off club aircraft, or provide an intro flight. See why so many pilots regardless of their experience level find us to be the most cost-effective flying option in the Chicagoland area. Please contact us at 847-483-4999, send us email, or visit website at https://www.flyifc.org

title: Schaumburg Flying Club
name: Schaumburg Flying Club
description: The Schaumburg Flying Club is a not-for-profit group of aviation enthusiasts who proudly own and operate a Cessna 172S and 182S.  In January of 2019 we made significant Avionics upgrades.  We have added all new Garmin radios and avionics including a GTN 650 WAAS GPS, dual G5s, GTX 345 Transponder with ADS-B in/out, GNC 255 NAV/COM, GMA 345 Audio Panel.  Both planes have Garmin GFC 500 Auto Pilots, which make them great cross country planes in addition to local flying.  We're based at the centrally located Schaumburg Regional Airport (06C), located just outside of Chicago, IL.   We are committed to maintaining a safe fleet of aircraft at reasonable prices.  We comply with all ADs and Service Bulletins, and our members perform routine maintenance regularly. All of our members are fully insured under our club's policy - you won't need to pay for "renter's" insurance.  Club members can check aircraft availability and make reservations over the Internet.  We currently cap the membership at 22, and we have a waiting list.  If you care to be put on the waiting list, go to our website and fill in the request for more info.  Ken or Gene will get back to you shortly after your request.

title: Texins Flying Club
name: Texins Flying Club
description: TFC is one of the oldest flying clubs in the country. Founded in the early 1960's, it has been in continuous operation since then. We are now located at the McKinney National Airport in McKinney, Texas.

title: RFC Dallas, Inc.
name: RFC Dallas, Inc.
description: RFC Dallas, Incorporated is a volunteer run, not-for-profit flying club that has been based at Addison Airport (KADS) since the late 1970s.  Our current fleet consists of a Piper PA28-180, a Cessna 182, a Piper Arrow, two F-33A Beechcraft Bonanzas and a Cirrus SR22.  We have an automated computer reservations system that is accessible either through the Web or over the phone.  RFC Dallas is one of the successor clubs to an employee flying club formed by Bob Hoover when North American Aviation and Rockwell merged in the mid-1960s.

title: Lehigh Valley Flying Club
name: Lehigh Valley Flying Club
description:
There is a practical and affordable solution that allows you to fly high quality, well maintained aircraft at a great value. Come join us at the Lehigh Valley Flying Club and enjoy great aircraft with fantastic benefits!

The Lehigh Valley Flying Club was organized in 1956 and over the years has become the premier flying club in the greater Lehigh Valley area.

Based at the Allentown-Bethlehem-Easton Airport (KABE) the club has its own clubhouse and hangar. Here are some of the benefits:
# Private hangar including a furnished Pilots' lounge with a computer and Wi-Fi
# Three high-quality, well-maintained aircraft: 

- 1976 PA28/181 Archer 
- 1978 Archer
- 2001 PA28/181 Archer III 
# Modern online scheduling system
# FAA Certified Flight Instructors for training
# "Wet" usage rates based on Tach time. 
# Low monthly membership fee
# All aircraft are completely insured and maintained

We are a non-profit group dedicated to your flying enjoyment. If you have an interest in general aviation, you owe it to yourself to explore the benefits of the Lehigh Valley Flying Club.

We are welcoming new members.  Please contact us (information@lvfc.org) to schedule a tour of our facilities.

title: BK Inc Twin Rentals
name: BK Inc Twin Rentals
description: Cessna 310q and Eclipse 500

title: Northwest Flyers
name: Northwest Flyers
description:
Our club's sole purpose is to provide safe aircraft at affordable rates. We are always interested in adding new aircraft types to our fleet.

Please contact us through our website or email at northwestflyerskosu@gmail.com

title: Patuxent River Navy Flying Club
name: Patuxent River Navy Flying Club
description: PRNFC is a recreational and instructional flying organization based at Naval Air Station Patuxent River in Maryland, USA. Membership is open to all active duty, reserve, and retired military, Civil Air Patrol, civil servants, DoD contractors, and their immediate families. The objective of PRNFC is to provide an off-duty, voluntary educational opportunity for base personnel to develop skills in aeronautics including piloting, navigation, mechanics, and other related aero sciences. We provide an opportunity for naval aviators to maintain pilot proficiency skills while assigned to non-flying billets, encourage awareness and appreciation of aviation requirements and techniques, provide a facility designed to assist in meeting the recreational needs for low-cost, safe, light aircraft operations, and provide a social program in the interest of promoting club activities and morale.

title: Marfa Gliders
name: Marfa Gliders
description:
Glider flight training, intro rides and "free" FAA Checkrides for all Glider category ratings including CFI-Glider. 
Owner / Master CFI / Designated Pilot Examiner BURT COMPTON has over 50 years of aviation experience to share.  "Rusty Pilot" course available.  Soaring (year-round) began here in 1960. Located on the Marfa Plateau at 5,000' msl near the Davis Mountains and Big Bend National Park.  No oil here, just a huge aquifer of water underground.
"Marfa Gliders Soaring Center" is a national aviation "Landmark" with a plaque next to the big hangar holding 
6 gliders (sailplanes) and a wall full of gliding memorabilia.      Advance appointments are required.  
Website: www.flygliders.com

title: Condair Flyers, Inc
name: Condair Flyers, Inc
description:
Flying in the Capital District of New York: Condair Flyers Wants you! 

One of the longest continuously operated not-for-profit flying club in the New York State Capital Region had some pretty humble beginnings.  Condair Flyers started in 1964 with a single Piper Cub and two members at the Schenectady county airport.  Over the years, the Club has grown to include nearly 75 pilots and five aircraft, and operates out of Albany International Airport, with aircraft in a hangar at the Million Air FBO.  

With heated hangar space and linemen to attend to the aircraft, and always hot coffee, meeting rooms, and refreshments, it's every GA pilot's dream location.  The Club's aircraft (a Piper Warrior II, Piper Archer IIl, Cessna 172SP, 172P, and 182RGII) are all IFR certified aircraft.  The Club is known for the quality aircraft, excellent maintenance, camaraderie between Club members and the monthly Club meetings that always include presentations of interest for pilots.  Supporting the Club are approved Certified Flight Instructors for the aspiring pilot through to the veteran pilot.  Club members have worked on their Private Pilot License right up through their CFI with knowledgeable instructors - several of whom are also Club members.  

The Club is an "equity based club" with Club members paying an initial equity share.  Pilots pay a wet hourly use rate based on the tachometer time for usage, monthly dues and members participate to keep the Club's aircraft in top shape.  Members schedule aircraft through an internet service operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week.  Aircraft can be scheduled for a maximum period of four days without Executive Board approval or for more than four days with Executive Board approval. 

If you are an aspiring pilot or seasoned pilot and are looking for a solid economical flying club to join, consider Condair Flyers.

title: Oxford Flying Club, Inc.
name: Oxford Flying Club, Inc.
description:
The Club owns maintains a fleet of six aircraft of five different models to address a wide a range of pilot experience and skill levels - from low-time PPL through high-time ATP. Our variety offer members opportunity to fly diverse configurations, grow their proficiency, and achieve new and advanced ratings.

N228TR - Cirrus SR-20
N735GC - Cessna 182Q Skylane
N8261H - Piper PA-28-181 Cherokee Archer II 
N4334X - Piper PA-28-181 Cherokee Archer II
N98819 - Cessna 172P Skyhawk
N11937 - Cessna 177B Cardinal

All six aircraft are very well maintained and include uniform avionics; GTN-650, GI-275's, GFC-500 autopilots, and in the case of the Cirrus, Avidyne Entegra with GNS 430's and S-TEC 55x Autopilot. Visit our website at www.oxfordflyingclub.com

title: Pittsburgh Flying Club

title: Monterey Navy Flying Club

description: This Military Flying Club is open to all U.S. Active Duty, National Guard, Retired, Active Reserve and their family members, Federal Government employees, DoD contractors and members of armed forces of foreign countries and their family members when on orders in the U.S. Civilians are also eligible for membership through affiliation with the Civil Air Patrol.

title: Pacific Coast Flyers
name: Pacific Coast Flyers
description:
Pacific Coast Flyers is a flying club in every sense. We are a cooperative of pilots that share a love of flying, united in supporting an organization that is transparent and responsive to its members.

At Pacific Coast Flyers, we offer well equipped and well maintained aircraft at the most affordable prices possible. Maintenance is taken seriously and, as a result, the aircraft are highly available and of high quality.

Once a member of PCF you can train in club aircraft. We have excellent instructors in the club with ratings available to instruct you to any level of certificate you desire. Just book an aircraft, call the instructor of your choice to join you and off you go. None of the flight school requirements and restrictions.... Just get yourself an airplane, find an instructor and GO!!! If your favorite instructor isn't in the club then have them join and go on a quick instructor checkout... no problem!

The AAC has always been a not-for-profit club dedicated to making flying accessible and affordable to everyone. We are based at Oakland International Airport (KOAK) in the San Francisco Bay Area of Northern California, and we welcome new members from anywhere in the Bay Area — and from all walks of life!

title: Toledo Flying Club
name: Toledo Flying Club
description:
On July 30, 1940, the Toledo Flying Club was organized into an educational, scientific, social and recreational corporation, under the laws of the State of Washington. Officers and Board members were elected, the Association Agreement was ratified and the Code of By-Laws was drawn up. The general purpose of this corporation shall be the promotion of the art and science of aerial navigation and the affording of the Club facilities to the members thereof for amateur powered flight.

The 1932 model Taylorcraft became the Club’s first aircraft. Through the years, the Club became the owners of various aircraft. At the present time the Club owns a Piper Warrior 161.

At one time, before the Columbus Day Storm of 1962, the Club progressed to about 20 members. However, after the storm, most of the members dropped their membership, except for three hearty individuals. Real dedication was displayed as they continued paying monthly dues for two years with no airplanes to fly.

Although many of the older members have retired from flying or have left the area, the remaining members, both old and new, operate the Club on the basic principles adopted through the years.

title: Williamson Flying Club
name: Williamson Flying Club
description:
Today's flying club is an incorporated organization supporting flying activities for pilots and enthusiasts from the Lake Ontario region of Western/Central New York.

We have one full time and several part time Flight Instructors that provide training for Private Pilot ratings as well as instruction for more advanced Commercial, CFI, and IFR ratings.

The clubs stated purpose is to promote and encourage interest in aviation and teach members to improve their flying skills.

For an opportunity to join the Williamson Flying Club ask any member for additional information.

title: Valley Soaring Club, Inc
name: Valley Soaring Club, Inc
description:
Valley Soaring Club is a non-profit club of soaring enthusiasts who share an unbridled passion for blue skies and the thrill of riding the wind like a bird in flight.

We provides affordable facilities, equipment and professional instruction. Our goal is promote and safely practice the exciting sport of soaring.

Open to beginners, novices and experts alike, our mission is to offer recreation, competition, and good fellowship in a social yet professional environment. 

Valley Soaring Club boasts one of the largest junior memberships in the country. Junior members are students aged 22 years and younger. Valley Soaring Club is dedicated to providing a safe, fun and educational environment for young people to learn and enjoy the sport of soaring.

We offer:
Demo rides, 4 flight packages, membership
Instruction and rentals for members only.

title: Penn Yan Flying Club, Inc.
name: Penn Yan Flying Club, Inc.
description:
The Penn Yan Flying Club resides in the beautiful Finger Lakes region of New York State. We are located at the Penn Yan Airport (KPEO) on the northeastern tip of Keuka Lake. We were founded in 1939 by some local business people with a love of flying. The club was incorporated in the State of New York in 1940, and has been in continuous operation since that time.

Since this inception its mission statement has been “To promote aviation through the conduct of a business which breaks even and enables members to fly safely and inexpensively”.
